الْجُزْءُ الْخَامِسُ
كِتَابُ الْأَسْمَاءِ وَالْصِفَاتِ
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَحْدَهُ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى مَنْ لَا نَبِيَّ بَعْدَهُ
سُئِلَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ:
 الْعَالِمُ الرَّبَّانِيُّ تَقِيُّ الدِّينِ أَحْمَد بْنُ عَبْدِ الْحَلِيمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ السَّلَامِ بْنِ تَيْمِيَّة - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى -:
مَا قَوْلُ السَّادَةِ الْعُلَمَاءِ أَئِمَّةِ الدِّينِ فِي 
" آيَاتِ الصِّفَاتِ "
 كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: 
{الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى}
 وَقَوْلِهِ: 
{ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ}
 وَقَوْلِهِ: 
{ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى إلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ}
 إلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ آيَاتِ الصِّفَاتِ وَ 
" أَحَادِيثِ الصِّفَاتِ "
 كَقَوْلِهِ: صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ 
{إنَّ قُلُوبَ بَنِي آدَمَ بَيْنَ أُصْبُعَيْنِ مِنْ أَصَابِعِ الرَّحْمَنِ}
 وَقَوْلِهِ: 
{يَضَعُ الْجَبَّارُ قَدَمَهُ فِي النَّارِ}
 إلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ وَمَا قَالَتْ الْعُلَمَاءُ فِيهِ وَابْسُطُوا الْقَوْلَ فِي ذَلِكَ مَأْجُورِينَ إنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.
فَأَجَابَ - رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ -:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، قَوْلُنَا فِيهَا مَا قَالَهُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
translated_text:
Volume Five
The Book of the Divine Names and Attributes

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful. Praise belongs to Allah alone, and may blessings and peace be upon him after whom there is no prophet.

Shaykh al-Islām, the godly scholar Taqī al-Dīn Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Halīm ibn ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Taymiyya—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked:

What do the esteemed scholars, the imams of the religion, say concerning the “verses concerning the divine attributes,” such as His saying, Most High:

“The Most Merciful has risen over the Throne,”

and His saying:

“Then He rose over the Throne,”

and His saying:

“Then He turned toward the heaven while it was smoke,”

and other verses concerning the divine attributes; and concerning the “hadiths concerning the divine attributes,” such as the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Indeed, the hearts of the children of Adam are between two fingers of the Most Merciful,”

and his saying:

“The Compeller places His foot in the Fire,”

and other such hadiths? What have the scholars said about these? Please discuss this matter at length; may you be rewarded, if Allah Most High wills.

He replied—may Allah be pleased with him:

Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds. What we say concerning them is what Allah and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said

original_text:
وَالسَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ:
 مِنْ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارِ وَاَلَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُمْ بِإِحْسَانِ؛ وَمَا قَالَهُ أَئِمَّةُ الْهُدَى بَعْدَ هَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِينَ أَجْمَعَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَلَى هِدَايَتِهِمْ وَدِرَايَتِهِمْ وَهَذَا هُوَ الْوَاجِبُ عَلَى جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ وَغَيْرِهِ؛ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى بَعَثَ مُحَمَّدًا صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ؛
 لِيُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنْ الظُّلُمَاتِ إلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ إلَى صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ وَشَهِدَ لَهُ بِأَنَّهُ بَعَثَهُ دَاعِيًا إلَيْهِ بِإِذْنِهِ وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَقُولَ:
 
{قُلْ هَذِهِ سَبِيلِي أَدْعُو إلَى اللَّهِ عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي}
 . فَمِنْ الْمُحَالِ فِي الْعَقْلِ وَالدِّينِ أَنْ يَكُونَ السِّرَاجُ الْمُنِيرُ الَّذِي أَخْرَجَ اللَّهُ بِهِ النَّاسَ مِنْ الظُّلُمَاتِ إلَى النُّورِ وَأَنْزَلَ مَعَهُ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ؛ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ فِيمَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ وَأَمَرَ النَّاسَ أَنْ يَرُدُّوا مَا تَنَازَعُوا فِيهِ مِنْ أَمْرِ دِينِهِمْ إلَى مَا بُعِثَ بِهِ مِنْ الْكِتَابِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ وَهُوَ يَدْعُو إلَى اللَّهِ وَإِلَى سَبِيلِهِ بِإِذْنِهِ عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ وَقَدْ أَخْبَرَ اللَّهُ بِأَنَّهُ أَكْمَلَ لَهُ وَلِأُمَّتِهِ دِينَهُمْ وَأَتَمَّ عَلَيْهِمْ نِعْمَتَهُ -
 مُحَالٌ مَعَ هَذَا وَغَيْرِهِ:
 أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدْ تَرَكَ بَابَ الْإِيمَانِ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْعِلْمِ بِهِ مُلْتَبِسًا مُشْتَبِهًا وَلَمْ يُمَيِّزْ بَيْنَ مَا يَجِبُ لِلَّهِ مِنْ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْحُسْنَى وَالصِّفَاتِ الْعُلْيَا وَمَا يَجُوزُ عَلَيْهِ وَمَا يَمْتَنِعُ عَلَيْهِ. فَإِنَّ مَعْرِفَةَ هَذَا أَصْلُ الدِّينِ وَأَسَاسُ الْهِدَايَةِ وَأَفْضَلُ وَأَوْجَبُ مَا اكْتَسَبَتْهُ الْقُلُوبُ وَحَصَّلَتْهُ النُّفُوسُ وَأَدْرَكَتْهُ الْعُقُولُ فَكَيْفَ يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ الْكِتَابُ وَذَلِكَ الرَّسُولُ وَأَفْضَلُ خَلْقِ اللَّهِ بَعْدَ النَّبِيِّينَ لَمْ يُحْكِمُوا هَذَا الْبَابَ اعْتِقَادًا وَقَوْلًا
translated_text:
and what the earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in righteousness, said; and what the imams of guidance who came after them said—those whose guidance and understanding the Muslims unanimously acknowledged. This is obligatory for everyone, in this matter and in all others. For Allah, glorified and exalted is He, sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with guidance and the religion of truth, to bring people out of darkness into light, by their Lord’s permission, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. He testified that He had sent him as one who calls to Him by His permission and as an illuminating lamp, and commanded him to say:

“Say: This is my way; I call to Allah with clear insight—I and those who follow me.”

It is therefore inconceivable, both rationally and religiously, that the illuminating lamp—through whom Allah brought people out of darkness into light, with whom He sent down the Book in truth to judge between people concerning their differences, and to whose message of the Book and wisdom He commanded people to refer their religious disputes; who calls to Allah and His path, by His permission, with clear insight; and for whom and whose community Allah declared that He had perfected their religion and completed His favour upon them—could, in view of all this and more, have left the matter of faith in Allah and knowledge of Him obscure and ambiguous, without distinguishing between the most beautiful names and the loftiest attributes that necessarily belong to Allah, what is possible with respect to Him, and what is impossible with respect to Him.

Knowledge of this is the root of religion, the foundation of guidance, and the noblest and most obligatory knowledge that hearts can acquire, souls attain, and minds comprehend. How, then, could that Book, that Messenger, and the best of Allah’s creation after the prophets have failed to establish this matter firmly in belief and speech?

original_text:
وَمِنْ الْمُحَالِ أَيْضًا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَدْ عَلَّمَ أُمَّتَهُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَتَّى الْخِرَاءَةَ وَقَالَ:
 
{تَرَكْتُكُمْ عَلَى الْمَحَجَّةِ الْبَيْضَاءِ لَيْلُهَا كَنَهَارِهَا لَا يَزِيغُ عَنْهَا بَعْدِي إلَّا هَالِكٌ}
 وَقَالَ فِيمَا صَحَّ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا: 
{مَا بَعَثَ اللَّهُ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ إلَّا كَانَ حَقًّا عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَدُلَّ أُمَّتَهُ عَلَى خَيْرِ مَا يَعْلَمُهُ لَهُمْ وَيَنْهَاهُمْ عَنْ شَرِّ مَا يَعْلَمُهُ لَهُمْ}
 .
 وَقَالَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ:
 لَقَدْ تُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَمَا طَائِرٌ يُقَلِّبُ جَنَاحَيْهِ فِي السَّمَاءِ إلَّا ذَكَرَ لَنَا مِنْهُ عِلْمًا. وَقَالَ 
{عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ: قَامَ فِينَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مَقَامًا فَذَكَرَ بَدْءَ الْخَلْقِ؛ حَتَّى دَخَلَ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ مَنَازِلَهُمْ وَأَهْلُ النَّارِ مَنَازِلَهُمْ حَفِظَ ذَلِكَ مَنْ حَفِظَهُ وَنَسِيَهُ مَنْ نَسِيَهُ}
 رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ. وَمُحَالٌ مَعَ تَعْلِيمِهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ لَهُمْ فِيهِ مَنْفَعَةٌ فِي الدِّينِ - وَإِنْ دَقَّتْ - أَنْ يَتْرُكَ تَعْلِيمَهُمْ مَا يَقُولُونَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَيَعْتَقِدُونَهُ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ فِي رَبِّهِمْ وَمَعْبُودِهِمْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ الَّذِي مَعْرِفَتُهُ غَايَةُ الْمَعَارِفِ وَعِبَادَتُهُ أَشْرَفُ الْمَقَاصِدِ وَالْوُصُولُ إلَيْهِ غَايَةُ الْمَطَالِبِ.
 بَلْ هَذَا خُلَاصَةُ الدَّعْوَةِ النَّبَوِيَّةِ وَزُبْدَةُ الرِّسَالَةِ الْإِلَهِيَّةِ فَكَيْفَ يَتَوَهَّمُ مَنْ فِي قَلْبِهِ أَدْنَى مُسْكَةٍ مِنْ إيمَانٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ أَنْ لَا يَكُونَ بَيَانُ هَذَا الْبَابِ قَدْ وَقَعَ مِنْ الرَّسُولِ عَلَى غَايَةِ التَّمَامِ ثُمَّ إذَا كَانَ قَدْ وَقَعَ ذَلِكَ مِنْهُ:
 فَمِنْ الْمُحَالِ أَنْ يَكُونَ خَيْرُ أُمَّتِهِ وَأَفْضَلُ قُرُونِهَا قَصَّرُوا فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ زَائِدِينَ فِيهِ أَوْ نَاقِصِينِ عَنْهُ. ثُمَّ مِنْ الْمُحَالِ أَيْضًا أَنْ تَكُونَ الْقُرُونُ الْفَاضِلَةُ - الْقَرْنُ الَّذِي بُعِثَ فِيهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ - كَانُوا غَيْرَ
translated_text:
It is also inconceivable that this should be so, when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, taught his community everything—even how to relieve themselves—and said:

“I have left you on a clear, radiant path, whose night is like its day. None will stray from it after me except one doomed to perish.”

He also said, as authentically reported from him:

“Allah never sent a prophet without obliging him to direct his community to the best of what he knew to be good for them and to forbid them from the worst of what he knew to be evil for them.”

Abū Dharr said:

“When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed away, there was not a bird beating its wings in the sky about which he had not imparted some knowledge to us.”

And ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb said:

“The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood among us and described the beginning of creation, continuing until the people of Paradise had entered their dwellings and the people of Hell had entered theirs. Some remembered what he said, while others forgot it.”

Reported by al-Bukhārī.

Having taught them everything that benefits them in religion, however slight that benefit may be, it is inconceivable that he should have neglected to teach them what to say with their tongues and believe in their hearts concerning their Lord and the One they worship—the Lord of all worlds. Knowledge of Him is the ultimate knowledge, worship of Him the noblest aim, and reaching Him the ultimate object of pursuit.

Indeed, this is the essence of the prophetic call and the very heart of the divine message. How, then, could anyone whose heart contains even the slightest measure of faith and wisdom imagine that the Messenger had not explained this matter with the utmost completeness? And if he did explain it, then it is inconceivable that the best of his community and its finest generations should have fallen short in this matter, either by adding to it or by leaving anything out.

Furthermore, it is also inconceivable that the virtuous generations—the generation among whom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent, then those who followed them, then those who followed them—were not

عَالِمِينَ وَغَيْرَ قَائِلِينَ فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ بِالْحَقِّ الْمُبِينِ لِأَنَّ ضِدَّ ذَلِكَ إمَّا عَدَمُ الْعِلْمِ وَالْقَوْلِ وَإِمَّا اعْتِقَادُ نَقِيضِ الْحَقِّ وَقَوْلِ خِلَافِ الصِّدْقِ. وَكِلَاهُمَا مُمْتَنِعٌ.
أَمَّا الْأَوَّلُ:
 فَلِأَنَّ مَنْ فِي قَلْبِهِ أَدْنَى حَيَاةٍ وَطَلَبٍ لِلْعِلْمِ أَوْ نَهْمَةٍ فِي الْعِبَادَةِ يَكُونُ الْبَحْثُ عَنْ هَذَا الْبَابِ وَالسُّؤَالُ عَنْهُ وَمَعْرِفَةُ الْحَقِّ فِيهِ أَكْبَرَ مَقَاصِدِهِ وَأَعْظَمَ مَطَالِبِهِ؛ أَعْنِي بَيَانَ مَا يَنْبَغِي اعْتِقَادُهُ لَا مَعْرِفَةُ كَيْفِيَّةِ الرَّبِّ وَصِفَاتِهِ. وَلَيْسَتْ النُّفُوسُ الصَّحِيحَةُ إلَى شَيْءٍ أَشْوَقَ مِنْهَا إلَى مَعْرِفَةِ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ. وَهَذَا أَمْرٌ مَعْلُومٌ بِالْفِطْرَةِ الوجدية فَكَيْفَ يُتَصَوَّرُ مَعَ قِيَامِ هَذَا الْمُقْتَضِي - الَّذِي هُوَ مَنْ أَقْوَى الْمُقْتَضَيَاتِ - أَنْ يَتَخَلَّفَ عَنْهُ مُقْتَضَاهُ فِي أُولَئِكَ السَّادَةِ فِي مَجْمُوعِ عُصُورِهِمْ هَذَا لَا يَكَادُ يَقَعُ فِي أَبْلَدِ الْخَلْقِ وَأَشَدِّهِمْ إعْرَاضًا عَنْ اللَّهِ وَأَعْظَمِهِمْ إكْبَابًا عَلَى طَلَبِ الدُّنْيَا وَالْغَفْلَةِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى؛ فَكَيْفَ يَقَعُ فِي أُولَئِكَ؟
 وَأَمَّا كَوْنُهُمْ كَانُوا مُعْتَقِدِينَ فِيهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ أَوْ قَائِلِيهِ:
 فَهَذَا لَا يَعْتَقِدُهُ مُسْلِمٌ وَلَا عَاقِلٌ عَرَفَ حَالَ الْقَوْمِ.

translated_text:
knowledgeable or affirming the manifest truth in this matter. For the alternative is either to lack knowledge and say nothing, or to believe the opposite of the truth and utter what is false. Both are impossible.

As for the first possibility, anyone whose heart possesses even the slightest life and desire for knowledge, or eagerness for worship, will make investigating this matter, asking about it, and knowing the truth concerning it among his foremost aims and greatest pursuits. I mean clarifying what ought to be believed, not knowing how the Lord is or how His attributes are. Sound souls yearn for nothing more than knowledge of this matter. This is known through innate, inward awareness. How, then, could such a powerful motive—one of the strongest motives of all—fail to produce its effect among those eminent people throughout all their generations? This would scarcely occur even among the most dull-witted people, those most averse to Allah and most absorbed in pursuing worldly gain and heedless of remembering Allah Most High. How, then, could it occur among them?

As for their having believed or asserted something other than the truth in this matter, no Muslim, nor any rational person acquainted with their circumstances, would believe this.

Moreover, their recorded statements on this subject are too numerous to set down in this fatwa or even in a work many times its length. Anyone who has sought them out and traced them knows this. Nor can the later generations be more knowledgeable than the earlier ones, as some foolish people may claim—people who have failed to appreciate the worth of the early generations, and indeed have not truly known Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe in him as they are commanded to know them—when they say: “The way of the early generations is safer

These proponents of innovation, who prefer the way of the later generations—the philosophizers and those who follow their lead—to that of the early generations, fell into error because they assumed that the way of the early generations consists merely in believing the words of the Quran and hadith without understanding them, like the unlettered people of whom Allah said:

“And among them are unlettered people who know the Scripture only through mere recitation.”

They also assumed that the way of the later generations consists in extracting meanings from the texts by diverting them from their actual meanings through various metaphorical interpretations and obscure linguistic usages. This corrupt assumption gave rise to “that statement,” whose substance is to cast Islam behind one’s back. They have misrepresented the way of the early generations and gone astray in deeming the way of the later generations correct. Thus they combined ignorance of the way of the early generations, expressed in their false claims about them, with ignorance and misguidance in endorsing the way of the later generations.

The reason for this is their belief that none of the attributes indicated by these texts actually exist—a belief based on the unsound specious arguments they share with their brethren among the disbelievers. Once they believed that the attributes did not actually exist, while the texts nevertheless had to have some meaning, they remained torn between believing the wording and entrusting the meaning—which they call the way of the early generations—and diverting the wording to meanings arrived at through strained interpretation—which they call the way of the later generations. This falsehood thus became a compound of corrupted reasoning and disbelief in revelation; for, in their denial, they relied solely

on rational arguments they supposed to be clear proofs, although they were merely specious doubts; and, as for revelation, they distorted its words from their proper meanings.

Since their position rested on these two false premises founded on disbelief, the result was to regard the earliest forerunners as ignorant and foolish. They believed them to have been unlettered people, comparable to righteous common folk, who had neither delved deeply into the realities of knowing Allah nor grasped the subtleties of knowledge concerning the Divine. They believed that the distinguished scholars of the later generations had surpassed them in all these matters.

Yet anyone who reflects on this claim will find it utterly ignorant—indeed, utterly misguided. How could these later scholars—especially when “the later generations” here refers to a particular group of speculative theologians whose confusion in religious matters was great, and whose veils separating them from knowledge of Allah were thick? One who had examined the furthest reaches of their endeavors described where their course had led them, saying:

By my life, I have toured every haunt,
And cast my gaze among those landmarks;
I saw only men resting a bewildered hand upon their chin,
Or striking their teeth in remorse.

They themselves acknowledged their condition through verses they quoted or composed in the books they wrote, such as these words of one of their leading figures:

The furthest advance of reason ends in fetters,
And most of mankind’s striving goes astray.
Our souls are estranged from our bodies,
And all our worldly gain is suffering and ruin.
We gained nothing from a lifetime of inquiry
But a collection of “it was said” and “they said.”

translated_text:
“I have reflected on the methods of speculative theology and the approaches of philosophy, but I have not found them to heal the ailing or quench the thirsty. I have found the Quran’s way to be the most direct.

For affirmation, read:

‘The Most Merciful rose over the Throne.’

‘To Him ascends good speech.’

And for negation, read:

‘There is nothing like unto Him.’

‘They do not encompass Him in knowledge.’

Whoever has experienced what I have experienced will know what I have come to know.” End quote.

Another of them says:

“I plunged into the vast sea, abandoning the people of Islam and their disciplines of knowledge, and delved into what they had forbidden me to pursue. Now, unless my Lord comes to my aid with His mercy, woe to so-and-so! Here I am, dying upon my mother’s creed.” End quote.

Another of them says:

“Those most beset by doubt at the time of death are the practitioners of speculative theology.”

When the position of these speculative theologians who oppose the early generations is thoroughly examined, they are found to possess no genuine knowledge of Allah or pure understanding of Him; they have attained neither its reality nor any trace of it.

How could these men—veiled from knowledge, accorded preference, yet deficient, outstripped, bewildered and floundering—know more about Allah, His names and His attributes, or possess greater wisdom concerning His essence and His signs, than the earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in goodness: the heirs of the prophets, the successors of the messengers, the beacons of guidance and the lamps in the darkness? Through them the Book was upheld, and by it they were upheld; through them the Book spoke, and by it they spoke. Allah bestowed upon them knowledge and wisdom by which they surpassed all other followers of the prophets, let alone the other nations that have no revealed Book. Their grasp of the realities of knowledge and the inner depths of truth was such that, were the wisdom of others gathered alongside it, anyone attempting the comparison would be ashamed.

translated_text:
Then how could the best generations of this community have less knowledge and wisdom—especially knowledge of Allah and the implications of His names and signs—than these men who are so insignificant beside them? How could the fledglings of the would-be philosophers, the followers of the Indians and Greeks, the heirs of the Magians, the polytheists, and the misguided Jews, Christians and Sabians, and others of their kind, know more about Allah than the heirs of the prophets and the people of the Quran and faith?

I have presented “this introduction” only because whoever firmly grasps it will recognize where the path of guidance lies, in this matter and elsewhere. He will understand that misguidance and confusion have overtaken many of the later generations only because they cast the Book of Allah behind their backs, turned away from the clear proofs and guidance with which Allah sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, neglected to investigate the way of the earliest forerunners and their successors, and sought knowledge of Allah from those who did not know Him—as they themselves admitted, as the community testified, and as much evidence demonstrates. I am not referring to any one individual; rather, I am describing these two kinds of people.

Since this is so, the Book of Allah from beginning to end, the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from beginning to end, the general body of statements from the Companions and their successors, and the statements of all the other leading scholars are replete with passages that either explicitly state or plainly indicate that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the Most High, the Highest; that He is above everything and over everything; and that He is above the Throne and above heaven. Examples include His words, exalted is He:

“To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it.”

“Indeed, I will take you and raise you to Myself.”

“Do you feel secure that He who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you?”

“Or do you feel secure

that He who is in heaven will not send against you a storm of stones?”

“Rather, Allah raised him to Himself.”

“The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him.”

“He directs the affairs from heaven to earth, then they ascend to Him.”

“They fear their Lord above them.”

“Then He rose over the Throne”—in six passages.

“The Most Merciful rose over the Throne.”

“O Hāmān, build me a lofty tower so that I may reach the ways—”

“the ways of the heavens—and look upon the God of Moses; indeed, I think he is a liar.”

“A revelation from One All-Wise, Praiseworthy.”

“Sent down from your Lord in truth.”

There are many similar passages, which can scarcely be counted without considerable effort. The authentic and good hadiths likewise contain examples that can be counted only with considerable effort, such as the account of the Messenger’s ascent to his Lord, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the angels’ descent from Allah and ascent to Him; and his words concerning the angels who take turns among you by night and day:

“Those who have spent the night among you then go forth to their Lord, who questions them, although He knows best about them.”

In an authentic hadith concerning the Kharijites, he said:

“Will you not trust me, when I am the trusted one of Him who is in heaven? News from heaven comes to me morning and evening.”

In the hadith concerning healing through supplication, narrated by Abū Dāwūd and others:

“Our Lord is Allah, who is in heaven. Hallowed be Your name. Your command prevails in heaven and on earth. As Your mercy is in heaven, place Your mercy on earth. Forgive us our sins and our misdeeds. You are the Lord of the righteous. Send down mercy from Your mercy and healing from Your healing upon this ailment.”

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“If any of you falls ill, or a brother of his falls ill, let him say: ‘Our Lord is Allah, who is in heaven.’”

He then related the rest of the supplication. And his words in the hadith of the mountain goats:

They impart certainty of the most compelling and self-evident kind: that the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who conveyed Allah’s message, taught the community to whom he directed his call that Allah, glorified is He, is upon the Throne and above heaven. Allah has naturally disposed all peoples to this recognition, Arabs and non-Arabs alike, both before Islam and within Islam—except those whom the devils have led astray from their innate disposition. Moreover, the statements of the early generations on this subject, if collected, would number in the hundreds or thousands.

Furthermore, neither in Allah’s Book nor in the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, nor in anything transmitted from the early generations of this community—whether the Companions, those who followed them faithfully, or the imams who lived through the age of doctrinal deviations and disputes—is there a single word contradicting this, either explicitly or in its apparent meaning. None of them ever said that Allah is not in heaven, that He is not upon the Throne, that He is present in His Essence in every place, that all places are alike in relation to Him, that He is neither within the world nor outside it, that He is neither connected to it nor separate from it, or that one cannot point towards Him with one’s fingers or similar physical gestures. Rather, it is established in the authentic hadith collection, on the authority of Jābir ibn ‘Abdullāh, that:

“When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delivered his great sermon on the Day of ‘Arafāt, at the largest gathering ever attended by the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he kept asking, ‘Have I conveyed the message?’

“They replied, ‘Yes.’

“He would raise his finger towards heaven, then turn it towards them, saying more than once, ‘O Allah, bear witness.’”

 إنَّكُمْ يَا مَعْشَرَ الْعِبَادِ لَا تَطْلُبُوا مَعْرِفَةَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَمَا يَسْتَحِقُّهُ مِنْ الصِّفَاتِ نَفْيًا وَإِثْبَاتًا لَا مِنْ الْكِتَابِ وَلَا مِنْ السُّنَّةِ وَلَا مِنْ طَرِيقِ سَلَفِ الْأُمَّةِ. وَلَكِنْ اُنْظُرُوا أَنْتُمْ فَمَا وَجَدْتُمُوهُ مُسْتَحِقًّا لَهُ مِنْ الصِّفَاتِ فَصِفُوهُ بِهِ - سَوَاءٌ كَانَ مَوْجُودًا فِي الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ أَوْ لَمْ يَكُنْ - وَمَا لَمْ تَجِدُوهُ مُسْتَحِقًّا لَهُ فِي عُقُولِكُمْ فَلَا تَصِفُوهُ بِهِ.
translated_text:
the Book and the Sunnah, using these expressions and the like, rather than what the Book and the Sunnah convey either explicitly or in their apparent meaning, then how can it be supposed that Allah Most High, then His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and then the best of this community continually speak in terms that either explicitly or apparently contradict the truth, yet never disclose the truth that must be believed, nor indicate it either explicitly or apparently—until the Nabataeans among the Persians and Romans, the offspring of the Jews and Christians, and the philosophers come to explain to the community the correct creed that every morally accountable person, or every person of learning, must believe?

If what these speculative theologians, with their strained arguments, say is indeed the belief that is obligatory, and if people are nevertheless directed to rely solely on their own reason to learn it and to reject, on the strength of their rational inferences, what the Book and the Sunnah convey explicitly or apparently, then leaving people without a Book or a Sunnah would, on this supposition, have afforded them better guidance and greater benefit. Indeed, the very existence of the Book and the Sunnah would have been wholly harmful to the foundation of religion.

For what their position really amounts to is this:

“O servants of Allah, do not seek knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or of the attributes that must be affirmed or denied of Him, from the Book, the Sunnah, or the way of the early generations of this community. Instead, consider the matter yourselves: whatever attributes you find Him worthy of, ascribe them to Him—whether or not they are found in the Book and the Sunnah. Whatever attributes your reason does not find Him worthy of, do not ascribe them to Him.”

translated_text:
On this point, they fall into two groups. Most say, “Deny whatever your reason does not affirm,” while some say, “Rather, suspend judgment concerning it.”

“Whatever your rational inferences deny—inferences over which you disagree and waver more than all other people on earth—deny it, and refer to those inferences whenever you dispute. For that is the truth I have obliged you to follow. As for anything mentioned in the Book and the Sunnah that contradicts these inferences of yours, or affirms what your reason has not apprehended—according to the approach of most of them—know that I am testing you by revealing it, not so that you may derive guidance from it, but so that you may strive to explain it through irregular linguistic usages, obscure expressions, and unusual turns of speech. Alternatively, remain silent about it, entrusting knowledge of it to Allah while denying that it indicates any attributes whatsoever.”

This is what the position of these speculative theologians really amounts to. I have seen some of them explicitly state the substance of this, and it is an inescapable consequence of the position they all hold. It entails that Allah’s Book cannot serve as a guide to knowing Allah; that the Messenger is excluded from teaching and conveying the attributes of the One who sent him; and that, when people dispute, they should not refer their disagreements to Allah and the Messenger. Rather, they should refer them to the likes of what they followed in the age of ignorance, and to the likes of the authorities to which those who do not believe in the prophets turn for judgment: the Brahmins and philosophers—who are polytheists—the Magians, and some of the Sabians.

Yet referring matters in this way only makes things worse and does not resolve disagreement, for each group has its own false authorities to whom they wish to turn for judgment, although they have been commanded to reject them.

How closely the condition of these speculative theologians resembles what He, glorified and exalted, describes in His words:

“Have you not seen those who claim

that they have believed in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They wish to seek judgment from false authorities, although they were commanded to reject them. And Satan wishes to lead them far astray.”

“And when they are told, ‘Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,’ you see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion.”

“How, then, will it be when a calamity befalls them because of what their own hands have done, and they come to you swearing by Allah, ‘We intended nothing but good and reconciliation’?”

For when these people are called to the Book Allah has revealed and to the Messenger—and calling them to him after his death means calling them to his Sunnah—they turn away, saying: “Through the path we have followed, we sought excellence in knowledge and practice, and reconciliation between rational and transmitted proofs.”

Moreover, most of these specious arguments that they call proofs were simply adopted on the authority of some false authority among the polytheists or the Sabians, or some of their heirs whom they were commanded to reject, such as so-and-so and so-and-so; or from others who expressed similar views, because their hearts resemble one another.

Allah Most High says:

“But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in their disputes, then find within themselves no discomfort concerning your decision and submit fully.”

“Mankind was one community. Then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of glad tidings and warnings, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people concerning their disagreements. And none differed over it…”—to the end of the verse.

This position necessarily entails that the Book is neither guidance for people, nor a clear exposition, nor a healing

translated_text:
for what is in the hearts, nor a light, nor a source of judgment in disputes. For we know with certainty that what these people who strain their reasoning call the truth that must be believed is indicated by neither the Book nor the Sunnah, whether explicitly or through their apparent meaning. The most a would-be intellectual can do is infer this from Allah’s words:

“Nor is there to Him any equivalent.”

“Do you know of any who is His equal?”

It is self-evident to every rational person that anyone who directs people to conclude that Allah is not upon the Throne or above the heavens, and similar claims, on the basis of His words—“Do you know of any who is His equal?”—has taken a thoroughly roundabout route. He is either speaking in riddles or misleading them; he has not addressed them in clear Arabic.

This position necessarily entails that leaving people without a revealed message would have been better for them with respect to the foundations of their religion. For the authority to which they refer is the same before and after the message; the message has only increased their blindness and misguidance.

Glory be to Allah! How is it that neither the Messenger nor any of the early generations of this community ever said: “Do not believe what these verses and hadiths indicate. Instead, believe what your own criteria dictate, or believe such-and-such, for that is the truth. Do not believe the apparent meaning of any text that conflicts with it. Or examine these texts: accept whatever accords with the reasoning of your minds, and suspend judgment on whatever does not, or reject it”?

Moreover, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, foretold that his community would split into three

 فَهُوَ ضَالٌّ؟ وَإِنَّمَا الْهُدَى رُجُوعُكُمْ إلَى مَقَايِيسِ عُقُولِكُمْ وَمَا يُحْدِثُهُ الْمُتَكَلِّمُونَ مِنْكُمْ بَعْدَ الْقُرُونِ الثَّلَاثَةِ - فِي هَذِهِ الْمَقَالَةِ - وَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ نَبَغَ أَصْلُهَا فِي أَوَاخِرِ عَصْرِ التَّابِعِينَ. ثُمَّ أَصْلُ هَذِهِ الْمَقَالَةِ - مَقَالَةِ التَّعْطِيلِ لِلصِّفَاتِ - إنَّمَا هُوَ مَأْخُوذٌ عَنْ تَلَامِذَةِ الْيَهُودِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَضُلَّالِ الصَّابِئِينَ؛ فَإِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَنْ حُفِظَ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ هَذِهِ الْمَقَالَةَ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ - أَعْنِي أَنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى لَيْسَ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ حَقِيقَةً وَأَنَّ مَعْنَى اسْتَوَى بِمَعْنَى اسْتَوْلَى وَنَحْوَ ذَلِكَ - هُوَ الْجَعْدُ بْنُ دِرْهَمٍ وَأَخَذَهَا عَنْهُ الْجَهْمُ بْنُ صَفْوَانَ؛ وَأَظْهَرَهَا فَنُسِبَتْ مُقَالَةُ الْجَهْمِيَّة إلَيْهِ.
 وَقَدْ قِيلَ إنَّ الْجَعْدَ أَخَذَ مَقَالَتَهُ عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ سَمْعَانَ وَأَخَذَهَا أَبَانُ عَنْ طَالُوتَ بْنِ أُخْتِ لَبِيَدِ بْنِ الْأَعْصَمِ وَأَخَذَهَا طَالُوتُ مِنْ لَبِيَدِ بْنِ الْأَعْصَمِ:
 الْيَهُودِيِّ السَّاحِرِ الَّذِي سَحَرَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ.
translated_text:
and seventy sects; thus he knew what was to come. He then said:

“I am leaving among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah.”

It is also reported that he described the saved sect as follows:

“They are those who adhere to what I and my Companions adhere to today.”

Why, then, did he not say: “Whoever adheres to the Quran, to what it indicates, to what is understood from it, or to its apparent meaning in matters of belief is astray. Guidance lies only in your referring to the criteria of your own reason and to what the speculative theologians among you introduce concerning this doctrine after the first three generations”? Its roots, however, had already emerged toward the end of the era of the Successors.

Furthermore, this doctrine—the denial of the divine attributes—was derived only from the pupils of the Jews, the polytheists, and the misguided Sabians. The first person recorded as having professed this doctrine within Islam—namely, that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is not truly upon the Throne, that istawā (rose over) means istawlā (took control), and similar claims—was al-Jaʿd ibn Dirham. Al-Jahm ibn Safwān took it from him and propagated it, so the Jahmī doctrine came to be named after him.

It has been said that al-Jaʿd took his doctrine from Abān ibn Samʿān, that Abān took it from Tālūt, the son of Labīd ibn al-Aʿsam’s sister, and that Tālūt took it from Labīd ibn al-Aʿsam, the Jewish sorcerer who bewitched the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

translated_text:
And this al-Jaʿd ibn Dirham was reportedly from Harrān, whose inhabitants included many Sabians and philosophers—remnants of the followers of the religion of Nimrod and the Canaanites, concerning whose magic some later authors composed works. Nimrod designates the king of the polytheistic Chaldean Sabians, just as Chosroes designates the king of the Persians and Magians, Pharaoh the king of Egypt, the Negus the king of Abyssinia, Ptolemy the king of the Greeks, and Caesar the king of the Romans. It is thus a generic designation, not a proper name.

At that time, the Sabians—with few exceptions—were polytheists, and their learned men were the philosophers. A Sabian, however, may not be a polytheist, but rather a believer in Allah and the Last Day, as Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, those who believed, the Jews, the Christians, and the Sabians—whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds—will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.”

And He says:

“Indeed, those who believed, the Jews, the Sabians, and the Christians—whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds—no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.”

Yet many, or most, of them were disbelievers or polytheists, just as many Jews and Christians altered and distorted their religion and became disbelievers or polytheists. Those Sabians who lived at that time were disbelievers or polytheists; they worshipped the heavenly bodies and built temples for them.

 كَثِيرٌ فِي ذَمِّهِمْ وَتَضْلِيلِهِمْ.
translated_text:
And those among them who deny the divine attributes hold that the Lord has only negative or relational attributes, or attributes combining the two. These were the people to whom Abraham, the intimate friend of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—was sent. Al-Jaʿd would therefore have acquired these ideas from the Sabian philosophers. Likewise, Abū Nasr al-Fārābī went to Harrān and completed his study of philosophy under the Sabian philosophers. Jahm also acquired these ideas—as reported by Imam Ahmad and others—when he debated the “Sumaniyya,” a group of Indian philosophers who deny all knowledge other than sensory knowledge. Thus, Jahm’s chains of transmission lead back to the Jews, the Sabians, and the polytheists. The misguided philosophers belong either to the Sabians or to the polytheists.

Then, when Roman and Greek books were translated into Arabic around the second century AH, the affliction intensified, in addition to what Satan had instilled in the hearts of the misguided from the outset—of the same kind as what he had instilled in the hearts of their counterparts.

Around the third century AH, this doctrine, which the early generations called the doctrine of the Jahmiyya, spread through Bishr ibn Ghiyāth al-Marīsī and his contemporaries. The leading scholars—including Mālik, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, Ibn al-Mubārak, Abū Yūsuf, al-Shāfiʿī, Ahmad, Ishāq, al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyād, Bishr al-Hāfī, and others—made numerous statements condemning them and declaring them misguided.

The interpretations circulating among people today—such as most of those mentioned by Abū Bakr ibn Fūrak in his Book of Interpretations and by Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muhammad ibn ʿUmar al-Rāzī in the book he entitled Ta’sīs al-Taqdīs (The Foundation of Sanctification), many of which also appear in the writings of numerous others, including Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbā’ī, ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Ahmad al-Hamdānī, Abū al-Husayn al-Basrī, Abū al-Wafā’ ibn ʿAqīl, Abū Hāmid al-Ghazālī, and others—are the very same interpretations that Bishr al-Marīsī set out in his book. Nevertheless, the writings of some of these scholars may also contain rejection and refutation of such interpretation, and they have made sound statements on certain matters.

All I have shown is that their interpretations are identical to those of Bishr al-Marīsī. This is demonstrated by the refutation written by ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī, one of the renowned imams of al-Bukhārī’s time. He composed a book entitled “ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd’s Refutation of the Obstinate Liar concerning His Fabrications about Allah in Matters of Monotheism.” In it, he cited these very interpretations from Bishr al-Marīsī in terms indicating that al-Marīsī was more firmly grounded in them, and more knowledgeable about transmitted teachings and rational arguments, than these later scholars, to whom they had been passed down through him and others.

ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd then refuted them with arguments which, when studied by an intelligent, discerning reader, reveal the true position of the early generations, the evident strength of the case for their approach, and the weakness of their opponents’ case. A fatwa does not allow for an extensive treatment of this subject. I merely point to its starting points; an intelligent person will pursue the matter and examine it. The statements of the early generations on this subject are found in many books, only a few of which we can mention here: The Book of Traditions by al-Lālakā’ī; The Clarification by Ibn Battah; The Sunnah by Abū Dharr al-Harawī; The Fundamentals by Abū ‘Amr al-Talamankī; the statements of Abū ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Barr; and The Names and Attributes by al-Bayhaqī. Earlier still are The Sunnah by al-Khallāl; Monotheism by Ibn Khuzaymah; the statements of Abū al-‘Abbās ibn Surayj; and refutations of the Jahmiyya by a number of scholars, such as al-Bukhārī and his teacher, ‘Abd Allāh ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allāh al-Ju‘fī. Before these are The Sunnah by ‘Abd Allāh ibn Ahmad; The Sunnah by Abū Bakr ibn al-Athram; The Sunnah by Hanbal, al-Marwazī, Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī, and Ibn Abī Shaybah; The Sunnah by Abū Bakr ibn Abī ‘Āsim; The Creation of the Acts of the Servants by al-Bukhārī; and Refutation of the Jahmiyya by ‘Uthmān ibn Sa‘īd al-Dārimī and others. There are also the statements of Abū al-‘Abbās ‘Abd al-‘Azīz al-Makkī, author of al-Haydah, in refutation of the Jahmiyya; the statements of Nu‘aym ibn Hammād al-Khuzā‘ī and others; and the statements of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal

We have scriptural and rational proofs that there is not enough room to mention here. I know that the speculative theologians who deny the divine attributes have objections to raise, but these cannot be set out in a fatwa. For anyone who examines them and wishes to clarify the objections they have presented, this is easily done.

If, then, this doctrine—the doctrine of denying the divine attributes and reinterpreting the scriptural texts—was originally taken from the pupils of polytheists, Sabians, and Jews, how can a believer—indeed, any rational person—feel content to follow the path of those who have incurred Allah’s anger or gone astray, while abandoning the path of those whom Allah has blessed: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous?

translated_text:
Section

The comprehensive principle governing this entire subject is that Allah is to be described as He has described Himself, as His Messenger has described Him, and as the earliest forerunners described Him, without going beyond the Quran and hadith. Imam Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “Allah is to be described only as He has described Himself or as His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has described Him, without going beyond the Quran and hadith.”

The way of the early Muslim generations is to describe Allah as He has described Himself and as His Messenger has described Him, without distorting or denying His attributes, specifying how they are, or likening them to those of His creation. We know that these descriptions of Allah are true and contain neither riddles nor puzzles. Rather, their meaning is understood in the same way that a speaker’s intent is understood from his words—especially when the speaker is the most knowledgeable of all creation about what he says, the most eloquent of all creation in conveying knowledge, and the most eloquent of all creation in explaining, informing, indicating, and guiding.

Nevertheless, there is nothing like Him—glory be to Him—whether in His holy Self, spoken of through His names and attributes, or in His actions. Just as we know with certainty that Allah—glory be to Him—has a real essence and real actions, so too does He have real attributes. There is nothing like Him in His essence, His attributes, or His actions. Allah is truly free of everything that entails imperfection or coming into existence, for His is the perfection beyond which there is no higher degree. Coming into existence is impossible for Him because nonexistence is impossible

 إذَا كَانَ لِلْعَالَمِ صَانِعٌ فَإِمَّا أَنْ
translated_text:
for Him, and coming into existence entails prior nonexistence; because whatever comes into existence requires someone to bring it into existence; and because His existence is necessary in and of Himself—glory be to Him, the Most High.

The way of the early Muslim generations lies between denying Allah’s attributes and likening them to those of His creation. They do not liken His attributes to those of His creation, just as they do not liken His essence to the essence of His creation. Nor do they deny what He has described Himself with or what His Messenger has described Him with, which would entail negating His most beautiful names and sublime attributes, distorting words from their proper meanings, and deviating concerning Allah’s names and signs.

Each of the two groups—those who deny His attributes and those who liken them to those of His creation—combines both errors. Those who deny His attributes understand His names and attributes only in a manner appropriate to created beings, then proceed to deny the meanings they have understood. Thus, they combine denial with likening: first they liken, then they deny. In doing so, they liken and equate what is understood from His names and attributes with what is understood from the names and attributes of His creation, while denying the names and attributes that rightfully belong to Him and befit Allah—glory be to Him, the Most High.

For example, someone might say:

“If Allah were above the Throne, He would necessarily be either larger than the Throne, smaller than it, or equal to it, and all of these are impossible.”

Someone who says this, or something similar, has understood Allah’s being over the Throne only in terms of what holds true of any body over any other body. The supposed necessary consequence follows from that understanding.

As for His being established over the Throne in a manner befitting the majesty of Allah Most High and unique to Him, this entails none of the false implications that must be rejected, such as those that follow in the case of bodies generally. And his claim:

“If He is established over the Throne, His establishment resembles that of a person upon a bed or aboard a ship, since establishment is known only in this form.”

Both have likened Allah to His creation, and both have denied the reality of what Allah has described Himself with. The first is distinguished by denying every designation of true establishment, while the second affirms a kind of establishment peculiar to created beings.

The decisive position is that held by the community that follows the middle way: Allah is established over His Throne in a manner befitting His majesty and unique to Him. Just as He is described as knowing all things, having power over all things, being All-Hearing and All-Seeing, and so forth—and it is impermissible to attribute to His knowledge and power the characteristics of accidents found in the knowledge and power of created beings—so too He, glory be to Him, is above the Throne. His being above it does not possess the characteristics of one created being’s being above another, nor entail the same implications.

Know that neither sound reason nor any authentic transmitted text requires any departure whatsoever from the way of the early Muslim generations. Yet there is no room here to answer the objections raised against the truth. If anyone has a doubt in his heart and wishes to have it resolved, doing so is easy and straightforward.

Those who oppose the Quran, the Sunnah, and the early generations of the Muslim community by reinterpreting the texts on this subject are mired in confusion. Whoever denies seeing Allah claims that reason rules it out and that he is therefore compelled to reinterpret the relevant texts. the texts contain details that reason cannot grasp in detail, knowing them only in general terms. There are other lines of argument as well.

Moreover, the leading authorities among these eminent scholars acknowledge that reason has no way of attaining certainty in most questions concerning divine matters. Since this is so, knowledge of these matters must be received from prophetic revelation just as it is conveyed. Believers know that Allah Most High sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion—and Allah is sufficient as a witness—and that he explained to people what he told them concerning belief in Allah and the Last Day.

Belief in Allah and the Last Day entails belief in the beginning and the return—that is, belief in creation and resurrection—as He joined the two in His saying, Most High:

“Among the people are those who say, ‘We believe in Allah and the Last Day,’ yet they are not believers.”

He also said, Most High:

“Your creation and resurrection are but like those of a single soul.”

And He said, Most High:

“He is the One who originates creation, then repeats it.”

Through His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Allah has explained matters concerning belief in Allah and the Last Day, thereby guiding His servants and making His intent clear.

Believers know that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, knows these matters better than anyone else, is more sincere in seeking the good of the community than anyone else, and is more eloquent in expression and explanation than anyone else. Indeed, he is the most knowledgeable of all creation concerning these matters, the most sincere in seeking the community’s good, and the most eloquent. Thus, perfect knowledge, ability, and will were united in him.

وَأَمَّا الْمُنْحَرِفُونَ عَنْ طَرِيقِهِمْ:
 فَهُمْ 
" ثَلَاثُ طَوَائِفَ "
: أَهْلُ التَّخْيِيلِ وَأَهْلُ التَّأْوِيلِ وَأَهْلُ التَّجْهِيلِ.
فَأَهْلُ التَّخْيِيلِ:
 هُمْ الْمُتَفَلْسِفَةُ وَمَنْ سَلَكَ سَبِيلَهُمْ مِنْ مُتَكَلِّمٍ وَمُتَصَوِّفٍ وَمُتَفَقِّهٍ.
 فَإِنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ:
 إنَّ مَا ذَكَرَهُ الرَّسُولُ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْإِيمَانِ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ إنَّمَا هُوَ تَخْيِيلٌ لِلْحَقَائِقِ لِيَنْتَفِعَ بِهِ الْجُمْهُورُ لَا أَنَّهُ بَيَّنَ بِهِ الْحَقَّ وَلَا هَدَى بِهِ الْخَلْقَ وَلَا أَوْضَحَ بِهِ الْحَقَائِقَ.
 ثُمَّ هُمْ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ:
 مِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إنَّ الرَّسُولَ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ الْحَقَائِقَ عَلَى مَا هِيَ عَلَيْهِ.
 وَيَقُولُونَ:
 إنَّ مِنْ الْفَلَاسِفَةِ الْإِلَهِيَّةِ مَنْ عَلِمَهَا وَكَذَلِكَ مِنْ الْأَشْخَاصِ
translated_text:
his speech and actions are perfect. Deficiency arises only from a lack of knowledge, an inability to express that knowledge, or an unwillingness to explain it. The Messenger possesses the utmost perfection of knowledge, the utmost resolve to convey the message clearly, and the utmost ability to do so.

When complete ability and firm resolve are present, the intended result must follow. It is therefore known with certainty that his explanation of belief in Allah and the Last Day achieved the clarification he intended. The clarification he intended accords with his knowledge, and his knowledge of these matters is the most perfect knowledge.

Anyone who supposes that someone other than the Messenger knows these matters better than he does, explains them more fully, or is more eager to guide people is among the heretics, not the believers. The Companions, the Successors who followed them in righteousness, and those who follow their way in this matter are on the straight path.

As for those who deviate from their way, they fall into “three groups”: the proponents of takhyīl (imaginative representation), ta’wīl (interpretation), and tajhīl (ascribing ignorance).

The proponents of imaginative representation are the adherents of philosophy and those speculative theologians, Sufis, and jurists who follow their path. They say that what the Messenger mentioned concerning belief in Allah and the Last Day is merely an imaginative representation of realities intended to benefit the general public—not that he thereby explained the truth, guided people, or clarified those realities.

They, in turn, fall into two groups. Some say that the Messenger did not know those realities as they truly are. They say that some metaphysical philosophers knew them, as did some individuals

original_text:
الَّذِينَ يُسَمُّونَهُمْ الْأَوْلِيَاءَ مَنْ عَلِمَهَا وَيَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ مِنْ الْفَلَاسِفَةِ وَالْأَوْلِيَاءِ مَنْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ مِنْ الْمُرْسَلِينَ.
 وَهَذِهِ مَقَالَةُ غُلَاةِ الْمُلْحِدِينَ مِنْ الْفَلَاسِفَةِ وَالْبَاطِنِيَّةِ:
 بَاطِنِيَّةِ الشِّيعَةِ وَبَاطِنِيَّةِ الصُّوفِيَّةِ.
 وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ:
 بَلْ الرَّسُولُ عَلِمَهَا لَكِنْ لَمْ يُبَيِّنْهَا وَإِنَّمَا تَكَلَّمَ بِمَا يُنَاقِضُهَا وَأَرَادَ مِنْ الْخَلْقِ فَهْمَ مَا يُنَاقِضُهَا؛ لِأَنَّ مَصْلَحَةَ الْخَلْقِ فِي هَذِهِ الِاعْتِقَادَاتِ الَّتِي لَا تُطَابِقُ الْحَقَّ.
 وَيَقُولُ هَؤُلَاءِ:
 يَجِبُ عَلَى الرَّسُولِ أَنْ يَدْعُوَ النَّاسَ إلَى اعْتِقَادِ التَّجْسِيمِ مَعَ أَنَّهُ بَاطِلٌ وَإِلَى اعْتِقَادِ مَعَادِ الْأَبْدَانِ مَعَ أَنَّهُ بَاطِلٌ وَيُخْبِرُهُمْ بِأَنَّ أَهْلَ الْجَنَّةِ يَأْكُلُونَ وَيَشْرَبُونَ مَعَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ بَاطِلٌ.
 قَالُوا:
 لِأَنَّهُ لَا يُمْكِنُ دَعْوَةُ الْخَلْقِ إلَّا بِهَذِهِ الطَّرِيقِ الَّتِي تَتَضَمَّنُ الْكَذِبَ لِمَصْلَحَةِ الْعِبَادِ. فَهَذَا قَوْلُ هَؤُلَاءِ فِي نُصُوصِ الْإِيمَانِ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ. (وَأَمَّا الْأَعْمَالُ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُقِرُّهَا وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُجْرِيهَا هَذَا الْمَجْرَى.
 وَيَقُولُ:
 إنَّمَا يُؤْمَرُ بِهَا بَعْضُ النَّاسِ دُونَ بَعْضٍ وَيُؤْمَرُ بِهَا الْعَامَّةُ دُونَ الْخَاصَّةِ فَهَذِهِ طَرِيقَةُ الْبَاطِنِيَّةِ الْمَلَاحِدَةِ والْإِسْمَاعِيلِيَّة وَنَحْوِهِمْ.
 (وَأَمَّا أَهْلُ التَّأْوِيلِ فَيَقُولُونَ:
 إنَّ النُّصُوصَ الْوَارِدَةَ فِي الصِّفَاتِ لَمْ يَقْصِدْ بِهَا الرَّسُولُ أَنْ يَعْتَقِدَ النَّاسُ الْبَاطِلَ وَلَكِنْ قَصَدَ بِهَا مَعَانِيَ وَلَمْ يُبَيِّنْ لَهُمْ تِلْكَ الْمَعَانِيَ وَلَا دَلَّهُمْ عَلَيْهَا؛ وَلَكِنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَنْظُرُوا فَيَعْرِفُوا الْحَقَّ بِعُقُولِهِمْ ثُمَّ يَجْتَهِدُوا فِي صَرْفِ تِلْكَ النُّصُوصِ عَنْ مَدْلُولِهَا وَمَقْصُودُهُ امْتِحَانُهُمْ وَتَكْلِيفُهُمْ
translated_text:
whom they call saints. They claim that some philosophers and saints know more about Allah and the Last Day than the Messengers do.

This is the position of the extreme heretics among the philosophers and esotericists—both Shia esotericists and Sufi esotericists.

Others among them say: Rather, the Messenger knew these realities but did not explain them. Instead, he spoke in terms that contradicted them and intended people to understand the opposite of those realities, because people’s welfare lay in holding these beliefs, which do not correspond to the truth.

These people say: The Messenger must call people to believe that Allah is corporeal, even though this is false; to believe in bodily resurrection, even though this is false; and tell them that the inhabitants of Paradise eat and drink, even though this is false.

They say this is because people cannot be called except by this method, which involves lying for their welfare. This, then, is their position concerning the texts about belief in Allah and the Last Day.

(As for religious practices, some of them uphold them, while others treat them in the same manner. They say that only some people are commanded to observe them, not others: the general public is commanded to observe them, but not the elite. This is the way of the heretical esotericists, the Ismā'īlīs, and others like them.

(As for the proponents of interpretation, they say that, through the texts concerning the divine attributes, the Messenger did not intend people to believe falsehood. Rather, he intended certain meanings but neither explained those meanings to them nor directed them to them. Instead, he wanted them to reflect and discover the truth through their own reason, then strive to turn those texts away from what they signify. His purpose was to test them and impose burdens upon them

original_text:
وَإِتْعَابُ أَذْهَانِهِمْ وَعُقُولِهِمْ فِي أَنْ يَصْرِفُوا كَلَامَهُ عَنْ مَدْلُولِهِ وَمُقْتَضَاهُ وَيَعْرِفُ الْحَقَّ مِنْ غَيْرِ جِهَتِهِ وَهَذَا قَوْلُ الْمُتَكَلِّمَةِ وَالْجَهْمِيَّة وَالْمُعْتَزِلَةِ وَمَنْ دَخَلَ مَعَهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ.
 وَاَلَّذِينَ قَصَدْنَا الرَّدَّ فِي هَذِهِ الْفُتْيَا عَلَيْهِمْ:
 هُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ؛ إذْ كَانَ نُفُورُ النَّاسِ عَنْ الْأَوَّلِينَ مَشْهُورًا بِخِلَافِ هَؤُلَاءِ فَإِنَّهُمْ تَظَاهَرُوا بِنَصْرِ السُّنَّةِ فِي مَوَاضِعَ كَثِيرَةٍ وَهُمْ - فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ - لَا لِلْإِسْلَامِ نَصَرُوا وَلَا لِلْفَلَاسِفَةِ كَسَرُوا؛ لَكِنَّ أُولَئِكَ الْمَلَاحِدَةَ أَلْزَمُوهُمْ فِي النُّصُوصِ - نُصُوصِ الْمَعَادِ - نَظِيرَ مَا ادَّعُوهُ فِي نُصُوصِ الصِّفَاتِ.
 فَقَالُوا لَهُمْ:
 نَحْنُ نَعْلَمُ بِالِاضْطِرَارِ أَنَّ الرُّسُلَ جَاءَتْ بِمَعَادِ الْأَبْدَانِ وَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا فَسَادَ الشُّبَهِ الْمَانِعَةِ مِنْهُ.
 وَأَهْلُ السُّنَّةِ يَقُولُونَ لَهُمْ:
 وَنَحْنُ نَعْلَمُ بِالِاضْطِرَارِ أَنَّ الرُّسُلَ جَاءَتْ بِإِثْبَاتِ الصِّفَاتِ.
 وَنُصُوصُ الصِّفَاتِ فِي الْكُتُبِ الْإِلَهِيَّةِ:
 أَكْثَرُ وَأَعْظَمُ مِنْ نُصُوصِ الْمَعَادِ.
 وَيَقُولُونَ لَهُمْ:
 مَعْلُومٌ أَنَّ مُشْرِكِي الْعَرَبِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ كَانُوا يُنْكِرُونَ الْمَعَادَ وَقَدْ أَنْكَرُوهُ عَلَى الرَّسُولِ وَنَاظَرُوهُ عَلَيْهِ؛ بِخِلَافِ الصِّفَاتِ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يُنْكِرْ شَيْئًا مِنْهَا أَحَدٌ مِنْ الْعَرَبِ.
 فَعُلِمَ أَنَّ إقْرَارَ الْعُقُولِ بِالصِّفَاتِ:
 أَعْظَمُ مِنْ إقْرَارِهَا بِالْمَعَادِ وَأَنَّ إنْكَارَ الْمَعَادِ أَعْظَمُ مِنْ إنْكَارِ الصِّفَاتِ فَكَيْفَ يَجُوزُ مَعَ هَذَا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ مِنْ الصِّفَاتِ لَيْسَ كَمَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ وَمَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ مِنْ الْمَعَادِ هُوَ عَلَى مَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ
translated_text:
and exhaust their minds and intellects in turning his words away from their meaning and implications, and in learning the truth from a source other than him. This is the position of the speculative theologians, the Jahmiyyah, the Muʿtazilah, and those who have joined them in any part of this approach.

These are the ones we intended to refute in this fatwa. People’s aversion to the former group is well known, unlike their attitude toward these, who have made a show of championing the Sunnah in many instances. In reality, however, they have neither supported Islam nor defeated the philosophers. Rather, those heretics confronted them with the same implications concerning the texts on resurrection as their own claims entailed concerning the texts on the divine attributes.

They said to them:
“We know of necessity that the Messengers taught bodily resurrection, and we know that the objections denying its possibility are invalid.”

The people of the Sunnah say to them:
“And we know of necessity that the Messengers came affirming the divine attributes.”

The texts concerning the divine attributes in the revealed scriptures are more numerous and more weighty than the texts concerning resurrection.

They also say to them:
“It is well known that the Arab polytheists and others denied resurrection. They rejected the Messenger’s teaching on it and debated it with him. This was not the case with the divine attributes, for none of the Arabs denied any of them.

“Thus, it is clear that reason’s acceptance of the divine attributes is greater than its acceptance of resurrection, and that denial of resurrection is greater than denial of the attributes. How, then, can it be permissible to hold that what he reported concerning the attributes is not as he reported it, while what he reported concerning resurrection is exactly as he reported it?”

original_text:
وَأَيْضًا؛ فَقَدْ عُلِمَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَدّ ذَمَّ أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ عَلَى مَا حَرَّفُوهُ وَبَدَّلُوهُ وَمَعْلُومٌ أَنَّ التَّوْرَاةَ مَمْلُوءَةٌ مِنْ ذِكْرِ الصِّفَاتِ فَلَوْ كَانَ هَذَا مِمَّا بُدِّلَ وَحُرِّفَ لَكَانَ إنْكَارُ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْلَى فَكَيْفَ وَكَانُوا إذَا ذَكَرُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ الصِّفَاتِ يَضْحَكُ تَعَجُّبًا مِنْهُمْ وَتَصْدِيقًا لَهَا وَلَمْ يَعِبْهُمْ قَطُّ بِمَا تَعِيبُ الْنُّفَاةِ أَهْلَ الْإِثْبَاتِ مِثْلَ لَفْظِ التَّجْسِيمِ وَالتَّشْبِيهِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ؛
 بَلْ عَابَهُمْ بِقَوْلِهِمْ:
 
{يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ}
 وَقَوْلِهِمْ: 
{إنَّ اللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ وَنَحْنُ أَغْنِيَاءُ}
 وَقَوْلِهِمْ: إنَّهُ اسْتَرَاحَ لَمَّا خَلَقَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فَقَالَ تَعَالَى: 
{وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِنْ لُغُوبٍ}
 . وَالتَّوْرَاةُ مَمْلُوءَةٌ مِنْ الصِّفَاتِ الْمُطَابِقَةِ لِلصِّفَاتِ الْمَذْكُورَةِ فِي الْقُرْآنِ وَالْحَدِيثِ؛ وَلَيْسَ فِيهَا تَصْرِيحٌ بِالْمَعَادِ كَمَا فِي الْقُرْآنِ. فَإِذَا جَازَ أَنْ تَتَأَوَّلَ الصِّفَاتُ الَّتِي اتَّفَقَ عَلَيْهَا الْكِتَابَانِ فَتَأْوِيلُ الْمَعَادِ الَّذِي انْفَرَدَ بِهِ أَحَدُهُمَا أَوْلَى وَالثَّانِي مِمَّا يُعْلَمُ بِالِاضْطِرَارِ مِنْ دِينِ الرَّسُولِ أَنَّهُ بَاطِلٌ فَالْأَوَّلُ أَوْلَى بِالْبُطْلَانِ. (وَأَمَّا الصِّنْفُ الثَّالِثُ وَهُمْ (أَهْلُ التَّجْهِيلِ فَهُمْ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ الْمُنْتَسِبِينَ إلَى السُّنَّةِ وَاتِّبَاعِ السَّلَفِ.
 يَقُولُونَ:
 إنَّ الرَّسُولَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمْ يَعْرِفْ مَعَانِيَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إلَيْهِ مِنْ آيَاتِ الصِّفَاتِ وَلَا جِبْرِيلُ يَعْرِفُ مَعَانِيَ الْآيَاتِ وَلَا السَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ عَرَفُوا ذَلِكَ.
 وَكَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُمْ فِي أَحَادِيثِ الصِّفَاتِ:
 إنَّ مَعْنَاهَا لَا يَعْلَمُهُ إلَّا اللَّهُ مَعَ أَنَّ الرَّسُولَ تَكَلَّمَ بِهَا ابْتِدَاءً فَعَلَى قَوْلِهِمْ تَكَلَّمَ بِكَلَامِ لَا يَعْرِفُ مَعْنَاهُ.
translated_text:
Moreover, it is well known that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, condemned the People of the Book for what they had distorted and altered. It is also well known that the Torah is filled with references to the divine attributes. Had these been among the things altered and distorted, they would have deserved even greater condemnation for that. Yet when they mentioned the attributes in his presence, he would laugh in amazement at them and in affirmation of those attributes. He never reproached them with the accusations that those who deny the attributes level against those who affirm them, such as corporealism, likening Allah to His creation, and the like.

Rather, he reproached them for saying:

“Allah’s hand is fettered,”

and:

“Allah is poor, while we are rich,”

and for saying that He rested after creating the heavens and the earth. Allah Most High therefore said:

“We certainly created the heavens and the earth and everything between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us.”

The Torah is filled with attributes corresponding to those mentioned in the Quran and hadith, yet it contains no explicit affirmation of resurrection comparable to that in the Quran. If it were permissible to reinterpret the attributes affirmed by both scriptures, then reinterpreting resurrection, which only one of them explicitly affirms, would be even more warranted. Yet it is necessarily known from the Messenger’s religion that the latter is false; the former is therefore even more clearly false.

As for the third group—those who attribute ignorance—they include many who profess adherence to the Sunnah and claim to follow the early generations. They say that the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not know the meanings of the verses concerning the attributes that Allah revealed to him; that Gabriel did not know their meanings either; and that the earliest forerunners in faith did not know them.

They likewise say of the hadiths concerning the attributes that Allah alone knows their meaning, even though the Messenger himself initially uttered them. According to their view, then, he spoke words whose meaning he did not know.

These people think that they have followed the words of Allah Most High:

“And no one knows its interpretation except Allah.”

Most of the early generations did indeed pause at His words:

“And no one knows its interpretation except Allah.”

This is a valid place to pause. However, these people failed to distinguish between the meaning and explanation of the words and the “ta’wīl” of which Allah Most High alone has knowledge. They assumed that the “ta’wīl” mentioned in the words of Allah Most High is the same as the “ta’wīl” spoken of by later scholars. In this they were mistaken, for the term “ta’wīl” has three meanings.

In the terminology of many later scholars, “ta’wīl” means diverting an expression from its more likely meaning to a less likely meaning on the basis of supporting evidence. Thus, in their terminology, a meaning that accords with an expression’s apparent sense is not ta’wīl. They assumed that this was what Allah Most High intended by the term ta’wīl, and that the scriptural texts have an interpretation contrary to what they indicate, known only to Allah and unknown to those who interpret them.

Yet many of these people say, “These texts are to be taken in their apparent sense, and their apparent sense is intended,” while also saying that they have a ta’wīl in this sense which Allah alone knows. This is a contradiction into which many who profess adherence to the Sunnah have fallen, including followers of the “four imams” and others.

The second meaning of “ta’wīl” is the explanation of speech—whether or not it accords with its apparent sense. This is “ta’wīl” in the terminology of the majority of Quran commentators and others. “And no one knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly grounded in knowledge.”

This is reported from Ibn ‘Abbās, Mujāhid, Muhammad ibn Ja‘far ibn al-Zubayr, Muhammad ibn Ishāq, Ibn Qutaybah, and others. Both views are correct in their respective senses, as we have explained at length elsewhere. Hence both views have been transmitted from Ibn ‘Abbās, and both are correct.

The third meaning is that ta’wīl is the reality to which the words ultimately refer—even when it accords with their apparent meaning. Thus, the ta’wīl of what Allah has told us about eating, drinking, clothing, and marital relations in Paradise, the coming of the Hour, and other matters consists of the actual realities themselves, not the meanings conceived in the mind and expressed in speech. This is “ta’wīl” in the language of the Quran, as Allah Most High relates that Joseph said:

“O my father, this is the fulfilment of my earlier dream. My Lord has made it come true.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Are they waiting for anything but its fulfilment? On the day its fulfilment comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, ‘The messengers of our Lord certainly came with the truth.’”

And Allah Most High says:

“If you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is better and best in outcome.”

This is the ta’wīl that Allah alone knows. The ta’wīl of the “attributes” is the reality whose knowledge belongs exclusively to Allah Most High. translated_text:
the ta’wīl known to those firmly grounded in knowledge. As for the manner of that istiwā’, it is the ta’wīl that none but Allah Most High knows.

It is reported from Ibn ‘Abbās, as ‘Abd al-Razzāq and others mention in their Quran commentaries, that he said:

“The explanation of the Quran falls into four categories: an explanation that the Arabs know from their language; an explanation for whose ignorance no one is excused; an explanation known to the scholars; and an explanation known only to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whoever claims to know this last category is a liar.”

This accords with the words of Allah Most High:

“No soul knows what delights are kept hidden for them as a reward for what they used to do.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah Most High says: ‘I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined.’”

Likewise, knowledge of the time of the Hour and similar matters belongs to the ta’wīl that none but Allah Most High knows, even though we understand the meanings of what is addressed to us and grasp from the words what we are meant to understand. As Allah Most High says:

“Do they not reflect upon the Quran, or are there locks upon their hearts?”

He also says:

“Have they not reflected upon the word?”

Thus, He commanded reflection upon the Quran, not merely upon part of it.

Abū ‘Abd al-Rahmān al-Sulamī said:

“Those who used to teach us the Quran—‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān, ‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd, and others—told us that when they learned ten verses from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, they would not proceed beyond them until they had learned the knowledge and practice set forth in them. They said: ‘Thus we learned the Quran, knowledge, and practice together.’”

" بَابِ مَعْرِفَةِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ "
 لَا عُلُومًا عَقْلِيَّةً وَلَا سَمْعِيَّةً؛ وَهُمْ قَدْ شَارَكُوا الْمَلَاحِدَةَ فِي هَذِهِ مِنْ وُجُوهٍ مُتَعَدِّدَةٍ وَهُمْ مُخْطِئُونَ فِيمَا نَسَبُوا إلَى الرَّسُولِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَإِلَى السَّلَفِ مِنْ الْجَهْلِ كَمَا أَخْطَأَ فِي ذَلِكَ أَهْلُ التَّحْرِيفِ وَالتَّأْوِيلَاتِ الْفَاسِدَةِ وَسَائِرُ أَصْنَافِ الْمَلَاحِدَةِ. وَنَحْنُ نَذْكُرُ مِنْ 
" أَلْفَاظِ السَّلَفِ "
 بِأَعْيَانِهَا 
" وَأَلْفَاظِ مَنْ نُقِلَ مَذْهَبُهُمْ "
 - إلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ الْوُجُوهِ بِحَسَبِ مَا يَحْتَمِلُهُ هَذَا الْمَوْضِعُ - مَا يُعْلَمُ بِهِ مَذْهَبُهُمْ.
translated_text:
And Mujāhid said:

“I recited the Quran to Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from beginning to end, stopping at each verse and asking him about it.”

Al-Sha‘bī said:

“No one has ever introduced an innovation without its clarification being found in the Book of Allah.”

Masrūq said:

“The Companions of Muhammad were never asked about anything without knowledge of it being in the Quran, but our knowledge fell short of reaching it.”

This is a vast subject that has been discussed at length in its proper place.

The purpose here is to draw attention to the foundations of the “false doctrines” that have led to misguidance concerning knowledge of, and faith in, what the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought. Anyone who holds that neither the Messenger nor Gabriel knew the meanings of the Quran revealed to him thereby holds that the Messenger lacked knowledge of matters conveyed by revelation, and does not regard the Quran as guidance or clarification for mankind.

Moreover, these people reject rational knowledge in this field altogether. Thus, they hold that the Messenger and his community possess neither rational nor revealed knowledge concerning “knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.” In this, they share common ground with the heretics in several respects. They are mistaken in attributing ignorance to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and to the early generations, just as those who distort the texts and advance false interpretations, and all the other categories of heretics, are mistaken in this regard.

We shall cite the exact “words of the early generations” and the “words of those whose doctrine has been transmitted,” together with other lines of evidence, as far as this discussion allows, to make their doctrine known.

translated_text:
Abū Bakr al-Bayhaqī narrated in al-Asmā’ wa-l-Sifāt (The Names and Attributes), through an authentic chain of transmission, that al-Awzā‘ī said:

“We used to say, while the Successors were still numerous: Allah—exalted be His mention—is above His Throne, and we believe in His attributes reported in the Sunnah.”

Al-Awzā‘ī was one of the four imams in the generation following the Successors: Mālik, the imam of the people of the Hijaz; al-Awzā‘ī, the imam of the people of Syria; al-Layth, the imam of the people of Egypt; and al-Thawrī, the imam of the people of Iraq. He reported that belief in Allah Most High being above the Throne, and in His attributes conveyed by revelation, was widespread during the time of the Successors. Al-Awzā‘ī made this statement only after the emergence of Jahm’s doctrine, which denied that Allah is above His Throne and negated His attributes, so that people would know that the doctrine of the early generations was contrary to it.

Abū Bakr al-Khallāl narrated in Kitāb al-Sunnah (The Book of the Sunnah) that al-Awzā‘ī said:

“Makhūl and al-Zuhrī were asked about the interpretation of the hadiths, and they said: ‘Let them pass as they have come.’”

He also narrated that al-Walīd ibn Muslim said:

“I asked Mālik ibn Anas, Sufyān al-Thawrī, al-Layth ibn Sa‘d, and al-Awzā‘ī about the reports concerning the divine attributes. They said: ‘Let them pass as they have come.’”

In another narration, they said: “Let them pass as they have come, without specifying how.”

Their words—may Allah be pleased with them—“Let them pass as they have come” refute those who negate the divine attributes, while their words “without specifying how” refute those who liken Allah to His creation.

Al-Zuhrī and Makhūl were the two most learned of the Successors in their time

translated_text:
and the other four were the leading imams of the world in the generation following the Successors. Hammād ibn Zayd, Hammād ibn Salamah, and others like them belonged to that same generation.

Abū al-Qāsim al-Azajī narrated through his chain of transmission from Mutarrif ibn ‘Abd Allāh, who said:

“I heard Mālik ibn Anas, whenever someone who rejected the hadiths concerning the divine attributes was mentioned in his presence, say that ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azīz said:

‘The Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and those who held authority after him established practices. Adhering to them affirms the Book of Allah, completes obedience to Allah, and strengthens adherence to Allah’s religion. None of Allah Most High’s creation has the right to change them or to consider anything contrary to them. Whoever seeks guidance through them is rightly guided; whoever seeks support through them is granted support. Whoever opposes them and follows a path other than that of the believers, Allah will leave him to what he has chosen and cause him to burn in Hell—an evil destination.’”

Al-Khallāl narrated through a chain whose transmitters were all trustworthy imams, from Sufyān ibn ‘Uyaynah, who said:

“Rabī‘ah ibn Abī ‘Abd al-Rahmān was asked about His words, ‘The Most Merciful rose over the Throne’: ‘How did He rise over it?’

“He replied: ‘Rising over the Throne is not unknown, and its manner cannot be comprehended. The message comes from Allah; the Messenger’s duty is to convey it clearly, and ours is to affirm its truth.’”

This statement is also narrated through several routes from Mālik ibn Anas, the student of Rabī‘ah ibn Abī ‘Abd al-Rahmān.

(Among these is the report narrated by Abū al-Shaykh al-Asbahānī and Abū Bakr al-Bayhaqī from Yahyā ibn Yahyā, who said:

“We were with Mālik ibn Anas when a man came and said, ‘O Abū ‘Abd Allāh:

translated_text:
“The Most Merciful rose over the Throne”—how did He rise over it?’

Mālik lowered his head until he broke out in perspiration. Then he said, ‘Rising over the Throne is not unknown, and its manner cannot be comprehended. Believing in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation. I can only regard you as an innovator.’ Then he ordered that the man be removed.”

The statement of Rabī‘ah and Mālik, “Rising over the Throne is not unknown, and its manner cannot be comprehended, and believing in it is obligatory,” agrees with the statement of the others: “Let them stand as they have come, without specifying how.” They denied knowledge of the manner, not the reality of the attribute. Had they believed only in the bare wording, without understanding its meaning in a sense befitting Allah, they would not have said, “Rising over the Throne is not unknown, and its manner cannot be comprehended.” Nor would they have said, “Let them stand as they have come, without specifying how.” For rising over the Throne would then have been unknown rather than known, like the letters of the alphabet.

Furthermore, there is no need to deny knowledge of the manner if no meaning is understood from the wording. The need to deny knowledge of the manner arises only when the attributes are affirmed.

Furthermore, someone who denies the attributes known through revelation—or denies the attributes altogether—has no need to say, “Without specifying how.” Someone who says, “Allah is not over the Throne,” has no need to say, “Without specifying how.” Had the position of the early generations been to deny that the attributes actually exist, they would not have said, “Without specifying how.”
