say: “Let their wording stand, while believing that what is understood from it is not intended,” or, “Let their wording stand, while believing that Allah is not truly described by what it signifies.” In that case, they would not have been allowed to stand as they came, nor would it then be said, “Without specifying how,” for denying the manner of something that is not affirmed is meaningless talk.

Al-Athram in al-Sunnah, Abū ‘Abd Allāh ibn Battah in al-Ibānah, Abū ‘Amr al-Talamankī, and others narrated through an authentic chain of transmission the following response from ‘Abd al-‘Azīz ibn ‘Abd Allāh ibn Abī Salamah al-Mājishūn—one of the “three imams of Medina,” namely Mālik ibn Anas, Ibn al-Mājishūn, and Ibn Abī Dhi’b—when he was asked about what the Jahmiyyah denied:

“To proceed: I have understood your question concerning what the Jahmiyyah and their followers have followed one another in saying about the attributes of the Magnificent Lord. His greatness surpasses all description and contemplation; tongues fail to explain His attributes, and minds fall short of comprehending His power. His greatness has repelled the minds, leaving them no way forward, so they have returned humbled and exhausted. They were commanded only to observe and reflect upon what He has created in due measure. The question ‘How?’ is asked only about one who once did not exist and then came into being. As for Him who neither changes nor passes away, who has always existed and has no equal, none but He knows how He is.

“How can the measure of Him who had no beginning, who neither dies nor decays, be known? How could any of His attributes have a limit or an endpoint that anyone could know, or whose extent anyone describing Him could define? Yet He is the manifest Truth: no truth is truer than He, and nothing is more evident than He. The proof that minds are incapable of fully comprehending His attributes is their inability to fully comprehend

the attributes of His smallest creature, so tiny that you can scarcely see it. It moves about and comes and goes, yet neither its hearing nor its sight can be seen. The workings of its intelligence, by which it acts and devises, are harder for you to grasp and more hidden from you than what is apparent of its hearing and sight. Blessed, then, is Allah, the best of creators and their Creator, the Master of all masters and their Lord:

“There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.”

Recognize—may Allah have mercy on you—that your inability to know the full extent of the attributes the Lord has described frees you from straining to describe what He has not described of Himself. If you do not know the full extent of what He has described, why burden yourself with seeking knowledge of what He has not described? Would such knowledge guide you to any act of obedience to Him, or deter you from any act of disobedience to Him?

As for the one who denies what the Lord has described of Himself through excessive probing and strained speculation, “the devils have lured him astray on earth, bewildered.” He then begins adducing what he claims are proofs for denying the attributes the Lord has described and named for Himself, saying: “If He has such-and-such, He must necessarily have such-and-such.” Thus, what is hidden blinds him to what is clear. He denies what the Lord has named for Himself because the Lord has remained silent about attributes He has not named. Satan continues to lead him on until he denies the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

“On that Day faces will be radiant, looking at their Lord.”

He says: “No one will see Him on the Day of Resurrection.” By Allah, he has thereby denied the greatest honor Allah bestows upon His friends on the Day of Resurrection: looking upon His face, and His making them radiant, “in a seat of honor with an All-Powerful Sovereign.” He has decreed that they will not die, and they grow radiant through looking upon Him.”

He went on to say:

“He denied seeing Allah on the Day of Resurrection only to uphold a misguided and misleading argument, for he

knew that, when He manifested Himself to them on the Day of Resurrection, they would see of Him what they had previously believed in and what he had denied.

The Muslims asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, replied, ‘Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun when no clouds obscure it?’

They said, ‘No.’

He asked, ‘Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon on the night of the full moon when no clouds obscure it?’

They said, ‘No.’

He said, ‘You will likewise see your Lord on that Day.’

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

‘The Fire will not be filled until the Compeller places His foot in it. Then it will say, “Enough, enough!” and its parts will draw together.’

He said to Thābit ibn Qays:

‘Allah has indeed laughed at what you did for your guest last night.’

According to what has reached us, he also said:

‘Allah Most High indeed laughs at your distress and despair, and at how swiftly you are answered.’

An Arab man asked him, ‘Does our Lord really laugh?’

He replied, ‘Yes.’

The man said, ‘We shall not lack goodness from a Lord who laughs.’

There are more reports like these than we can count. Allah Most High says:

‘And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.’

‘And be patient for the judgment of your Lord, for indeed, you are under Our eyes.’

Allah Most High also says:

‘And that you would be brought up under My eye.’

And He says:

‘What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?’

And He says:

‘The entire earth will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.’

By Allah, nothing showed them the greatness of what He has described of Himself, and of what His grasp encompasses, except the smallness of the corresponding grasp they themselves possess. Indeed, this is what was instilled in their minds and fashioned in accordance with their hearts’ understanding.

translated_text:
Thus, whatever Allah has described of Himself and named through His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, we name just as He has named it, without presuming to ascribe anything else to Him. We follow neither of the two courses: we neither deny what He has described nor presume to know what He has not described.

Know—may Allah have mercy on you—that safeguarding your religion means stopping where you have been directed to stop and not exceeding the limits set for you. Recognizing what is right and rejecting what is wrong are among the foundations that sustain religion. Whatever is recognized, in which hearts find reassurance, whose basis is mentioned in the Book and the Sunnah, and whose knowledge the Muslim community has passed down, do not fear that mentioning it and describing your Lord as He has described Himself entails any imperfection. Nor should you presume to determine a measure for what has been described to you.

Whatever your soul rejects, and which you find mentioned neither in your Lord’s Book nor in a hadith from your Prophet concerning your Lord’s attributes, do not strain to comprehend it through your own reason or describe Him with it. Remain silent about it, just as the Lord has remained silent about it concerning Himself. For presuming to know what He has not described of Himself is like denying what He has described. Just as you regard the deniers’ denial of what He has described of Himself as a grave matter, so too regard as grave the presumption of those who ascribe to Him what He has not described of Himself.

Rare indeed, by Allah, are those Muslims who recognize what is right, through whom it is recognized, and who reject what is wrong, through whose rejection it is rejected. They hear these descriptions that Allah has given of Himself in His Book, and similar reports that have reached them from His Prophet. No Muslim’s heart has been troubled by mentioning these attributes and naming them, nor has any believer presumed to describe their measure or to ascribe anything else to the Lord.

translated_text:
Whatever the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have named among his Lord’s attributes has the same standing as what the Lord Most High has named and described of Himself. Those firmly grounded in knowledge—who stop where their knowledge ends, describe their Lord as He has described Himself, and refrain from mentioning what He has left unmentioned—neither deny the attributes He has named nor presume, through excessive speculation, to describe Him with what He has not named. For the truth lies in leaving unmentioned what He has left unmentioned and naming what He has named.

‘Whoever follows a path other than that of the believers, We will leave him to what he has chosen and burn him in Hell—what an evil destination!’

May Allah grant us and you wisdom and join us with the righteous.”

All of this is the statement of Imam Ibn al-Mājishūn. Reflect upon it, and consider how he affirmed the attributes while denying knowledge of their manner—in agreement with the other imams—and how he rebuked those who deny the attributes on the grounds that affirming them would entail such-and-such consequences. This is what the Jahmiyyah say: that He would necessarily be a body or an accident, and would therefore be originated.

In Al-Fiqh al-Akbar (The Greater Understanding), a book well known among the followers of Abū Hanīfah, which they transmitted with a chain of narration from Abū Mutīʿ, al-Hakam ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Balkhī, he said: “I asked Abū Hanīfah about the greater understanding, and he replied: ‘Do not declare anyone an unbeliever because of a sin, nor exclude anyone from faith on its account. Enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. Know that whatever has befallen you could never have missed you, and whatever has missed you could never have befallen you. Do not disavow any of the Companions of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, nor give your allegiance to some to the exclusion of others. Entrust the affair of ʿUthmān and ʿAlī to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.’”

He thereby explained that Allah’s words,

“The Most Merciful rose over the Throne,”

show that Allah is above the heavens, above the Throne, and that His rising over the Throne indicates that Allah Himself is above the Throne.

He then followed this by declaring an unbeliever the person who says that He rose over the Throne but suspends judgment as to whether the Throne is in heaven or on earth. He said, “Because he has denied that He is in heaven; for Allah is in the highest heights, and supplication is directed to Him above, not below.”

This is an explicit statement by Abū Hanīfah declaring anyone who denies that Allah is in heaven to be an unbeliever. He supported this with the arguments that Allah is in the highest heights and that supplication is directed to Him above, not below. Shaykh al-Islām Abū Ismā‘īl al-Ansārī al-Harawī transmitted this wording from him with a chain of narration in Kitāb al-Fārūq.

Ibn Abī Hātim also reported that Hishām ibn ‘Ubayd Allāh al-Rāzī—a companion of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and the judge of Rayy—imprisoned a man for adhering to Jahmī doctrines. The man repented and was brought before Hishām to be released. He said, “Praise be to Allah for repentance.” Hishām then tested him, asking:

“Do you testify that Allah is above His Throne, distinct from His creation?”

He replied, “I testify that Allah is above His Throne, but I do not know what ‘distinct from His creation’ means.”

Hishām said, “Return him to prison, for he has not repented.”

It is also reported that Yahyā ibn Mu‘ādh al-Rāzī said:

“Allah is above the Throne, distinct from creation. His knowledge encompasses everything, and He has counted everything precisely. None doubts this statement except a vile, misguided Jahmī, doomed and beset by doubt, who mingles Allah with His creation and mixes His Essence with filth and foul stenches.”

It is also reported that Ibn al-Madīnī, when asked, “What do the people of the united community believe?” replied:

“They believe in seeing Allah and in His speech, and that Allah is above the heavens, having risen over the Throne.”

He was then asked about His words:

“There is no private conversation between three but He is their fourth.”

He replied, “Read what precedes it:

‘Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth?’”

 مِنْ غَيْرِ تَفْسِيرٍ؛ وَلَا وَصْفٍ وَلَا تَشْبِيهٍ؛ فَمَنْ فَسَّرَ الْيَوْمَ شَيْئًا مِنْهَا فَقَدْ خَرَجَ مِمَّا كَانَ عَلَيْهِ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَفَارَقَ الْجَمَاعَةَ؛ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَمْ يَصِفُوا وَلَمْ يُفَسِّرُوا؛ وَلَكِنْ أَفْتَوْا بِمَا فِي الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ ثُمَّ سَكَتُوا؛
 فَمَنْ قَالَ:
 بِقَوْلِ جَهْمٍ فَقَدْ فَارَقَ الْجَمَاعَةَ لِأَنَّهُ قَدْ وَصَفَهُ بِصِفَةِ لَا شَيْءَ. مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ أَخَذَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَمَالِكٍ وَطَبَقَتِهِمَا مِنْ الْعُلَمَاءِ. وَقَدْ حَكَى هَذَا الْإِجْمَاعَ وَأَخْبَرَ أَنَّ الْجَهْمِيَّة تَصِفُهُ بِالْأُمُورِ السَّلْبِيَّةِ غَالِبًا أَوْ دَائِمًا.
 وَقَوْلُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ تَفْسِيرٍ:
 أَرَادَ بِهِ تَفْسِيرَ "
 الْجَهْمِيَّة الْمُعَطِّلَةِ " الَّذِينَ ابْتَدَعُوا تَفْسِيرَ الصِّفَاتِ بِخِلَافِ مَا كَانَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّحَابَةُ وَالتَّابِعُونَ مِنْ الأثبات.
translated_text:
It is also reported that Abū ‘Īsā al-Tirmidhī said:

“He is above the Throne, as He has described in His Book, and His knowledge, power, and authority are everywhere.”

It is reported that when Abū Zur‘ah al-Rāzī was asked about the interpretation of His words:

“The Most Merciful rose over the Throne,”

he replied: “Its interpretation is just as it is recited: He is above the Throne, and His knowledge is everywhere. Whoever says otherwise, may Allah’s curse be upon him.”

Abū al-Qāsim al-Lālakā’ī al-Tabarī, the hadith master and companion of Abū Hāmid al-Isfarāyīnī, reported in his well-known book on the Fundamentals of the Sunnah, through his chain of narration, that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, the companion of Abū Hanīfah, said:

“All the jurists, from east to west, have agreed upon believing in the Quran and the hadith concerning the attributes of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, transmitted by trustworthy narrators from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace—without interpretation, description, or likening Him to creation. Whoever today interprets any of these has departed from what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, followed and has separated from the united community. For they neither described nor interpreted; rather, they issued rulings according to the Book and the Sunnah, then remained silent. Whoever adopts Jahm’s teaching has separated from the united community, for he has described Him as nothing at all.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan studied under Abū Hanīfah, Mālik, and scholars of their generation. He reported this consensus and stated that the Jahmīs describe Him mostly—or always—in negative terms.

By his words “without interpretation,” he meant the interpretation of the Jahmīs who deny the divine attributes: those who introduced an interpretation of the attributes contrary to the affirmation upheld by the Companions and their successors.

translated_text:
Al-Bayhaqī and others narrated with an authentic chain of transmission that Abū ‘Ubayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām said:

“These hadiths which state, ‘Our Lord laughed at His servants’ despair despite the nearness of the change He would bring,’ ‘Hell will not be filled until your Lord places His Foot in it,’ and ‘The Footstool is the place of the two Feet,’ together with the hadiths concerning seeing Allah, are true according to us. Trustworthy narrators transmitted them from one another. However, when asked to interpret them, we do not interpret them, and we never encountered anyone who did so.”

Abū ‘Ubayd was one of the four imams: al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad, Ishāq, and Abū ‘Ubayd. His knowledge of jurisprudence, language, and scriptural interpretation is too well known to need describing. He lived at a time when tribulations and deviant doctrines emerged, yet he stated that he had never encountered any scholar who interpreted these reports—that is, in the manner of the Jahmīs.

Al-Lālakā’ī and al-Bayhaqī narrated through their respective chains of transmission that a man said to ‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak: “Abū ‘Abd al-Rahmān, I dislike descriptions”—meaning descriptions of the Lord.

‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak replied: “No one dislikes that more than I do. Nevertheless, when the Book states something, we affirm it; and when the transmitted reports convey something, we venture to affirm it”—or words to that effect.

Ibn al-Mubārak meant that we dislike initiating descriptions of Allah on our own authority before they are conveyed by the Book and the transmitted reports.

 لَيْسَ فِي أَصْحَابِ
translated_text:
“By what do we know our Lord?”

He replied: “By the fact that He is above His heavens, upon His Throne, distinct from His creation. We do not say, as the Jahmīs do, that He is here on earth.” Imam Ahmad and others said the same.

It is narrated through an authentic chain of transmission that Imam Sulaymān ibn Harb said: “I heard Hammād ibn Zayd mention these Jahmīs and say: ‘They are only trying to say that there is nothing in heaven.’”

In his book al-Radd ‘alā al-Jahmiyyah (The Refutation of the Jahmīs), Ibn Abī Hātim narrated that when the Jahmīs were mentioned in the presence of Sa‘īd ibn ‘Āmir al-Duba‘ī—the leading scholar of Basra in knowledge and religious devotion, and one of Imam Ahmad’s teachers—he said:

“What they say is worse than what the Jews and Christians say. The Jews, Christians, and adherents of other religions, together with the Muslims, have agreed that Allah is upon the Throne, whereas they say that He is not upon anything.”

Muhammad ibn Ishāq ibn Khuzaymah, the imam of imams, said:

“Anyone who does not affirm that Allah is above His heavens, upon His Throne, distinct from His creation, must be called upon to repent. If he repents, well and good; otherwise, he is to be beheaded and then cast onto a rubbish heap, so that neither Muslims nor non-Muslims under the covenant of protection are troubled by his stench.”

Al-Hākim related this from him through an authentic chain of transmission.

‘Abd Allāh, the son of Imam Ahmad, narrated through his chain of transmission that ‘Abbād ibn al-‘Awwām al-Wāsitī—the leading scholar of Wāsit, who belonged to the generation of al-Shāfi‘ī’s and Ahmad’s teachers—said:

“I spoke with Bishr al-Marīsī and his followers, and found that their arguments ultimately led to saying: ‘There is nothing in heaven.’”

In al-Radd ‘alā al-Jahmiyyah (The Refutation of the Jahmīs), ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Abī Hātim narrated that ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Mahdī said:

“The followers of Jahm intend to say that Allah did not speak to Moses. They intend to say: ‘There is nothing in heaven, and Allah is not upon the Throne.’ I hold that they should be called upon to repent. If they repent, well and good; otherwise, they are to be put to death.”

It is narrated that al-Asma‘ī said:

“Jahm’s wife arrived and lodged among the tanners. A man in her presence said: ‘Allah is upon His Throne.’ She replied: ‘One bounded thing upon another.’”

Al-Asma‘ī said: “She disbelieved by making this statement.”

“I debated a Jahmī, and it became clear from his words that he did not believe that there is a Lord in heaven.”

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal al-Shaybānī narrated: Surayj ibn al-Nu‘mān informed us, saying that he heard ‘Abd Allāh ibn Nāfi‘ al-Sā’igh say:

“I heard Mālik ibn Anas say: ‘Allah is in heaven, and His knowledge is everywhere; no place is devoid of His knowledge.’”

Al-Shāfi‘ī said:

“The caliphate of Abū Bakr al-Siddīq is rightful. Allah decreed it in heaven and united the hearts of His servants upon it.”

translated_text:
In the Sahīh (Authentic Collection), Anas ibn Mālik said:

“Zaynab used to boast to the other wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: ‘Your families married you to him, whereas Allah married me to him from above seven heavens.’”

This is akin to al-Shāfi‘ī’s statement. The account of Abū Yūsuf—a disciple of Abū Hanīfah—is well known: when Bishr al-Marīsī denied that Allah is above His Throne, Abū Yūsuf pressed him to repent until Bishr fled from him. Ibn Abī Hātim and others have related this account.

Abū ‘Abd Allāh Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allāh ibn Abī Zamanīn, a renowned imam of the Mālikī school, said in his book Usūl al-Sunnah (The Foundations of the Sunnah), under the heading “Chapter on Belief in the Throne”:

“Among the beliefs of Ahl al-Sunnah (the people of the Sunnah) is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the Throne and distinguished it by its height and elevation above everything He created. Then He rose over it as He willed, as He declared concerning Himself in His words:

‘The Most Merciful rose over the Throne,’

and His words:

‘Then He rose over the Throne. He knows what enters the earth’—and the remainder of the verse.

Glory be to Him who is far, yet near through His knowledge, and thus hears confidential discourse.”

He also cited the hadith of Abū Razīn al-‘Uqaylī:

“I said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, where was our Lord before He created the heavens and the earth?’ He replied:

original_text:
فِي عَمَاءٍ مَا تَحْتَهُ هَوَاءٌ وَمَا فَوْقَهُ هَوَاءٌ ثُمَّ خَلَقَ عَرْشَهُ عَلَى الْمَاءِ} قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ:
 الْعَمَاءُ السَّحَابُ الْكَثِيفُ الْمُطْبِقُ - فِيمَا ذَكَرَهُ الْخَلِيلُ - وَذَكَرَ آثَارًا أُخَرَ.
ثُمَّ قَالَ:

" وَمِنْ قَوْلِ أَهْلِ السُّنَّةِ أَنَّ الْكُرْسِيَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ الْعَرْشِ وَأَنَّهُ مَوْضِعُ الْقَدَمَيْنِ. ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ

 .

 مَا بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا وَاَلَّتِي تَلِيهَا مَسِيرَةُ خَمْسمِائَةِ عَامٍ وَبَيْنَ كُلِّ سَمَاءٍ خَمْسُمِائَةِ عَامٍ وَبَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ السَّابِعَةِ وَالْكُرْسِيِّ خَمْسُمِائَةِ عَامٍ وَبَيْنَ الْكُرْسِيِّ وَالْمَاءِ خَمْسُمِائَةِ عَامٍ وَالْعَرْشُ فَوْقَ الْمَاءِ وَاَللَّهُ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ وَهُوَ يَعْلَمُ مَا أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ.
ثُمَّ قَالَ فِي بَابِ الْإِيمَانِ بِالْحُجُبِ قَالَ:

translated_text:
‘In a cloud, with air beneath it and air above it; then He created His Throne upon the water.’”

Muhammad said: “The word ‘amā’ means a dense, enveloping cloud, according to al-Khalīl.” He also cited other reports.

He then said:

Chapter on Belief in the Kursī

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allāh said: “Among the beliefs of Ahl al-Sunnah is that the Kursī is before the Throne and is the resting place of the two feet.”

He then cited the hadith of Anas concerning the divine manifestation on Fridays in the Hereafter. It includes the words:

“When Friday comes, He descends from ‘Illiyyīn onto His Kursī. Around the Kursī are pulpits of gold crowned with jewels; then the prophets come and sit upon them.”

He also cited what Yahyā ibn Sālim, the author of the well-known Quran commentary, related: “Al-‘Alā’ ibn Hilāl narrated to me from ‘Ammār al-Duhnī, from Sa‘īd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said:

‘The Kursī, which encompasses the heavens and the earth, is indeed the resting place of the two feet. None knows the magnitude of the Throne except the One who created it.’”

He also cited a report transmitted by Asad ibn Mūsā: “Hammād ibn Salamah narrated to us from Zirr, from Ibn Mas‘ūd, who said:

‘Between the lowest heaven and the one above it is a journey of five hundred years, and between each heaven and the next is five hundred years. Between the seventh heaven and the Kursī is five hundred years, and between the Kursī and the water is five hundred years. The Throne is above the water, and Allah is above the Throne, and He knows your circumstances.’”

Then, in the chapter on belief in the veils, he said:

“Among the beliefs of Ahl al-Sunnah is that Allah is separate

from His creation, veiling Himself from them with veils. Exalted is Allah far above what the wrongdoers say!

‘Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak nothing but a lie.’”

He also cited reports concerning the veils.

Then, in the chapter on belief in the descent, he said:

“Among the beliefs of Ahl al-Sunnah is that Allah descends to the lowest heaven. They believe in this without assigning it any limit.”

He cited the hadith through Mālik and others, until he said:

“Wahb informed me, from Ibn Waddāh, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn ‘Abbād, who said: ‘The scholars whom I met—Mālik, Sufyān, Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād, ‘Īsā ibn al-Mubārak, and Wakī‘—used to say: “The descent is real.”’

“Ibn Waddāh said: ‘I asked Yūsuf ibn ‘Adī about the descent. He said: “Yes, I believe in it without assigning it any limit.” I also asked Ibn Ma‘īn about it, and he said: “Yes, I affirm it without assigning it any limit.”’”

Muhammad said:

“This hadith makes clear that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is upon the Throne in heaven, not on earth. This is also clear in Allah’s Book and in numerous hadiths from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Allah Most High says:

‘He directs affairs from heaven to earth; then they ascend to Him.’

“And Allah Most High says:

‘Do you feel secure that He who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, and suddenly it begins to quake?’

‘Or do you feel secure that He who is in heaven will not send against you a storm of stones?’

“And Allah Most High says:

‘To Him ascends good speech, and righteous deeds raise it.’

“And He says:

‘He is the Subduer, above His servants.’

“And Allah Most High says:

‘O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Myself.’

“And He says:

‘Rather, Allah raised him to Himself.’”

He also cited, through Mālik, the Prophet’s words to the slave girl, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Where is Allah?

” She replied, “In heaven.” He asked, “Who am I?” She replied, “You are the Messenger of Allah.” He said, “Then set her free.”

He said: “Hadiths like this are very numerous. Glory be to Him whose knowledge of what is in heaven is like His knowledge of what is on earth! There is no god but Him, the Most High, the Magnificent.”

Earlier, in the section entitled “Belief in the Attributes and Names of Allah Most High,” he said:

“Know that those who have knowledge of Allah and of what His prophets and messengers brought regard ignorance of what He has not disclosed about Himself as knowledge, and inability regarding what He has not called them to as faith. In describing Him by His attributes and names, they go no further than what He has stated in His Book through His Prophet. He has said—and He is the most truthful of speakers:

‘Everything will perish except His Face.’

“And He said:

‘Say, “What thing is greatest in testimony?” Say, “Allah is witness between me and you.”’

“And He said:

‘Allah warns you of Himself.’

“And He said:

‘When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit.’

“And He said:

‘For you are under Our eyes.’

“And He said:

‘So that you may be brought up under My eye.’

“And He said:

‘The Jews say, “Allah’s hand is tied.” May their hands be tied, and may they be cursed for what they have said! Rather, both His hands are outstretched.’

“And He said:

‘The entire earth will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection’—to the end of the verse.

“And He said:

‘Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.’

“And He said:

‘Allah spoke directly to Moses.’

“And Allah Most High said:

‘Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth’—to the end of the verse.

“And He said:

‘Allah—there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence’—to the end of the verse.

“And He said:

‘He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden.’

“There are many passages like this in the Quran.

فَهُوَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى نُورُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كَمَا أَخْبَرَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَلَهُ وَجْهٌ وَنَفْسٌ وَغَيْرُ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا وَصَفَ بِهِ نَفْسَهُ وَيَسْمَعُ وَيَرَى وَيَتَكَلَّمُ هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ لَا شَيْءَ قَبْلَهُ وَالْآخِرُ الْبَاقِي إلَى غَيْرِ نِهَايَةٍ وَلَا شَيْءَ بَعْدَهُ وَالظَّاهِرُ الْعَالِي فَوْقَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَالْبَاطِنُ بَطَنَ عِلْمُهُ بِخَلْقِهِ فَقَالَ:
 
{وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ}
 قَيُّومُ حَيٌّ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ.
 وَذَكَرَ:
 
" أَحَادِيثَ الصِّفَاتِ "
 ثُمَّ قَالَ: فَهَذِهِ صِفَاتُ رَبِّنَا الَّتِي وَصَفَ بِهَا نَفْسَهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَوَصَفَهُ بِهَا نَبِيُّهُ وَلَيْسَ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنْهَا تَحْدِيدٌ وَلَا تَشْبِيهٌ وَلَا تَقْدِيرٌ 
{لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ}
 لَمْ تَرَهُ الْعُيُونُ فَتَحُدُّهُ كَيْفَ هُوَ؟ وَلَكِنْ رَأَتْهُ الْقُلُوبُ فِي حَقَائِقِ الْإِيمَانِ اهـ.
وَكَلَامُ الْأَئِمَّةِ فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ أَطْوَلُ وَأَكْثَرُ مِنْ أَنْ تَسَعَ هَذِهِ الْفُتْيَا عُشْرَهُ. وَكَذَلِكَ كَلَامُ النَّاقِلِينَ لِمَذْهَبِهِمْ. مِثْلُ مَا ذَكَرَهُ أَبُو سُلَيْمَانَ الخطابي فِي رِسَالَتِهِ الْمَشْهُورَةِ فِي 
" الغنية عَنْ الْكَلَامِ وَأَهْلِهِ "
 قَالَ: " فَأَمَّا مَا سَأَلْت عَنْهُ مِنْ الصِّفَاتِ وَمَا جَاءَ مِنْهَا فِي الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ فَإِنَّ مَذْهَبَ السَّلَفِ إثْبَاتُهَا وَإِجْرَاؤُهَا عَلَى ظَوَاهِرِهَا وَنَفْيُ الْكَيْفِيَّةِ وَالتَّشْبِيهِ عَنْهَا وَقَدْ نَفَاهَا قَوْمٌ فَأَبْطَلُوا مَا أَثْبَتَهُ اللَّهُ وَحَقَّقَهَا قَوْمٌ مِنْ الْمُثْبِتِينَ فَخَرَجُوا فِي ذَلِكَ إلَى ضَرْبٍ مِنْ التَّشْبِيهِ وَالتَّكْيِيفِ وَإِنَّمَا الْقَصْدُ فِي سُلُوكِ الطَّرِيقَةِ الْمُسْتَقِيمَةِ بَيْنَ الْأَمْرَيْنِ وَدِينُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى بَيْنَ الْغَالِي فِيهِ وَالْجَافِي وَالْمُقَصِّرِ عَنْهُ.
translated_text:
So He, blessed and exalted, is the Light of the heavens and the earth, as He has said of Himself. He has a Face, a Self, and the other attributes with which He has described Himself. He hears, sees, and speaks. He is the First, with nothing before Him; the Last, who remains without end, with nothing after Him; the Manifest, exalted above everything; and the Hidden, whose knowledge encompasses the innermost realities of His creation. Thus He said:

‘And He has knowledge of all things.’

“He is the Sustainer of all existence, the Ever-Living; neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.”

He cited “hadiths concerning the divine attributes,” then said:

“These are the attributes of our Lord with which He has described Himself in His Book and with which His Prophet has described Him. None of them imposes limits on Him, likens Him to anything, or assigns Him a measure.

‘There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.’

“Eyes have not seen Him so as to define what He is like; rather, hearts have seen Him through the realities of faith.” End of quotation.

The statements of the imams on this subject are far too extensive and numerous for this fatwa to contain even a tenth of them. The same applies to the statements of those who transmit their teachings. An example is what Abū Sulaymān al-Khattābī mentioned in his well-known epistle, Dispensing with Speculative Theology and Its Practitioners. He said:

“As for your question concerning the attributes and what has been reported about them in the Book and the Sunnah, the way of the early generations is to affirm them, accept them according to their apparent meanings, and reject specifying how they are or likening them to anything. Some people have denied them, thereby nullifying what Allah has affirmed. Others among those who affirm them have asserted their reality, but in doing so have fallen into a form of likening them to created things and specifying how they are. The aim is simply to follow the straight path between these two extremes. The religion of Allah Most High stands between those who go to excess in it and those who turn away from it or fall short of it.

وَالْأَصْلُ فِي هَذَا:

" هَذَا كُلُّهُ كَلَامُ الخطابي.

" وَ "
 ذَمِّ الْكَلَامِ " وَهُوَ أَشْهَرُ مِنْ أَنْ يُوصَفَ وَشَيْخِ الْإِسْلَامِ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ الصَّابُونِيِّ وَأَبِي عُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْبَرِّ النمري إمَامِ الْمَغْرِبِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ.
translated_text:
And the underlying principle here is that discussion of the attributes follows from discussion of the divine Essence and is governed by the same principles. Since it is understood that affirming the Creator—glory be to Him—means affirming His existence, not specifying how He is, likewise affirming His attributes means affirming their existence, not defining their limits or specifying how they are. When we speak of a Hand, hearing, sight, and similar attributes, these are simply attributes that Allah has affirmed for Himself.

We do not say that the Hand means strength or bounty, or that hearing and sight mean knowledge. Nor do we say that these attributes are bodily parts, or liken them to hands and organs of hearing and sight that are bodily parts and instruments of action. Rather, we say that affirming the attributes is obligatory because revelation has attested to them, and that rejecting any likeness to created things is obligatory because there is nothing like Allah. This is the approach the early generations followed regarding the hadiths concerning the divine attributes.”

All of this is al-Khattābī’s statement.

The hadith master Abū Bakr al-Khatīb likewise stated this in an epistle in which he explained that this was the position of the early generations. Statements similar to what al-Khattābī mentioned have been transmitted by countless scholars, including Abū Bakr al-Ismāʿīlī; Imam Yahyā ibn ʿAmmār al-Sijzī; Shaykh al-Islām Abū Ismāʿīl al-Harawī, the author of “Stations of the Wayfarers” and “Condemnation of Speculative Theology,” whose renown needs no elaboration; Shaykh al-Islām Abū ʿUthmān al-Sābūnī; Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr al-Namarī, the imam of the Maghreb; and others.

Abū Nu'aym al-Asbahānī, author of al-Hilya (The Adornment), said at the beginning of a creed he wrote:

“Our way is that of those who follow the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the Muslim community.” He continued: “Among their beliefs is that they accept and affirm the hadiths authentically transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concerning the Throne and Allah’s establishment over it, without specifying how, positing an equivalent, or likening Him to creation. Allah is distinct from His creation, and creation is distinct from Him: He neither dwells within them nor mingles with them. He is established over His Throne, in His heaven, not in His earth or His creation.”

The hadith master Abū Nu'aym also said in his own work, Mahajjat al-Wāthiqīn wa-Madrajat al-Wāmiqīn (The Path of the Confident and the Ascent of the Loving):

“They unanimously agreed that Allah is above His heavens, high above His Throne, established over it—not ‘having gained mastery over it,’ as the Jahmiyyah say, asserting that He is everywhere, contrary to what He revealed in His Book:

‘Do you feel secure from Him who is above heaven?’

‘To Him ascends good speech.’

‘The Most Merciful is established over the Throne.’

To Him belongs the Throne over which He is established, and the Kursī, which encompasses the heavens and the earth. This is His statement:

‘His Kursī encompasses the heavens and the earth.’

His Kursī is a physical body. The seven earths and the seven heavens, compared with the Kursī, are like a ring in an open desert. His Kursī is not His knowledge, as the Jahmiyyah have claimed. Rather, His Kursī will be set in place on the Day of Resurrection for judgment to be rendered between His creatures, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said. He—exalted and holy is He—will come on the Day of Resurrection to render judgment between His servants, with the angels in rows, as He, Most High, said:

‘And your Lord comes, with the angels in rows.’

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, further stated that He—exalted and holy is He—will come on the Day of Resurrection to render judgment between His servants, and will forgive whomever He wills among

‘He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.’”

The imam renowned for his knowledge of Allah, Ma‘mar ibn Ahmad al-Asbahānī—the leading Sufi in his region around the fourth century AH—said:

“I wished to offer my companions counsel drawn from the Sunnah and an admonition drawn from wisdom, and to bring together the beliefs held by the adherents of hadith and transmitted reports, without specifying how, and by those versed in knowledge of Allah and Sufism, both earlier and later generations.”

In this counsel he said:

“Allah is established over His Throne without specifying how, likening Him to creation, or reinterpreting His establishment. Its meaning is intelligible, but its manner is unknown. He, Almighty and Majestic, is established over His Throne, distinct from His creation, and creation is distinct from Him, without indwelling, mingling, intermixture, or contact. For He is unique, distinct from creation, the One who has no need of creation.

“Allah, Almighty and Majestic, is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, All-Knowing, All-Aware. He speaks, is pleased, is displeased, laughs, marvels, and manifests Himself to His servants on the Day of Resurrection, laughing. Every night He descends to the lowest heaven however He wills:

‘Then He says: “Is there anyone calling upon Me, that I may answer him? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness, that I may forgive him? Is there anyone repenting, that I may accept his repentance?”—until dawn breaks.’

“The Lord’s descent to heaven is affirmed without specifying how, likening Him to creation, or reinterpreting it. Whoever denies the descent or reinterprets it is a misguided innovator. The rest of the elect among those who know Allah hold this belief.” End of quotation.

The shaykh and imam Abū Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hārūn al-Khallāl said in The Book of the Sunnah:

" الْفَارُوقِ "

" التَّعَرُّفُ بِأَحْوَالِ الْعِبَادِ والمتعبدين "
 قَالَ: (بَابُ مَا يَجِيءُ بِهِ الشَّيْطَانُ لِلتَّائِبِينَ وَذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ يُوقِعُهُمْ فِي الْقُنُوطِ ثُمَّ فِي الْغُرُورِ وَطُولِ الْأَمَلِ ثُمَّ فِي التَّوْحِيدِ.
 فَقَالَ:
 
" مِنْ أَعْظَمِ مَا يُوَسْوِسُ فِي "
 التَّوْحِيدِ " بِالتَّشَكُّلِ أَوْ فِي صِفَاتِ الرَّبِّ بِالتَّمْثِيلِ وَالتَّشْبِيهِ أَوْ بِالْجَحْدِ لَهَا وَالتَّعْطِيلِ.
 فَقَالَ بَعْدَ ذِكْرِ حَدِيثِ الْوَسْوَسَةِ:
translated_text:
ibn Yahyā, who said: I heard Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ash‘ath—Abū Bakr said that he was al-Fudayl’s companion—say: I heard al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād say:

‘We have no right to imagine what Allah is like, for Allah, Most High, has described Himself in the most eloquent terms, saying:

“Say: He is Allah, the One;
Allah, the Eternal Refuge.
He neither begets nor is born,
nor is there anyone equal to Him.”

‘No description is more eloquent than that with which He has described Himself. All this descending, laughing, taking pride, and observing is as He wills: He descends as He wills, takes pride as He wills, laughs as He wills, and observes as He wills. It is not for us to speculate about how any of this occurs.

‘If a Jahmī says, “I disbelieve in a Lord who moves from His place,” say, “Rather, I believe in a Lord who does whatever He wills.”’”

A number of scholars transmitted this from al-Fudayl, including al-Bukhārī in The Acts of the Servants. Shaykh al-Islām also transmitted it with his chain of narration in his book al-Fārūq, saying: Yahyā ibn ‘Ammār narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Yūsuf ibn Ya‘qūb narrated to us: Harmī ibn ‘Alī al-Bukhārī and Hāni’ ibn al-Nadr narrated to us from al-Fudayl.

‘Amr ibn ‘Uthmān al-Makkī said in his book, which he entitled Understanding the States of Worshippers and Devotees: “Chapter on What Satan Brings to Those Who Repent.” He mentioned that Satan leads them into despair, then into delusion and hopes of a long life, and then attacks their belief in divine oneness. He said:

“Among his gravest insinuations concerning divine oneness is imagining a form; or, concerning the Lord’s attributes, equating or likening them to those of creation, or denying and nullifying them.”

After mentioning the hadith concerning satanic insinuations, he said:

translated_text:
“And know—may Allah have mercy on you—that whatever your heart imagines, whatever arises in the course of your thoughts, or whatever passes through your heart—whether beauty, splendour, light, radiance, loveliness, questions that arise, or an imagined figure—Allah Most High is other than all of that. Rather, He is greater, more majestic, and more exalted. Do you not hear His words:

‘There is nothing like unto Him,’

and His words:

‘Nor is there anyone equal to Him’?

“That is, He has no likeness, counterpart, equal, or peer. Do you not know that when He manifested Himself to the mountain, it crumbled beneath His overwhelming majesty and supreme sovereignty? Just as nothing to which He manifests Himself remains unshattered, so no one imagines what He is like without perishing. Thus, what Allah Himself has explained about Himself in His Book refutes any likeness, peer, counterpart, or equal.

“If you hold fast to these truths and protect yourself from Satan, he will approach you by urging you to deny the attributes of the Lord—exalted and holy is He—mentioned in His Book and the sunnah of His Messenger Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He will say to you: ‘If He is described as such-and-such, or you describe Him thus, that necessarily likens Him to creation.’ I declare him a liar, for the accursed one seeks only to make you stumble, lead you astray, and cause you to adopt the characteristics of those who deviate from the truth, stray, and deny the attributes of the Lord Most High.

“And know—may Allah Most High have mercy on you—that Allah Most High is One, unlike any other one: unique, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there anyone equal to Him.”

He went on to say:

“His sublime names belong exclusively to Him and have applied to Him from eternity, expressing true realities. He Most High did not acquire an attribute that He had previously lacked, or a name that had not previously been His—blessed and exalted is He. Thus, He was the Guide who would guide, the Creator who would create, the Provider who would provide, the Forgiver who would forgive, and the Doer who would act. Nor did there newly arise for Him

translated_text:
the act of rising above, without His already being described as One who would perform that act; thus He is designated by it among His acts. Likewise, Allah Most High says:

‘And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank.’

This means that He will come. He did not acquire the name upon coming; rather, the act was deferred until the time of His coming. Thus He has come and will come, and His coming will actually occur without modality or likeness attaching to it, for this is an act of Lordship. The mind grows weary and the soul falters when one seeks to determine how the One worshipped is. Therefore, do not incline towards either extreme: neither deny His attributes nor liken Him to creation. Accept for Allah what He has accepted for Himself, and stop at what He has revealed about Himself, accepting, submitting, and believing, without debates that provoke aversion or comparisons that invite probing.”

He went on to say:

“He—blessed and exalted is He—is the One who says, ‘I am Allah,’ not the tree; the One who comes even before He comes—not His command; the One who manifests Himself to His close servants in the Hereafter, so that through Him their faces become radiant and their argument prevails against the deniers; the One who has risen above His Throne in the greatness of His majesty, above every place—blessed and exalted is He; the One who spoke directly to Moses and showed him some of His signs. Moses thus heard Allah’s speech, for He brought him near for intimate converse.

“He is too holy for His speech to be created, newly originated, or subject to a lord. He is the Inheritor, through His creation, of His creatures; the One who hears their voices and looks with His eye upon their bodies. His two hands are outstretched, and they are not His favour. He created Adam and breathed into him of His spirit—which is His command. Exalted and holy is He, above dwelling within a body, mingling with a body, or being in contact with it. Far exalted is He above that.

Imam Abū ‘Abd Allāh al-Hārith ibn Ismā‘īl ibn Asad al-Muhāsibī said in his book Fahm al-Qur’ān (Understanding the Quran), while discussing the abrogating and the abrogated, and explaining that abrogation cannot apply to statements of fact:

“It is not lawful for anyone to believe that any praise of Allah, or any of His attributes or names, may be abrogated.”

Later he said:

“Likewise, if He has declared that His attributes are good and exalted, He cannot then declare that they are base and lowly, describing Himself as ignorant of some of the unseen after having declared that He knows the unseen; or declaring that He does not see what has occurred, does not hear voices, has no power, does not speak and has never spoken, or that He is beneath the earth rather than above the Throne. “and the following verses, and His words:

 كَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ:

 فَأَقَرَّ التِّلَاوَةَ عَلَى اسْتِئْنَافِ الْعِلْمِ مِنْ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَنْ أَنْ يَسْتَأْنِفَ عِلْمًا بِشَيْءِ لِأَنَّهُ مَنْ لَيْسَ لَهُ عِلْمٌ بِمَا يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَصْنَعَهُ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ أَنْ يَصْنَعَهُ - نَجِدُهُ ضَرُورَةً -

{أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ}
 قَالَ: وَإِنَّمَا قَوْلُهُ

{إنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُسْتَمِعُونَ}

translated_text:
and he said:

Some people have interpreted this to mean that Allah intended to save Pharaoh bodily from the Fire because he believed when he was drowning. They said that Allah mentioned only Pharaoh’s people entering the Fire, not Pharaoh himself. He said:

‘And he will lead them into the Fire.’

And He said:

‘And the people of Pharaoh were enveloped by the worst punishment.’

He did not say ‘Pharaoh.’

He said: Such is the fabrication of lies against Allah, for Allah Most High says:

‘So Allah seized him with an exemplary punishment in the Hereafter and in this world.’

Likewise, His words:

‘Allah will surely know those who are truthful.’

The recited wording was thus taken to imply newly acquired knowledge in Allah—far exalted is He above acquiring knowledge of anything anew. For whoever has no knowledge of what he intends to make cannot make it; we know this necessarily. He said:

‘Does He who created not know, while He is the Most Subtle, the All-Aware?’

He said: His words, ‘Until We know those who strive,’ mean only: until We see it, so that it is known as something existing. For it is not possible that He should know a thing as nonexistent before it comes into being, yet also know it as already existing. He would then know it at one and the same time as both nonexistent and existent, even though it had not come into being. This is impossible.”

He also discussed this matter in relation to the will.

Later he said:

“Likewise, His words:

‘Indeed, We are with you, listening.’

“This does not mean that hearing newly arises in Him, or that hearing what they say requires any effort. Some among the ‘people of the Sunnah’ held that Allah has an act of listening within His essence. They understood this in terms of what they knew of themselves: that hearing what has been said gives rise to knowledge in them. For when a created being hears, an understanding arises in him through which he comprehends the sound his ear has perceived.

“Likewise, His words:

‘And say, “Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger.”’

“He does not acquire a newly originated faculty of sight within His essence. Rather, the thing comes into being, and He sees it as existing, just as He has always known it before it came into being.”

He went on to say:

“Likewise, His words, Most High:

‘And He is the Subduer, above His servants.’

And His words:

‘The Most Merciful rose over the Throne.’

And His words:

‘Do you feel secure from Him who is in heaven?’

And His words:

‘To Him ascends good speech, and righteous deeds raise it.’

He also said:

‘He directs the affairs from heaven to earth; then they ascend to Him.’

And He said:

‘The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him.’

He said to Jesus:

‘Indeed, I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve’—the verse.

And He said:

‘Rather, Allah raised him to Himself.’

And He said:

‘Indeed, those who are with your Lord are not too proud to worship Him.’

He also mentioned the gods: if there were gods, they would seek a way to the Lord of the Throne, where He is. He said:

‘Say: If there were gods alongside Him, as they claim, they would surely seek a way to the Lord of the Throne.’

That is, they would seek Him. And He said:

‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.’

Abū ‘Abd Allāh said: That will never be abrogated by this. Likewise, His words:

‘He is the One who is God in heaven and God on earth.’

And His words:

‘We are closer to him than his jugular vein.’

And His words:

‘He is Allah in the heavens and on earth; He knows what you conceal and what you reveal.’

And His words:

‘There is no private conversation among three but that He is their fourth’—the verse.

These do not abrogate those, nor do they contradict them. Know that these verses do not mean that Allah intended His presence in His very essence, such that He would be in the lowest of things, move within them as they move, be divided among them according to their dimensions, or depart from them when they perish. Glorified and exalted is He above that. Yet some misguided people have invoked these verses, claiming that Allah

Most High, is Himself present in every place just as He is upon the Throne, with no distinction between the two. Their subsequent denial was incoherent, since their own statements had already allowed the very things they denied to apply to Him. For whoever affirms something in substance and then denies it verbally gains nothing from his verbal denial. They cited these verses as evidence that Allah Most High is Himself present in everything, then denied the implications of what they had affirmed, saying: ‘Not as one thing is within another.’

Abū ‘Abd Allāh said to us: “His words:

‘Until We know,’

‘Then Allah will see,’

and ‘Indeed, We are with you, listening,’

mean only that the thing comes into existence, whereupon He knows it as existent, hears it as something heard, and sees it as something seen—not that any new knowledge, hearing, or sight arises.

As for His words, ‘And when We intend,’ this means when the time comes for what is intended to occur.

His words:

‘He rose over the Throne,’

‘And He is the Subduer, above His servants’—the verse—

‘Do you feel secure from Him who is in heaven?’

and ‘They would surely seek a way to the Lord of the Throne,’

along with other statements such as:

‘The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him,’

and ‘To Him ascends good speech,’

are self-contained statements establishing that He is above the Throne, above all things, and far exalted above entering into His creation. Nothing about them is hidden from Him. In these verses, He made it clear that He meant that He Himself is above His servants, for He said:

‘Do you feel secure from Him who is in heaven, that He will not cause the earth to swallow you?’

This means above the Throne, and the Throne is above heaven. For one who is above everything, over heaven, is spoken of as being ‘in heaven.’ He used a similar expression in His words:

‘Travel freely through the land,’

meaning on the earth; He does not mean entering its interior. Likewise, His words:

‘They will wander through the land,’

mean on the earth; He does not mean entering its interior. Likewise, His words:

‘I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees,’

mean over them, upon them.

And He said:

‘Do you feel secure from Him who is in heaven?’

Then He made a distinction, saying:

‘That He will not cause the earth to swallow you,’

without joining the two statements. Thus, when He sets apart His words ‘Him who is in heaven’ and then begins the threat of the earth swallowing them, this can mean only that He is upon His Throne, above heaven.

The Most High said:

‘He directs the affairs from heaven to earth; then they ascend to Him.’

And He said:

‘The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him.’

He thus made clear the ascent of the affairs and the ascent of the angels. He then described the time of their upward ascent to Him, saying:

‘In a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years.’

He thus spoke of their ascent to Him. The separation after His words ‘to Him’ is like someone saying, ‘I ascend to so-and-so in a night or a day.’ This means that the person is on high, and that your ascent to him takes a day. Thus, when they ascend to the Throne, they have ascended to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, even though they have neither seen Him nor risen as high as He is. They have ascended from the earth and carried the affairs upward.

The Most High said:

‘Rather, Allah raised him to Himself.’

He did not say, ‘into His presence.’

Pharaoh said:

‘O Hāmān, build me a tower so that I may reach the pathways—the pathways of the heavens—and look upon the God of Moses.’

Then he began a new statement, saying:

‘Indeed, I think he is a liar,’

in telling me that his God is above the heavens.

Allah, Glorified and Most High, thus made clear that Pharaoh thought Moses was lying in what he said. Yet Pharaoh set out to seek Him where Moses had said He was, despite thinking that Moses was lying. Had Moses said that He Himself was in every place, Pharaoh would have sought Him in his house, in his body, or in his privy—far exalted is Allah above that! And Pharaoh would not have troubled himself with building the tower.

translated_text:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh said:

As for the verses which they claim He joined together—without separating them as He separated the statement in which He meant that He is upon His Throne—He said:

“Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth?”

He spoke of His knowledge, then stated that He is with everyone engaged in a private conversation, and then concluded the verse by speaking of His knowledge:

“Indeed, Allah knows all things.”

Thus He began with knowledge and ended with knowledge, making clear that He meant that He knows them wherever they are. They are not hidden from Him, nor are their private conversations hidden from Him. If a group gathered below, and someone looking down at them from above said, “I have been watching you all along and know your private conversations,” he would be speaking truthfully—yet to Allah belongs the highest description; He is far above resembling His creation.

If they insist on nothing but the apparent meaning of the wording and say, “This is merely an assertion on your part,” they depart from their own position concerning that apparent meaning. For whoever is with two or more people is with them, not within them; and whoever is with something is bodily separate from it. This contradicts their position.

The same applies to His words, Most High:

“And We are closer to him than his jugular vein.”

For whatever is close to something is not within it. Thus, on their own claim to follow the apparent meaning of the wording, He is not within the jugular vein.

The same applies to His words:

“And it is He who is God in heaven and God on earth.”

He did not say “in heaven” and then separate what follows—as He said:

“Do you feel secure from Him who is in heaven?”

Then He separated what follows, saying:

“That He will not cause the earth to swallow you.”

Rather, He said:

“And it is He who is God in heaven,”

meaning the God of the inhabitants of heaven and the God of the inhabitants of earth. This usage is found in “the language.” You say, “So-and-so is a ruler in Khurāsān, a ruler in Balkh, and a ruler in Samarkand,” although he is in only one place, and what lies beyond him is hidden from him. What, then, of the One who is above all things, from whom nothing that He governs is hidden? He is therefore God in both

Imam Abū ‘Abd Allāh Muhammad ibn Khafīf said in his book entitled Belief in Divine Oneness through Affirming the Names and Attributes, at the end of his introduction:

“The statements of the Emigrants and the Helpers concerning the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and knowledge of His names, attributes, and decree were unanimous and constituted a clear religious teaching. They were the ones who transmitted this from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, including his words: ‘You must adhere to my Sunnah.’”

He cited the hadith, as well as the hadith, “Allah curses whoever introduces wrongdoing.” He said:

“The Companions were unanimously agreed, without disagreement—and they are those from whom we have been commanded to learn. Praise be to Allah Most High, they did not disagree concerning the teachings of divine oneness and the fundamentals of religion, including ‘the names and attributes,’ as they disagreed over subsidiary matters. Had they disagreed about these matters, that disagreement would have been transmitted to us, just as their other disagreements were transmitted. Thus, the soundness of this was firmly established among their leading figures and ordinary members alike, until they conveyed it to those who followed them in righteousness. Its soundness was then firmly established among the recognized scholars, who transmitted it generation after generation, for they regarded disagreement concerning the foundation of religion as disbelief. All favour belongs to Allah.

“I further say—and I say this with Allah’s help—that when people began disagreeing concerning the teachings of divine oneness and the discussion of the names and attributes, contrary to the way of the earlier Companions and Successors, people who were not known for knowledge of transmitted traditions plunged into these matters. They did not understand the statements of their predecessors in light of the transmitted reports. Their reliance came to rest on judgments dictated by self-pleasing desires, derived from thinking ill of Him, in opposition to the Sunnah, and on clinging to verses in which they found no support for what pleased their souls, so they interpreted them to suit their desires

and thereby justified their doctrine, I found it necessary to explain the way of the early generations, the sources from which the believers drew, and the path of the earliest Muslims, lest I fall into any of those views against which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, warned his community and which he forbade his followers to adopt, cautioning them against them.”

Abū ‘Abd Allāh then mentioned how the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out while they were disputing about divine decree, and how angry he became. He also cited the hadith, “Let me not find any of you,” and the hadith, “My community will split into seventy-three sects,” explaining that the saved group follows the way that he and his Companions followed.

He then said:

“The entire community is therefore obliged to know the way of the Companions. This knowledge can be reached only through those who followed them in righteousness, who were known for transmitting reports and did not accept newly introduced doctrines. This transmission thus continues, generation after generation, through those known for uprightness and trustworthiness, who preserve for the community its rights and obligations in upholding the Sunnah.”

He went on to say:

“The first thing we shall address is the very reason we raised this question: the mention of ‘the names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,’ in His Book; what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained of ‘His attributes’ in his Sunnah; and the descriptions given of Him, Mighty and Majestic. We shall cite the statements of those who affirm these matters. We may not subject them to the judgments of our own minds by seeking to determine their modality; rather, they are among the matters we have been commanded to accept submissively.”

He went on to say:

“Then Allah made Himself known to us, after His oneness had been established and His sole right to worship acknowledged, through what He, Most High, mentioned in His Book, after confirming the names and attributes with which He began; and he, peace be upon him, reinforced this with his words

so they accepted it from him just as they accepted the first principles of divine oneness from the plain meaning of his words, ‘There is no god but Allah.’”

He went on to discuss the affirmation of His Self, moving from the general to the particular:

“He said to Moses, peace be upon him:

‘I have chosen you for Myself.’

And He said:

‘Allah warns you of Himself.’

The truth of this is further confirmed by what the Messiah, peace be upon him, brought, for he said:

‘You know what is within myself, whereas I do not know what is within Yourself.’

And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:

‘Your Lord has prescribed mercy for Himself.’

He, peace be upon him, further confirmed the validity of affirming this in his Sunnah, saying:

‘Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself.”’

And he said:

‘He wrote with His Hand a decree binding upon Himself: “My mercy has prevailed over My wrath.”’

And he said:

‘Glory be to Allah, to the measure of His own good pleasure.’

And, concerning Adam’s debate with Moses, he said:

‘You are the one whom Allah chose and selected for Himself.’

Thus, through the plain meaning of His words, He explicitly affirmed a Self for Himself, and the Messenger affirmed this for Him. Whoever believes Allah and His Messenger must therefore believe what He has stated about Himself, basing this upon the plain meaning of His words:

‘There is nothing like Him.’”

He then said:

“All believers, elite and ordinary alike, must accept everything reported from him, peace be upon him, through transmission from one upright narrator to another in a chain reaching him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Among the things Allah has enjoined upon us in His Book, with which He has described Himself and whose truth the Sunnah confirms, is His statement:

‘Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.’

Then, immediately thereafter, He said:

‘Light upon light.’

And he invoked Him by this description

 أَنَّ الْكُرْسِيَّ مَوْضِعُ الْقَدَمَيْنِ وَأَنَّ الْعَرْشَ لَا يُقَدِّرُ قَدْرَهُ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَذَكَرَ قَوْلَ مُسْلِمٍ الْبَطِينِ نَفْسِهِ وَقَوْلَ السدي وَقَوْلَ وَهْبِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ وَأَبِي مَالِكٍ وَبَعْضُهُمْ يَقُولُ: مَوْضِعُ قَدَمَيْهِ وَبَعْضُهُمْ يَقُولُ وَاضِعَ رِجْلَيْهِ عَلَيْهِ.
 ثُمَّ قَالَ:
 
" فَهَذِهِ الرِّوَايَاتُ قَدْ رُوِيَتْ عَنْ هَؤُلَاءِ مِنْ صَدْرِ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ مُوَافَقَةً لِقَوْلِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مُتَدَاوَلَةً فِي الْأَقْوَالِ وَمَحْفُوظَةً فِي الصَّدْرِ وَلَا يُنْكِرُ خَلَفٌ عَنْ السَّلَفِ وَلَا يُنْكِرُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَحَدٌ مِنْ نُظَرَائِهِمْ نَقَلَتْهَا الْخَاصَّةُ وَالْعَامَّةُ مُدَوَّنَةٌ فِي كُتُبِهِمْ إلَى أَنْ حَدَثَ فِي آخِرِ الْأُمَّةِ مَنْ قَلَّلَ اللَّهُ عَدَدَهُمْ مِمَّنْ حَذَّرَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنْ مُجَالَسَتِهِمْ وَمُكَالَمَتِهِمْ وَأُمِرْنَا أَنْ لَا نَعُودَ مَرْضَاهُمْ وَلَا نُشَيِّعَ جَنَائِزَهُمْ فَقَصَدَ هَؤُلَاءِ إلَى هَذِهِ الرِّوَايَاتِ فَضَرَبُوهَا بِالتَّشْبِيهِ وَعَمَدُوا إلَى الْأَخْبَارِ فَعَمِلُوا فِي دَفْعِهَا إلَى أَحْكَامِ الْمَقَايِيسِ وَكُفْرِ الْمُتَقَدِّمِينَ وَأَنْكَرُوا عَلَى الصَّحَابَةِ وَالتَّابِعِينَ؛ وَرَدُّوا عَلَى الْأَئِمَّةِ الرَّاشِدِينَ فَضَّلُوا وَأَضَلُّوا عَنْ سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ.
 ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ:
 الْمَأْثُورَ عَنْ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَجَوَابَهُ لنجدة الحروري؛ ثُمَّ حَدِيثَ "
 الصُّورَةِ " وَذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ صَنَّفَ فِيهِ كِتَابًا مُفْرَدًا وَاخْتِلَافَ النَّاسِ فِي تَأْوِيلِهِ.
translated_text:
He then cited the hadith:

“People are cast into the Fire, and it says, ‘Are there any more?’ until He places His Leg in it.”

This is al-Bukhārī’s narration. Another narration reads: “He places His Foot upon it.”

He then cited what Muslim al-Batīn narrated from Ibn ‘Abbās: that the Kursī (Seat) is the resting place of the two Feet, and that none but Allah can fathom the magnitude of the Throne. He also cited the statements of Muslim al-Batīn himself, al-Suddī, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and Abū Mālik. Some of them say, “The resting place of His two Feet,” while others say, “He places His two Legs upon it.”

He then said:

“These narrations have been transmitted from these figures of the earliest generations of this community, in agreement with the words of the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They have circulated in speech and been preserved in memory. No succeeding generation denied what it received from its predecessors, nor did any of their contemporaries object to them. Scholars and ordinary people alike transmitted these narrations, which were recorded in their books, until people arose in the later generations of this community—may Allah diminish their numbers—from among those whom the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—warned us against sitting with and speaking to. We were commanded not to visit their sick or accompany their funeral processions. These people targeted these narrations, branding them as likening Allah to His creation. They turned to the transmitted reports and sought to subject them to the judgments of analogical reasoning, charging the earlier generations with unbelief. They objected to the Companions and their Successors and rejected the rightly guided imams. Thus they went astray and led others away from the straight path.”

He then cited the report transmitted from Ibn ‘Abbās and his reply to Najda al-Harūrī, followed by the hadith concerning the “Image.” He mentioned that he had written a separate book on it and discussed people’s differing interpretations of it.

 الصِّدِّيقِ 
" وَأَنَّهُ أَفْضَلُ الْأُمَّةِ.

 الْكَبَائِرِ

 الْأَسْمَاءِ وَالْأَحْكَامِ

 قَوْلُنَا وَقَوْلُ أَئِمَّتِنَا فِيمَا نَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُرَى فِي الْقِيَامَةِ وَذَكَرَ الْحُجَّةَ.
 ثُمَّ قَالَ:
 اعْلَمْ رَحِمَك اللَّهُ أَنِّي ذَكَرْت أَحْكَامَ الِاخْتِلَافِ عَلَى مَا وَرَدَ مِنْ تَرْتِيبِ الْمُحَدِّثِينَ فِي كُلِّ الْأَزْمِنَةِ وَقَدْ بَدَأْت أَنْ أَذْكُرَ أَحْكَامَ الْجُمَلِ مِنْ الْعُقُودِ.
 فَنَقُولُ:
 وَنَعْتَقِدُ: أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لَهُ عَرْشٌ وَهُوَ عَلَى عَرْشِهِ فَوْقَ سَبْعِ سَمَوَاتِهِ
translated_text:
He then said:

“We shall mention the foundations of the sunnah and the disagreements reported concerning our beliefs: the matters in which we differ from those who deviate from the truth and those in which we agree with the scholars of hadith who affirm the divine attributes—if Allah wills.”

He then discussed the disagreement concerning leadership of the Muslim community and presented arguments on the matter. He mentioned the agreement of the Emigrants and Helpers on giving precedence to al-Siddīq and that he is the best of this community.

He then said:

“There was also disagreement concerning ‘the creation of deeds’: are they decreed or not?”

He said:

“Our position is that the deeds of Allah’s servants are decreed and known to Him.”

He discussed the affirmation of divine decree. He then mentioned the disagreement concerning those who commit “major sins” and the question of “religious designations and rulings,” saying:

“Our position is that they are believers without qualification. Their case rests with Allah: if He wills, He punishes them, and if He wills, He pardons them.”

He also said:

“The foundation of ‘faith’ is a gift from which the deeds of Allah’s servants arise. It is thus the foundation of belief, affirmation, and deeds.”

He mentioned the disagreement concerning the increase and decrease of faith, saying:

“Our position is that it increases and decreases.”

He said:

“Then there was disagreement concerning whether the Quran is created or uncreated. Our position and that of our imams is that the Quran is Allah’s speech, uncreated, and that it is an attribute of Allah. From Him it originated as speech, and to Him it returns in judgment.”

He then mentioned the disagreement concerning seeing Allah, saying:

“Our belief and that of our imams is that Allah will be seen on the Day of Resurrection.”

He cited the supporting proof, then said:

“Know—may Allah have mercy on you—that I have discussed the rulings concerning these disagreements in the order followed by the hadith scholars throughout the ages. I have now begun to set out the provisions of the general articles of belief.

“We therefore say and believe that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has a Throne, and that He is upon His Throne, above His seven heavens

translated_text:
with all His names and attributes, as He says:

‘The Most Merciful rose over the Throne.’

‘He directs affairs from heaven to earth.’

We do not say that He is on earth as He is in heaven upon His Throne, for He knows what happens to His servants: ‘Then it ascends to Him.’”

He went on to say:

“We believe that Allah Most High created Paradise and Hell, and that they were created to endure, not to perish.”

He went on to say:

“We believe that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ascended in person to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary.”

He went on to say:

“We believe that Allah took two handfuls and said, ‘These are for Paradise, and these are for Hell.’

“We believe that the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has a ‘Pool,’ and we believe that he is the first to intercede and the first whose intercession is accepted.”

He mentioned the “Bridge,” the “Balance,” and “death,” and that a person who is killed dies at his appointed time, having received his allotted provision in full.

He went on to say:

“Among our beliefs is that Allah descends every night to the lowest heaven during the last third of the night, stretches out His hand, and says, ‘Is there anyone asking?’”—and he cited the rest of the hadith—“and on the night of mid-Sha'bān and the afternoon of the day of Arafah.”

He mentioned the hadith concerning this.

He said:

“We believe that Allah Most High truly spoke to Moses and took Abraham as an intimate friend, and that intimate friendship is distinct from poverty—not as the people of innovation claim. We believe that Allah Most High singled out Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for the vision, and took him as an intimate friend just as He took Abraham as an intimate friend. We believe that Allah Most High alone possesses the key to five matters of the unseen, which none but Allah knows: ‘Indeed, Allah alone has knowledge of the Hour’”—to the end of the verse.
