{لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ أَحْدَثَ حَدَثًا أَوْ آوَى مُحْدِثًا}
 وَلِقَوْلِهِ: 
{وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَمُحْدَثَاتِ الْأُمُورِ فَإِنَّ كُلَّ بِدْعَةٍ ضَلَالَةٌ}
 .
 فَإِنَّهُ يُقَالُ لَهُ:
 الْحَادِثُ فِي اللُّغَةِ مَا كَانَ بَعْدَ أَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ وَاَللَّهُ تَعَالَى يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ؛ فَمَا مِنْ فِعْلٍ يَفْعَلُهُ إلَّا وَقَدْ حَدَثَ بَعْدَ أَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ.
translated_text:
accidents without qualification—is that which inheres in something else, such as life, knowledge, power, motion, rest, and the like.

Others say: “It is that which does not persist for two successive moments.” They say: “The Creator’s attributes endure, unlike the attributes inhering in created beings, which do not persist for two successive moments.”

The point here is that the claim, “If knowledge and power inhered in Him, it would be an accident; and whatever has an accident inhering in it has afflictions inhering in it,” involves equivocation, for one of its two premises is false. If the term “accident” means an attribute, the second premise is false; if it means an illness or the like that befalls a person, the first premise is false.

A parallel example would be someone saying:

“If He had risen over the Throne, He would have brought about something new, and temporally originated events would inhere in Him. For rising over the Throne is a temporally originated act—one that came to be after not having been. Thus, if rising over the Throne inhered in Him, temporally originated events would inhere in Him; and anyone in whom such events inhere has brought about something new. Yet Allah Most High is far above that, because the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

‘May Allah curse whoever commits an offence or shelters an offender.’

And he said:

‘Beware of newly introduced matters, for every innovation is misguidance.’”

The reply is:

In ordinary language, “temporally originated” means that which comes to be after not having been. Allah Most High does whatever He wills, and every act He performs comes to be after not having been.

original_text:
وَأَمَّا الْمُحْدَثَاتُ الَّتِي ذَكَرَهَا النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَهِيَ الْمُحْدَثَاتُ فِي الدِّينِ وَهُوَ أَنْ يُحْدِثَ الرَّجُلُ بِدْعَةً فِي الدِّينِ لَمْ يَشْرَعْهَا اللَّهُ وَالْإِحْدَاثُ فِي الدِّينِ مَذْمُومٌ مِنْ الْعِبَادِ وَاَللَّهُ يُحْدِثُ مَا يَشَاءُ لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ. فَاللَّفْظُ الْمُشْتَبِهُ الْمُجْمَلُ إذَا خُصَّ فِي الِاسْتِدْلَالِ وَقَعَ فِيهِ الضَّلَالُ وَالْإِضْلَالُ. وَقَدْ قِيلَ إنَّ أَكْثَرَ اخْتِلَافِ الْعُقَلَاءِ مِنْ جِهَةِ اشْتِرَاكِ الْأَسْمَاءِ.
الْوَجْهُ الثَّانِي:
 فِي بَيَانِ بُطْلَانِ مَا ذَكَرَ مِنْ الِاسْتِدْلَالِ أَنْ يُقَالَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ مُنَزَّهٌ أَنْ يَكُونَ مِنْ جِنْسِ شَيْءٍ مِنْ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ: لَا أَجْسَادَ الْآدَمِيِّينَ وَلَا أَرْوَاحَهُمْ وَلَا غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَ مَنْ جِنْسِ شَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ بِحَيْثُ تَكُونُ حَقِيقَتُهُ كَحَقِيقَتِهِ لَلَزِمَ أَنْ يَجُوزَ عَلَى كُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا مَا يَجُوزُ عَلَى الْآخَرِ وَيَجِبُ لَهُ مَا يَجِبُ لَهُ وَيَمْتَنِعُ عَلَيْهِ مَا يَمْتَنِعُ عَلَيْهِ وَهَذَا مُمْتَنِعٌ؛ لِأَنَّهُ يَسْتَلْزِمُ أَنْ يَكُونَ الْقَدِيمُ الْوَاجِبُ الْوُجُودِ بِنَفْسِهِ؛ غَيْرَ قَدِيمٍ وَاجِبِ الْوُجُودِ بِنَفْسِهِ وَأَنْ يَكُونَ الْمَخْلُوقُ الَّذِي يَمْتَنِعُ غِنَاهُ غَنِيًّا يَمْتَنِعُ افْتِقَارُهُ إلَى الْخَالِقِ؛ وَأَمْثَالُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ الْأُمُورِ الْمُتَنَاقِضَةِ وَاَللَّهُ تَعَالَى نَزَّهَ نَفْسَهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ كُفُؤٌ أَوْ مِثْلٌ أَوْ سَمِيٌّ أَوْ نِدٌّ.
فَهَذِهِ الْأَدِلَّةُ الشَّرْعِيَّةُ وَالْعَقْلِيَّةُ يُعْلَمُ بِهَا تَنَزُّهُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى أَنْ يَكُونَ مِنْ جِنْسِ أَجْسَادِ الْآدَمِيِّينَ أَوْ غَيْرِهَا مِنْ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ؛
 لَكِنَّ الْمُسْتَدِلَّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ بِقَوْلِهِ:
translated_text:
As for the newly introduced matters mentioned by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, these are matters newly introduced into religion: a person introduces a religious innovation that Allah has not prescribed. Introducing innovations into religion is blameworthy on the part of His servants, whereas Allah brings into being whatever He wills; none can overturn His judgment. Thus, when an ambiguous, indeterminate expression is singled out for use in an argument, error and misguidance result. It has been said that most disagreements among rational people arise from words having multiple meanings.

The second argument:

The invalidity of the reasoning he has presented may also be demonstrated as follows: Allah, glorified be He, is far above belonging to the same kind as any created thing—whether human bodies, human souls, or any other created beings. Were He of the same kind as any of these, such that His reality was like its reality, it would follow that whatever is possible for either would be possible for the other, whatever is necessary for either would be necessary for the other, and whatever is impossible for either would be impossible for the other. This is impossible, since it would entail that the Eternal, whose existence is necessary in and of Himself, is not eternal and necessarily existent in and of Himself; and that a created being, which cannot be independent, is independent and cannot depend upon the Creator—along with other such contradictions. Allah Most High has declared Himself far above having any equal, likeness, namesake, or rival.

These scriptural and rational proofs establish that Allah Most High is far above belonging to the same kind as human bodies or any other created things. Yet one who argues for this on the basis of His words:

" الْجَسَدَ "
 وَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ قَالَ الْجَوْهَرِيُّ وَغَيْرُهُ: إنَّ الْجَسَدَ هُوَ الْبَدَنُ يُقَالُ مِنْهُ تَجَسَّدَ كَمَا يُقَالُ: مِنْ الْجِسْمِ تَجَسَّمَ وَالْجَسَدُ أَيْضًا الزَّعْفَرَانُ وَنَحْوُهُ مِنْ الصَّبْغِ وَهُوَ الدَّمُ أَيْضًا.
 كَمَا قَالَ النَّابِغَةُ:
وَمَا أُرِيقَ عَلَى الْأَصْنَامِ مِنْ جَسَدٍ
فَلَيْسَ الْمُرَاد بِالْجَسَدِ فِي الْقُرْآنِ لَا هَذَا وَلَا هَذَا فَلَيْسَ الْمُرَاد مِنْ الْعِجْلِ أَنَّ لَهُ بَدَنًا مِثْلُ بَدَنِ الْآدَمِيِّينَ وَلَا بَدَنًا كَأَبْدَانِ الْبَقَرِ فَإِنَّ الْعِجْلَ لَمْ يَكُنْ كَذَلِكَ وَالْعَرَبُ تَقُولُ جَسِدَ بِهِ الدَّمُ يَجْسَدُ جَسَدًا إذَا لَصِقَ بِهِ فَهُوَ جَاسِدٌ وَجَسِدٌ.
 قَالَ الشَّاعِر:
سَاعِدٌ بِهِ جَسِدٌ مُوَرَّسُ … مِنْ الدِّمَاءِ مَائِعٌ وَيَبِسُ
وَالْجَسَدُ الْأَحْمَرُ وَالْجَسَدُ مَا أُشْبِعَ صَبْغُهُ مِنْ الثِّيَابِ؛ لِكَمَالِ مَا لَصِقَ بِهِ مِنْ الصَّبْغِ فَاللَّفْظُ فِيهِ مَعْنَى التَّكَاثُفِ وَالتَّلَاصُقِ؛ وَلِهَذَا يَقُولُ الْفُقَهَاءُ نَجَاسَةٌ مُتَجَسِّدَةٌ وَغَيْرُ مُتَجَسِّدَةٍ وَهُوَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ يُرَادُ بِهِ الْجَسَدُ الْمُصْمَتُ الْمُتَلَاصِقُ الْمُتَكَاثِفُ أَوْ الَّذِي لَا حَيَاةَ فِيهِ. وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لَفْظَةَ الْجَسَدِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ.
 فَقَالَ تَعَالَى:
 
{وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ جَسَدًا لَا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ}
 وَقَالَ تَعَالَى:
translated_text:
“In his absence, the people of Moses made from their ornaments a calf—a bodily form that lowed,” has relied on a weak argument.

Al-Jawharī and others have indeed said that jasad means “body,” with the derived verb tajassada (“to take bodily form”), just as tajassama is derived from jism (“body”). Jasad also means saffron and similar dyes, as well as blood, as al-Nābigha said:

And the blood poured out upon the idols.

Yet neither of these meanings is intended by jasad in the Quran. The description of the calf does not mean that it had a body like a human body, nor a body like those of cattle, for the calf was not like that. The Arabs say jasida bihi al-damu (“blood adhered to him”), with the forms yajsadu and jasadan; such blood is called jāsid or jasid. A poet said:

A forearm thickly stained with blood,
Some flowing, some dried.

Jasad also means “red” and denotes cloth saturated with dye, because of how thoroughly the dye adheres to it. The word thus conveys a sense of density and cohesion. Hence jurists speak of impurity with physical substance and impurity without it. In the Quran, it denotes a solid, cohesive, compact body, or one devoid of life. Allah Most High has used the word jasad in four places.

He Most High said:

“We did not make them bodies that ate no food.”

And He Most High said:

{وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ}
 وَقَالَ: 
{وَاتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسَى مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَهُ خُوَارٌ}

{فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَهُ خُوَارٌ}
 كَأَنَّهُ عِجْلٌ مُصْمَتٌ لَا جَوْفَ لَهُ.
 وَقَدْ يُقَالُ:
 إنَّهُ لَا حَيَاةَ فِيهِ خَارَ خورة. وَلَمْ يَقُلْ عِجْلًا لَهُ جَسَدٌ لَهُ بَدَنٌ لَهُ جِسْمٌ؛ لِأَنَّهُ مِنْ الْمَعْلُومِ أَنَّ كُلَّ عِجْلٍ لَهُ جَسَدٌ هُوَ بَدَنُهُ وَهُوَ جِسْمُهُ وَالْعِجْلُ الْمَعْرُوفُ جَسَدٌ فِيهِ رُوحٌ.
 وَالْمَقْصُودُ:
 أَنَّ مَا أَخْرَجَهُ كَانَ جَسَدًا مُصْمَتًا لَا رُوحَ فِيهِ حَتَّى تَبَيَّنَ نَقْصُهُ وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ مَسْلُوبَ الْحَيَاةِ وَالْحَرَكَةِ.
 وَقَدْ رُوِيَ:
 أَنَّهُ إنَّمَا خَارَ خورة وَاحِدَةً وَقَدْ يُقَالُ: إنْ أُرِيدَ بِالْجَسَدِ الْمُصْمَتُ أَوْ الْغَلِيظُ وَنَحْوُهُ فَلِمَ قِيلَ إنَّ ذَلِكَ ذَكَرَ لِبَيَانِ نَقْصِهِ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ؛ بَلْ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ ضَلُّوا بِهِ وَإِنَّمَا كَانَ النَّقْصُ مِنْ جِهَةِ 
{أَنَّهُ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمْ وَلَا يَهْدِيهِمْ سَبِيلًا}
 وَقَدْ يُقَالُ: إذَا كَانَ لَا حَيَاةَ فِيهِ فَالنَّقْصُ كَانَ فِيهِ مِنْ جِهَةِ عَدَمِ الْحَيَاةِ وَغَيْرِهَا مِنْ صِفَاتِ الْكَمَالِ؛ لَا مِنْ جِهَةِ كَوْنِهِ لَهُ بَدَنٌ أَوْ لَيْسَ لَهُ بَدَنٌ؛ فَالْآدَمِيُّ لَهُ بَدَنٌ.
 وَلَوْ أَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا كَسَائِرِ الْعُجُولِ أَوْ آدَمِيًّا كَامِلًا أَوْ فَرَسًا حَيًّا أَوْ جَمَلًا أَوْ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ الْحَيَوَانِ:
 لَكَانَ أَيْضًا لَهُ بَدَنٌ وَلَكِنَّ ذَلِكَ أُعْجُوبَةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ وَكَانَتْ الْفِتْنَةُ بِهِ أَشَدَّ؛ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ بَيَّنَ أَنَّ الْمُخْرَجَ كَانَ مَوْصُوفًا بِصِفَاتِ النَّقْصِ يُحَقِّقُ ذَلِكَ.
translated_text:
“And We placed upon his throne a body; then he turned back in repentance.”

And He said:

“In his absence, the people of Moses made from their ornaments a calf—a bodily form that lowed.”

And He Most High said:

“Then he brought forth for them a calf—a bodily form that lowed.”

It was as though it were a solid calf with no hollow interior. It may also be said that it had no life in it, though it let out a low. He did not say “a calf possessing a jasad, badan, or jism”—all meaning “body”—for it is well known that every calf has a jasad, namely its badan or jism. An ordinary calf is a body containing a soul.

The point is that what he brought forth was a solid body without a soul, thus making its deficiency apparent: it was devoid of life and movement. It has been reported that it lowed only once.

It may be asked: If jasad means something solid, dense, or the like, why is it said that this description was mentioned to show its deficiency in this respect? Rather, it was precisely this aspect that led them astray through it. Its deficiency lay only in the fact that “it neither spoke to them nor guided them to any way.”

It may also be said: If it had no life, its deficiency lay in its lack of life and other attributes of perfection, not in whether or not it had a body; a human being, after all, has a body. Had he brought forth for them a calf like any other calf, a complete human being, a living horse, a camel, or any other animal, it too would have had a body. That, however, would have been a tremendous marvel, and the trial it posed would have been even greater. Yet Allah, glorified be He, made clear that what had been brought forth possessed attributes of deficiency. The following confirms this.

The third argument:

He, glorified be He, said:

“Did they not see that it neither spoke to them nor guided them to any way?”

He did not mention its having a body among the faults He identified in it. Rather, He mentioned “that it neither spoke to them nor guided them to any way.” Had merely having a body been a fault and a deficiency, He would have mentioned it.

Thus, the verse shows the inadequacy of the argument advanced by those who cite it as evidence that having a body is a fault and a deficiency. This argument resembles their appeal to setting: they altered its linguistic meaning, making it mean movement, and supposed that Abraham used this as evidence that it was not the Lord of all worlds. Yet even if matters were as they claimed, this would be an argument against them, not for them.

(The fourth argument): Allah Most High described it as a calf—a bodily form that lowed—and then said:

“Did they not see that it neither spoke to them nor guided them to any way?”

And He said in the other surah:

“And so al-Sāmirī cast it in.”

“Then he brought forth for them a calf—a bodily form that lowed—and they said, ‘This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot.’”

“Did they not see that it could not return a word to them and had no power to harm or benefit them?”

Thus, He did not confine His description to its merely being a body. Rather, He described it as lowing and made clear that it neither spoke to them nor had any power to harm or benefit them. Its deficiency must therefore arise either from these attributes collectively, from some of them, or from each one individually. If it arises from their combination, this does not show that any one of them, taken separately, is a deficiency. If it arises from some of them, then its being a body is no more likely to be the cause than its lowing. And neither of these is more likely to be the cause than its being deprived of

 فَالْعَابِدُ أَكْمَلُ مِنْ الْمَعْبُودِ يُبَيِّنُ هَذَا أَنَّهُ لَوْ كَلَّمَهُمْ لَكَانَ أَيْضًا مُصَوِّتًا فَلَوْ كَانَ ذِكْرُ الصَّوْتِ لِبَيَانِ نَقْصِهِ لَبَطَلَ الِاسْتِدْلَالُ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى:
 
{أَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّهُ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمْ}
 فَإِنَّ تَكْلِيمَهُ لَهُمْ لَوْ كَلَّمَهُمْ إنَّمَا كَانَ يَكُونُ بِصَوْتِ يَسْمَعُونَهُ مِنْهُ. فَعُلِمَ أَنَّ ذِكْرَ التَّصْوِيتِ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِكَوْنِهِ صِفَةَ نَقْصٍ فَكَذَلِكَ ذِكْرُ الْجَسَدِ.
 وَبِالْجُمْلَةِ:
 مَنْ ذَكَرَ أَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ دَلَّ عَلَى هَذَا وَهَذَا هُوَ الْعَيْبُ الَّذِي عَابَهُ بِهِ وَجَعَلَهُ دَلِيلًا عَلَى نَفْيِ إلَهِيَّتِهِ؛ فَقَدْ قَالَ عَلَى الْقُرْآنِ مَا لَا يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؛ بَلْ هُوَ عَلَى نَقِيضِهِ أَدَلُّ.
translated_text:

(The fifth argument): Nothing in the Quran indicates that its being a bodily form or its lowing is an attribute of deficiency. Rather, what the Quran indicates is that its failure to speak to them and its inability to benefit or harm them constitute a deficiency.

This is made clear by the fact that lowing is sound. A human being, too, produces sound—one says of a bull, “It lowed; it lows”—yet he speaks to others and may guide them to the way. Allah, glorified be He, made clear that the calf’s attributes fell short of those of a human being who speaks to others and guides them. Thus, the worshipper is more perfect than the object of worship.

This is further clarified by the fact that, had it spoken to them, it would also have produced sound. If sound had been mentioned to establish its deficiency, the argument conveyed by His words, Most High,

“Did they not see that it did not speak to them?”

would have been invalid. For had it spoken to them, it would only have done so through a sound they could hear from it. It is therefore clear that its producing sound was not mentioned because this was an attribute of deficiency. The same applies to the mention of its bodily form.

In short, whoever claims that the Quran identifies these two features as the fault for which Allah censured it and which He made evidence against its divinity has attributed to the Quran something it does not indicate. Indeed, it points more clearly to the opposite.

The sixth argument:

Allah Most High relates that Abraham, His intimate friend—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees nor can benefit you at all?”

And He, Most High, says:

“He said, ‘Do they hear you when you call, or do they benefit you or harm you?’ They said, ‘Rather, we found our fathers doing the same.’”

Thus, he argued against their divinity on the grounds that they neither hear nor see, neither benefit nor harm, even though each of them has a body and physical form, whether made of stone or anything else. Had this consideration alone sufficed as an argument, Abraham, the intimate friend of Allah, and the other prophets—may the finest blessings and peace be upon them—would have mentioned it. Instead, they argued as Allah did, pointing to their lack of attributes of perfection, such as speech, power, movement, and so forth.

The seventh argument:

It may be said: What Allah Most High has mentioned either indicates that the Deity, glorified be He, possesses some of these attributes, or it does not. If it does not, their argument is invalid. If it does, then it indicates that attributes of perfection are to be affirmed of Allah Most High: speaking to His servants, hearing, sight, power, and the ability to benefit and harm. This means that these verses are evidence for affirming the attributes, not denying them.

Those who deny the attributes do so only because they claim that affirming them entails corporeality and embodiment. Thus, the verses they invoke as evidence count against them, not in their favour. We have found this to be a consistent pattern in most of the verses invoked by those who deny the attributes: these verses indicate the opposite of what they seek to establish, not what they seek to establish.

The eighth argument:

If every body is a physical form, and everything worshipped besides Allah Most High—the sun, the moon, the stars, idols, and other things—consists of bodies that are physical forms, then, if Allah mentioned this concerning the calf in order thereby to deny its divinity, this argument must apply consistently to all objects of worship.

Yet it is well known that Allah did not mention this concerning anything other than the calf. He mentioned its being a physical form to explain why they were captivated by it, not to make that the argument against them. Rather, He argued against them on the grounds that it neither spoke to them nor guided them to any path.

The ninth argument:

He, glorified be He, says in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf:

“Do they have feet with which they walk, or hands with which they grasp, or eyes with which they see, or ears with which they hear?”

There are two views concerning this verse:

The first is that He described them as having these deficiencies to show that the worshipper is more perfect than the object of worship.

The second is that He mentioned this because the object of worship must possess the opposite of these attributes. If the first view is adopted, the same could be said concerning the verse about the calf; it would then have no bearing on the attributes of the Deity.

If the second view is adopted, the Lord Most High must possess what He denied of the idols.

In that case, if these things are bodies, this indication would contradict

Allah, Almighty and Majestic, must therefore be described as possessing hands and the other attributes mentioned in the Quran and Sunnah. These need not be bodies, nor does affirming them amount to ascribing corporeality to Him. (The tenth argument):

It may be said: The evidence in the Quran and Sunnah affirming the attributes of perfection and that He Himself is above the Throne is too abundant to enumerate. Examples include His words:

“To Him ascends good speech,”

and His words:

“Rather, Allah raised him to Himself,”

and His words:

“The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him,”

and His words:

“Indeed, those who are with your Lord.”

It has been said that these amount to three hundred verses. They are clear, manifest proofs, readily understood from the Quran and grasped from the words of Allah Most High.

If affirming this necessarily entails that Allah is a body and a physical form, then the implications of these texts cannot be set aside on the basis of what was mentioned in the account of the calf. For that account does not state that merely being a physical form was the deficiency that Allah condemned and made an obstacle to its divinity.

If, however, affirming that He is above and affirming His attributes does not necessarily entail that He is a body and a physical form, then the very foundation of their argument collapses. Their mainstay is the claim that affirming that He is above entails corporeality and embodiment. If they concede that it does not necessarily entail corporeality and embodiment, they would have no evidence for denying it.

Section: Reconciling the Lord’s Being on High—Mighty and Majestic Is He—with His Nearness to Those Who Call upon Him and Worship Him

We say:

Allah has described Himself in His Book and through His Messenger as being on high, established over the Throne, and above His creation. This appears in many verses of His Book, so much so that one of al-Shāfi‘ī’s leading followers said: “The Quran contains a thousand proofs, or more, indicating that Allah is high above creation and above His servants.”

Another said: “It contains three hundred proofs indicating this,” such as His words:

“Indeed, those who are with your Lord”

and:

“To Him belong all those in the heavens and the earth, and those who are with Him.”

If “with Him” meant “within His power,” as the Jahmiyyah say, then all creation would be within His power and subject to His will; there would be no distinction between those in the heavens, those on earth, and those with Him. Likewise, if being established over meant exercising dominion, He would be established over all created things, and He would always have been established over the Throne, even before He created it. Yet His establishment is specific to the Throne and took place after the creation of the heavens and the earth, as He has stated in

Hence, according to the leading scholars who affirm the divine attributes, being on high is an attribute known through both revelation and reason, whereas being established over the Throne is an attribute known through revelation, not through reason.

The point is that He, Most High, has also described Himself as being with His creation and being near. His being with His creation is of two kinds: general and special. The first is exemplified by His words:

“And He is with you wherever you are.”

The second is exemplified by His words:

“Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who do good.”

There are other verses to this effect. As for nearness, examples include His words:

“Indeed, I am near.”

And His words:

“And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.”

“And We are nearer to him than you are.”

People have divided into four groups on this issue.

The Jahmiyyah who deny the divine attributes—those who say that He is neither within the world nor outside it, neither above nor below—affirm neither His being on high nor His being above creation. Instead, they either reinterpret all such descriptions or leave their meaning to Allah.

All the groups given to religious innovation may appeal to scriptural texts—the Khawārij, the Shī‘ah, the Qadariyyah, the Rāfidah, the Murji’ah, and others—except the Jahmiyyah. They have not a single statement from the prophets that supports the negations they assert. Hence Ibn al-Mubārak and Yūsuf ibn Asbāt said:

" الْعُلُوِّ وَالِاسْتِوَاءِ "
. وَكُلُّ نَصٍّ يَحْتَجُّونَ بِهِ حُجَّةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ؛ فَإِنَّ الْمَعِيَّةَ أَكْثَرُهَا خَاصَّةً بِأَنْبِيَائِهِ وَأَوْلِيَائِهِ وَعِنْدَهُمْ أَنَّهُ فِي كُلِّ مَكَانٍ. وَفِي النُّصُوصِ مَا يُبَيِّنُ نَقِيضَ قَوْلِهِمْ؛
 فَإِنَّهُ قَالَ:
 
{سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ}
 فَكُلُّ مَنْ فِي السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُسَبِّحُ وَالْمُسَبِّحُ غَيْرُ الْمُسَبَّحِ ثُمَّ قَالَ: 
{لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ}
 فَبَيَّنَ أَنَّ الْمُلْكَ لَهُ.
 ثُمَّ قَالَ:
 
{هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ}
 .
 وَفِي الصَّحِيحِ:
 
{أَنْتَ الْأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَك شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَك شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَك شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَك شَيْءٌ؛}
 فَإِذَا كَانَ هُوَ الْأَوَّلَ كَانَ هُنَاكَ مَا يَكُونُ بَعْدَهُ وَإِذَا كَانَ آخِرًا كَانَ هُنَاكَ مَا الرَّبُّ بَعْدَهُ وَإِذَا كَانَ ظَاهِرًا لَيْسَ فَوْقَهُ شَيْءٌ كَانَ هُنَاكَ مَا الرَّبُّ ظَاهِرٌ عَلَيْهِ وَإِذَا كَانَ بَاطِنًا لَيْسَ دُونَهُ شَيْءٌ كَانَ هُنَاكَ أَشْيَاءُ نُفِيَ عَنْهَا أَنْ تَكُونَ دُونَهُ.
translated_text:
“The Jahmiyyah fall outside the seventy-three sects.” This is one of the two views held by Ahmad’s followers, both mentioned by Abū ‘Abd Allāh ibn Hāmid and others.

A second group say that He is everywhere in His very essence, as the Najjāriyyah and many of the Jahmiyyah—their devotees, Sufis, and common people—say. They say that He is the very existence of created things, as do the advocates of the unity of existence, who maintain that existence is one, and those whose doctrine combines indwelling and union. They appeal to the scriptural texts concerning His being with creation and His nearness, while reinterpreting the texts concerning His being on high and His being established over the Throne.

Yet every text they cite is evidence against them. Most references to His being with others concern His prophets and His allies specifically, whereas they maintain that He is everywhere. Moreover, the texts contain statements that demonstrate the opposite of their claim. He says:

“Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

Thus, everyone in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and the one who glorifies is distinct from the One glorified. He then says:

“To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens.”

He thereby makes clear that dominion belongs to Him. Then He says:

“He is the First and the Last, the Most High and the Most Near, and He has knowledge of all things.”

An authentic hadith states:

“You are the First, and nothing is before You. You are the Last, and nothing is after You. You are the Most High, and nothing is above You. You are the Most Near, and nothing is nearer than You.”

Thus, if He is the First, there is something that comes after Him. If He is the Last, there is something after which the Lord remains. If He is the Most High, with nothing above Him, there is something above which the Lord is. And if He is the Most Near, with nothing nearer than Him, there are things of which it is denied that they are nearer than Him.

translated_text:
For this reason, Ibn ‘Arabī said:

“Among His Most Beautiful Names is ‘the Most High.’ Above whom is He high, when none exists but Him? Above what is He high, when nothing exists but Him? His highness therefore belongs to Him intrinsically, and in terms of existence He is identical with existing things. Thus, what are called originated things are themselves intrinsically high, and they are none other than He.”

Then he said:

“Al-Kharrāz said—he being one of the faces of the Real and one of His tongues, speaking of himself—that Allah is known through His uniting opposites. He is the very thing that is manifest, and He is the very thing that is hidden even while He is manifest. There is no one you see other than Him, and there is no one from whom He is hidden other than Himself. He is therefore manifest to Himself and hidden from Himself, and He is the one named ‘Abū Sa‘īd al-Kharrāz.’”

“Being with” does not imply intermingling or mixing, nor does the expression “nearness.” The advocates of indwelling hold that He is within the jugular vein, just as, in their view, He is within all other entities. All of this is disbelief and ignorance of the Quran.

The third group consists of those who say: “He is above the Throne, and He is everywhere.” Such a person says: “I affirm both sets of texts and do not divert any of them from their apparent meaning.” This is the position of several groups mentioned by al-Ash‘arī in al-Maqālāt al-Islāmiyyah (Islamic Doctrines), and it appears in the statements of some of the Sālimiyyah and Sufis. Something similar appears in the statements of Abū Tālib al-Makkī, Ibn Barrajān, and others, despite the contradictions in much of what these two say. In this connection, Abū ‘Alī al-Ahwāzī—who wrote The Faults of Ibn Abī Bishr and refuted Abū al-Qāsim ibn ‘Asākir—belonged to the Sālimiyyah. Likewise, al-Khatīb al-Baghdādī mentioned that a number of people criticized Abū Tālib for his statements concerning the divine attributes.

translated_text:
This third group is admittedly closer to adhering to the texts, and further from contradicting them, than the first two groups. The first followed none of the texts, but contradicted them all. The second abandoned the many clear, unambiguous texts and clung to a few texts whose meanings it had misunderstood.

As for this group, it says: “I have followed all the texts.” Yet it too is mistaken. Whoever says that Allah Himself is everywhere contradicts the Quran, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the early generations of this community and its leading scholars. He also contradicts the innate disposition upon which Allah created His servants, sound reason, and numerous proofs.

These people make contradictory statements. They say: “He is above the Throne,” yet they also say: “The Throne’s share of Him is like that of the heart of one who knows Him,” as Abū Tālib and others state.

It is well known that the heart’s share of Him consists in knowledge of Him, faith, and what follows from these. If they say that the same applies to the Throne, they contradict their assertion that He Himself is above the Throne. If they say that He Himself indwells the hearts of those who know Him, this amounts to outright affirmation of indwelling. A group of Sufis has fallen into this—even the author of Manāzil al-Sā’irīn (The Stations of the Wayfarers), in his account of divine oneness at the end of that work, fell into this kind of indwelling.

For this reason, the leading masters among them used to warn against such things. Al-Junayd was asked about affirming divine oneness and replied: “It is to distinguish what originated in time from what has no beginning.” He thus explained that whoever affirms Allah’s oneness must distinguish between the beginningless Creator and the originated creation

In the Quran:

“Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets?”

—and so on to the end of the verse. Affirming His seeing and hearing is intended to establish His knowledge of these things, and that He knows whether they are good or evil, rewarding good deeds and punishing evil deeds.

Likewise, His power over creation is affirmed in His words:

“You cannot escape Him, either on earth or in heaven.”

And His words:

“Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us? How ill they judge!”

The intention is to instil fear of the consequences necessarily ensuing from evil deeds: punishment and retribution.

Thus, the Lord often describes Himself by His knowledge and actions, warning and inspiring fear, and encouraging souls to pursue good. He also describes Himself by His power, hearing, sight, and recording. The meaning signified by the expression is intended, while what that meaning necessarily implies is also intended. Thus, what the expression signifies in its original linguistic usage is intended, both by direct signification and by necessary implication. The expression is therefore not used solely to convey the implication; rather, its own signified meaning, from which that implication follows, is intended. This is literal usage.

As for the term “nearness,” He has spoken of it sometimes in the singular and sometimes in the plural;

the former occurs only in connection with answering the supplicant:

“When My servants ask you about Me, I am indeed near. I answer the supplicant’s call.”

Likewise, the hadith states:

“Be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. You are calling upon One who is All-Hearing and Near. The One you call upon is nearer to each of you than the neck of his mount.”

The plural form occurs in His words:

“We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.”

This is like His words:

“We recite to you,”

“We relate to you,”

“So when We have recited it,”

“Indeed, it is for Us to gather it and recite it,”

and “It is for Us to explain it.”

Here, the recitation takes place when he hears it from Gabriel, and the explanation means explaining it to those whom the Quran reaches.

The position of the early generations of this Muslim community, its leading scholars, and its later generations is that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, heard the Quran from Gabriel, and Gabriel heard it from Allah, Almighty and Majestic.

As for His words, “We recite,” “We relate,” and “So when We have recited it,” this form is used in Arabic for a single person of great standing who has helpers who obey him. When his helpers do something at his command, he says, “We did it.” Thus a king says, “We conquered this land and defeated this army,” and the like, because he acts through his helpers.

Allah Most High is the Lord of the angels. They do not speak before He speaks, and they act at His command. They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, but do as they are commanded. Moreover, He is their Creator and the Creator of their actions and their power, and He has no need of them.

He is not like a king whose helpers act with power and movement by which they can act independently of him. Thus, His saying, “We did it,” concerning what He has done through His angels is more warranted and appropriate than such words spoken by certain kings.

They followed the ambiguous passages, seeking thereby discord—unsettling hearts by suggesting the existence of multiple gods—and seeking their interpretation. Regarding “None knows its interpretation except Allah” and “those firmly grounded in knowledge,” the early generations held two views, both of which are true.

Those who say that people firmly grounded in knowledge do not know its interpretation explain that its interpretation is the reality to which it ultimately refers. What the Quran speaks of through the expressions “Indeed, We” and “We” refers to the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful and through whom He directs the affairs of heaven and earth. None but Allah knows their number; none other than Him knows their attributes; and He alone knows how He commands them to act. Allah Most High says:

“None knows the hosts of your Lord except Him.”

Although each angel knows his own condition and that of others, he does not know all the angels or everything Allah has created in this regard.

Those who say that people firmly grounded in knowledge know its interpretation explain that “interpretation” means explanation: making the meaning of the discourse known to people. Those firmly grounded in knowledge therefore know the explanation of the entire Quran and the meanings Allah has made clear, as is abundantly reported from the early generations.

Thus, those firmly grounded in knowledge know that His words:

Those firmly grounded in knowledge are not like the ignorant, who do not understand “Indeed, We” and “We,” but merely utter words whose meanings they do not know, or allow the possibility of three distinct gods, or one with no helpers.

“Allah takes the souls.”

For He, glorified be He, takes them through His messengers, as He says:

He takes them through His messengers, foremost among whom is the Angel of Death.

refers to Gabriel’s recitation of it to him. Allah recited it through Gabriel, as He says:

“Or He sends a messenger who reveals, by His permission, whatever He wills.”

Thus, He speaks to Muhammad through Gabriel’s tongue and by sending him to Muhammad. The same is established concerning the believers, as He Most High says:

“Allah has already informed us about you.”

Allah informed them only through Muhammad.

Likewise, He says:

“Say, ‘We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to us.’”

“And what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom.”

It was sent down to the believers through Muhammad. Likewise, the angels themselves draw near to the dying person.

He, glorified be He, and His angels know what the servant’s soul whispers within him, as is established in the two Sahih collections:

—to the end of the hadith. Thus, the angels know what good or evil a person intends, and “intention” occurs within the soul before action. More striking still, Satan flows through the son of Adam as blood flows, whispering to him about what he desires, and thus knows what his soul desires.

The worshipper has been commanded to say in prostration:

“Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.”

This is reported by the compilers of the Sunan collections. Likewise, the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd states:

“When the servant prostrates and says three times during his prostration, ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High,’ his prostration is complete, and that is its minimum.”

This is reported by Abū Dāwūd. In the hadith of Hudhayfah reported by Muslim:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, offered a night prayer in which he recited al-Baqarah, al-Nisāʾ, and Āl ʿImrān. He then bowed and then prostrated, for approximately as long as his recitation, saying while bowing, ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent,’ and while prostrating, ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’”

This is because prostration represents the servant’s utmost submission and humility, and his lowering and humbling himself to the fullest extent before Allah by placing the noblest part of himself—his face—on the dust. It is therefore fitting that, when he is at his lowest, he should describe his Lord as the Most High. “Most High” is more emphatic than “High,” for the servant possesses nothing of himself: considered in himself, he is sheer nonexistence, and he has no share in grandeur or greatness.

Likewise, the servant has no right to “exaltation on earth,” for Allah, glorified is He, has condemned those who desire exaltation on earth, such as Pharaoh and Iblīs. The believer, however, attains an elevated rank through faith, not by desiring it, as Allah Most High says:

“Do not lose heart or grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers.”

Since prostration represents the servant’s utmost lowliness and submission, he glorifies the name of his Lord, the Most High. He, glorified is He, is the Most High, and the servant is the lowliest, just as He is the Lord and the servant is the servant. He is the Self-Sufficient, and the servant is

in need. There is nothing between the Lord and the servant but pure servitude: the more perfectly the servant fulfils it, the closer he draws to Him. For He, glorified is He, is kind, generous and beneficent, giving the servant what befits him. The greater his need of Him, the richer he becomes; and the greater his humility before Him, the more honour he attains. The soul, with its varied desires and Satan’s enticements, grows distant from Allah until it becomes accursed, far removed from mercy.

A “curse” means being removed far away. Among the soul’s gravest sins is the desire for exaltation on earth, whereas prostration brings it to the utmost lowliness. Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation.”

An authentic hadith states:

“No one who has an atom’s weight of pride in his heart will enter Paradise.”

He said to Iblīs:

“Then descend from it! It is not for you to be arrogant therein.”

And He said:

“And the word of Allah is supreme.”

This is an established attribute of His word. Yet whoever seeks to raise anything else above it is fought. The Prophet said:

“Whoever fights so that the word of Allah may be supreme is fighting in the cause of Allah.”

The “word of Allah” comprises His statements and His commands: His command is to be obeyed and given precedence over anyone else’s command, and His statements are to be heeded and given precedence over anyone else’s statements. He also said:

“And all worship is devoted to Allah alone.”

“Dīn” means worship, obedience, submission and the like. One says, “I subdued him, and he submitted,” meaning, “I humbled him, and he became humble.” As the poet said:

He subdued al-Rabāb when they spurned submission,
with raid upon raid and fierce assault.
Then al-Rabāb submitted;
the punishment dealt by kings was like torment.

Thus, if worship, obedience and humility before Him establish His supremacy in the servants’ hearts—just as He is Most High in Himself, and just as His word becomes supreme in their hearts while it is supreme in itself—then likewise, the purpose of declaring His greatness is that He should be greater than everything else in the servant’s estimation. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to ‘Adī ibn Hātim:

“O ‘Adī, what makes you turn away? Is it the declaration, ‘There is no god but Allah’? Do you know of any god other than Allah? O ‘Adī, what makes you turn away? Is it the declaration, ‘Allah is greater’? Is there anything greater than Allah?”

This refutes those who take akbar (“greater”) to mean merely kabīr (“great”). The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“We prophets have one religion.”

That religion is Islam: submission to Allah, not to anyone else, with worship, obedience and humility devoted to Him. This is the true meaning of “There is no god but Allah.” Undoubtedly, nothing other than this is accepted. He, glorified is He, is to be obeyed in every age according to what He commanded in that age. Thus, after Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent, Islam can consist only in following what he brought and obeying him. This is the religion of Abraham, which none turns away from except one who makes a fool of himself.

Abraham is the “exemplar,” one who is followed, just as a “role model” is one whose example is emulated. He is the “leader,” as in His words:

“I will make you a leader for the people.”

He is “devoutly obedient”; devout obedience means constant obedience, for he obeys Allah at all times. The “upright monotheist” is one who turns unswervingly to his Lord, and to none besides Him.

And His saying:

“Whoever draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by a cubit; and whoever draws near to Me by a cubit,

I draw near to him by an armspan; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running.”

When one thing is near another, this necessarily entails that the other is near it. Yet the nearness of the second may simply follow from the first drawing near, or the second may also draw near in its own right. The first is like someone approaching Mecca or the wall of the Kaaba: the nearer he comes to it, the nearer it is to him, without any action on its part. The second is like a person drawing near to someone who is also drawing near to him, as in the divine report quoted above.

Numerous texts speak of the servant drawing near to Allah and of Allah bringing him near, such as His sayings:

“Those whom they invoke seek a means of approach to their Lord, striving to be nearest to Him.”

“Then, if he is among those brought near.”

“A spring from which those brought near will drink.”

“Nor the angels brought near.”

“And among those brought near.”

“My servant has not drawn near to Me with anything like fulfilling what I have made obligatory upon him”—to the end of the hadith.

Another hadith states:

“The nearest a servant is to his Lord is during the last part of the night.”

We have discussed these hadiths and people’s views on this subject at length in Response to the Egyptian Questions on the Hamāh Fatwa. This, then, is the Lord Himself drawing near to His servant, and it is like His descent to the lowest heaven.

An authentic hadith states:

“Allah draws near on the afternoon of ʿArafah”—to the end of the hadith.

All this nearness is specific. Neither the Book nor the Sunnah ever speaks of His Essence being near to all created beings in every circumstance. This establishes the falsity of the position of those who advocate divine indwelling: they have taken what is specific and qualified and made it universal and unqualified. Their brethren, the advocates of divine union, have done the same with statements such as His saying:

“I become his hearing,”

and His saying:

“He then comes to them in a form other than His own,”

and with Allah’s saying through His Prophet:

“Allah hears whoever praises Him.”

And all these texts are evidence against them; this becomes clear when the distinctions are drawn. The person who supplicates or prostrates directs his soul towards Allah. The soul has an ascent appropriate to it, and undoubtedly draws near to Allah Most High in proportion to its freedom from impurities. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is then near to it with a nearness that necessarily follows from its nearness to Him. There is also another nearness on His part, such as His drawing near on the afternoon of Arafah and in the depth of the night, and His drawing an arm’s length nearer to whoever draws a handspan nearer to Him.

In Ahmad’s al-Zuhd, it is reported from Imrān al-Qasīr:

“Moses, peace be upon him, said, ‘My Lord, where should I seek You?’ He said, ‘Seek Me among those whose hearts are broken. Every day I draw an armspan nearer to them; were it not for that, they would fall apart.’”

This may resemble His saying:

“I have divided the prayer into two halves between Myself and My servant”—to the end of the report.

The apparent meaning of His saying,

“I am indeed near,”

indicates that nearness is His attribute, not merely a necessary consequence of the nearness of the person who supplicates or prostrates. His drawing near on the afternoon of Arafah is on account of the pilgrims’ supplication, remembrance and repentance that night. Otherwise, if it were supposed that no one stood at Arafah, that drawing near to them on His part—glory be to Him—would not occur. For He boasts of the people of Arafah before the angels; if it were supposed that no one was there, this would not occur. This therefore indicates that He draws near to them because they draw near to Him, as the other hadith also indicates.

In the latter part of the night, people’s hearts turn towards Him and draw near to Him with a tenderness not found at other times. This accords with His descent to the lowest heaven and His saying:

“Is there anyone supplicating? Is there anyone asking? Is there anyone repenting?”

As for someone who does not believe that Allah is above the Throne, he does not believe in His descent, whether the Throne becomes empty of Him or not. One of their leading figures said to someone who affirmed the divine attributes, “His command descends.” The latter replied, “From whom does it descend? According to you, there is no one there! First affirm that He is there, then say, ‘His command descends.’” This resembles what Ishāq ibn Rāhawayh said in the presence of the emir Abd Allāh ibn Tāhir.

The correct view is that of the early generations: He descends without the Throne becoming empty of Him. A person’s soul remains in his body night and day until he dies. During sleep it ascends and may prostrate beneath the Throne, although it has not left his body. Likewise:

“The closest a servant comes to his Lord is when he is prostrating.”

His soul is still in his body. The principles governing souls differ from those governing bodies; how much more so with the angels, and then with the Lord of all worlds!

Night occurs at different times: the third of the night comes in the East before it comes in the West. His descent, as reported by His Messenger, is to the heaven above these people during the third of their night, and to the heaven above those people during the third of their night. No matter distracts Him from another. Likewise, His nearness to the supplicant who draws near to Him, and to the one who prostrates, is according to each individual, wherever he may be. Two men may prostrate in the same place, yet each has a nearness particular to him in which the other does not share.

The transmitted texts contain guidance and healing. The one who conveyed them clearly knew his Lord better than anyone else, was the most sincere in counselling His creation, and was the clearest in expression and most effective in conveying the message. No one, therefore, can match what the Messenger knew and said. Everyone whom Allah blesses with insight in his heart recognizes this. Then the Exalted said:

“Those who have been given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, and that it guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.”

Of those opposed to them, He said:

“Those who deny Our signs are deaf and mute, in darkness. Whomever Allah wills, He leaves astray, and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path.”

His saying, “al-Zāhir (the Manifest),” incorporates the meaning of being high, as in His saying:

“They could not climb over it.”

One also says, “The preacher ascended the pulpit.” The outer surface of a garment is its uppermost layer, as opposed to its lining. Likewise, the outside of a house is its upper surface; the apparent meaning of a statement is what is evident and clear from it; and a person’s outward aspect is the opposite of his inward aspect. The higher something rises, the more manifest it becomes. Hence he said:

“You are the Manifest, and there is nothing above You.”

He thus affirmed manifestness and stated that it entails there being nothing above Him. He did not say, “Nothing is more evident or better known than You.” This makes clear the error of interpreting “the Manifest” as “the known,” as do those who say, “Manifest through evidence, hidden behind a veil,” an interpretation found in the words of Abū al-Faraj and others. Such an interpreter has not stated what Allah and His Messenger intended, even if what he has stated carries a valid meaning. He also said:

“You are the Hidden, and there is nothing nearer than You.”

translated_text:
He is manifest and hidden, although both concepts convey manifestation and concealment, as well as a further meaning, such as elevation in the case of manifestness; for He, glorified be He, is not described as being low.

We have explained this at length in our discussion of encompassing. However, He is manifest only from the direction above us: He is manifest through the hearts’ knowledge of Him and their turning towards Him, and through direct vision when He is seen on the Day of Resurrection. He is manifest and exalted, with nothing above Him.

From another direction, He is hidden: He is neither sought nor beheld from that direction, even though nothing is nearer than He. For He encompasses them from behind, and nothing is nearer than He, glorified be He.

translated_text:
Section: Concluding the Discussion of Nearness

The Lord, glorified be He, is not distracted by hearing one thing from hearing another, nor do requests confuse Him. Rather, He, glorified be He, will speak to His servants on the Day of Resurrection and call them to account, without His dealings with one distracting Him from another.

Ibn Abbās was asked, “How will He speak to them all on the Day of Resurrection at the same time?” He replied, “Just as He provides for them at the same time.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There is not one of you with whom his Lord will not be alone, just as one of you is alone with the moon on the night of the full moon.”

In this world, Allah, glorified be He, hears the supplications of those who call upon Him and answers those who ask, despite their different languages and varied needs. One of us may have sufficiently keen hearing to hear many people speaking, just as some teachers of Quran recitation can listen to several people reciting. Yet these can only be a small number close by.

One of us also finds within himself a sense of closeness, nearness, and inclination towards some people rather than others, whether they are present or absent, and finds that this nearness and closeness vary in degree. The Lord, exalted be He, is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing: His hearing encompasses all voices, and His bounty encompasses all needs.

translated_text:
Some people have erred in supposing that His nearness resembles the movement of a human body, which turns away from one direction when it inclines towards another. Yet a person finds that his spirit acts differently from his body: he finds his soul drawing near to the souls of many people, without its nearness to one detracting from its nearness to another. Likewise, he finds within himself humility and love towards some people, remoteness and distance from others, a sense of elevation, and a turning towards some people and away from others—all distinct from what occurs in the body.

In sum, the nearness of the Lord to His worshippers and those who call upon Him, as expressed in the Quran and Sunnah, is qualified and specific, not unrestricted and universal to all creation. Thus, the claim of those who advocate divine indwelling is invalid. As He says:

“And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near.”

This is His nearness to those who call upon Him. As for His nearness to His worshippers, it is expressed in such statements as:

“Those whom they invoke themselves seek a means of nearness to their Lord, each striving to be closest.”

And His saying:

“My servant has not drawn near to Me with anything like fulfilling what I have made obligatory upon him.”

He also said:

“Whoever draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by a cubit.”

This is His nearness to His servant and His servant’s nearness to Him. His drawing near to the lowest heaven on the afternoon of Arafah does not fall outside these two categories, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The best supplication is the supplication on the Day of Arafah.”

Thus, His drawing near is on account of their supplication. As for His descent to the lowest heaven every night, if it is for those who call upon Him, ask of Him, and seek His forgiveness, then at that time there is a degree of the Lord’s nearness to His worshippers that does not occur at other times

translated_text:
so it falls within this category. If, however, it is unrestricted, then it is occasioned by the time itself being suited to such worship, even if none actually occurs.

A parallel is the “hour when supplications are answered” on Friday. It is reported that this is tied to the performance of the Friday prayer, extending from when the imam ascends the pulpit until the prayer ends. Accordingly, it is tied to the performance of the Friday prayer: anyone who fails to perform it without an excuse, despite believing it obligatory, has no share in that hour. As for someone who habitually attends the Friday prayer but then falls ill or travels, the deeds he used to perform while healthy and resident are recorded for him. The same applies to someone imprisoned and others in similar circumstances. They receive a reward equal to that of those who attend the Friday prayer, so their supplication is like the supplication of those who attend it.

The blessings of the mercy that descends upon the pilgrims on the afternoon of Arafah and upon those attending the Friday prayer may also extend to others who have valid excuses. They may thus receive a share in the answering of supplications and partake alongside those present, as occurs during Ramadan. This is available to those who love these worshippers and the worship in which they are engaged: their hearts thereby draw nearer to Allah, and they wish they could be with them.

As for the disbeliever or hypocrite who does not regard Hajj as an act of righteousness, nor the Friday prayer as an obligation and an act of righteousness, but turns away from loving or desiring such worship, his heart is far from Allah’s mercy. For Allah’s mercy is near to those who do good, and he is not among them.

It is also reported that this hour on Friday falls at the end of the day, in which case it is occasioned by the time itself. It is established in the Sahīh collection:

“There is an hour during the night when supplication is answered, just as there is on Friday, and this occurs every night. The closest a servant comes to his Lord is in the latter part of the night.”

translated_text:
Section

As for the Lord’s nearness to the hearts of believers and their hearts’ nearness to Him, this is a well-known matter, not something unknown. Hearts ascend to Him in proportion to the faith, knowledge, remembrance, reverent fear, and reliance upon Him that they contain. This is agreed upon by all people, unlike the nearness discussed earlier. For this is denied by the Jahmī who says, “Above the heavens there is no Lord to be worshipped, nor any God to whom prayer and prostration are offered.” This is disbelief and folly.

The former is denied by the Kullābiyyah and those who say, “Nothing dependent on His will subsists in Him.” Among the followers of al-Ashʿarī, from the adherents of Ahmad and others, are those who identify pleasure, anger, joy, and love with the will. At other times, they regard them as other eternal attributes distinct from the will.

This agreed-upon nearness within the heart is, in reality, the nearness of the mental representation, and it necessarily entails love for Him. For when someone loves a person, a representation of that person forms in his heart, and he finds him close to his heart. When he remembers him, he becomes present in his heart. A person’s love for a created being may even cause him to lose awareness of himself, as the poet said:

“Through you I lost awareness of myself,
And so I thought that you were I.”

translated_text:
And of the same kind are the poet’s words:

“Present in my heart, I behold him;
I never forget him, that I should need to recall him.”

And another’s words:

“Your image is before my eyes, your remembrance on my lips;
Your dwelling is my heart—how, then, could you be absent?”

This is the “highest similitude” of which Allah says:

“To Him belongs the highest similitude.”

Likewise, He says:

“It is He who is God in heaven and God on earth.”

“He is Allah in the heavens and on earth.”

This is also the “likeness” referred to in His words:

“There is nothing like Him.”

For nothing whatsoever resembles Him, glorified is He. Nothing that exists resembles His holy Self, and no attributes resemble His attributes. No other knowledge resembles the knowledge of Him held in hearts, and no love resembles love for Him. Thus, to Him belongs the “highest similitude,” just as He Himself is the Most High.

The Most High also says:

“Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire.”

“The likeness of those who spend their wealth seeking Allah’s pleasure and out of their own firm conviction is that of a garden on high ground: heavy rain falls upon it, and it yields twice its produce. If no heavy rain falls upon it, then a drizzle suffices. And Allah sees all that you do.”

And there are other such passages.

translated_text:
The likeness of one thing is compared with that of another, and this entails comparing the things themselves. For things can only be spoken of after they are known. He, glorified is He, first speaks of the “mental representation,” also called the mental image. Then, if the account is true, it provides evidence that the reality corresponds to the conception of it. This is why people speak of a thing and describe it only in terms of what they know of it, and their names for it vary according to the attributes they know it to possess.

Whoever sees Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in a dream sees Him in a form corresponding to the dreamer’s condition. If he is righteous, he sees Him in a beautiful form. Hence the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw Him in the most beautiful form.

The “visions” that some of those who know Allah may experience while awake relate only to the mental representation being beheld. An example is what Ibn ‘Umar said to Ibn al-Zubayr when the latter asked for his daughter’s hand in marriage during circumambulation: “Are you speaking to me about women while we behold Allah, Mighty and Majestic, during our circumambulation?” The same applies to similar experiences. However, the Prophet’s seeing his Lord—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—is a matter for discussion elsewhere. Ibn ‘Abbās said: “He saw Him with his heart twice.” Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was singled out for something in which no one else shared.

This mental representation varies in hearts in countless ways according to their knowledge of Allah and their love for Him. Indeed, people differ in their faith in “Allah,” “His Book,” and “His Messenger”;

original_text: فَلِكُلِّ مِنْهُمْ فِي قَلْبِهِ لِلْكِتَابِ وَالرَّسُولِ مِثَالٌ عِلْمِيٌّ بِحَسَبِ مَعْرِفَتِهِ مَعَ اشْتِرَاكِهِمْ فِي الْإِيمَانِ بِاَللَّهِ وَبِكِتَابِهِ وَبِرَسُولِهِ - فَهُمْ مُتَنَوِّعُونَ فِي ذَلِكَ مُتَفَاضِلُونَ. وَكَذَلِكَ إيمَانُهُمْ بِالْمَعَادِ وَالْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أُمُورِ الْغَيْبِ وَكَذَلِكَ مَا يُخْبِرُ بِهِ النَّاسُ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا مِنْ أُمُورِ الْغَيْبِ هُوَ كَذَلِكَ بَلْ يُشَاهِدُونَ الْأُمُورَ وَيَسْمَعُونَ الْأَصْوَاتَ وَهُمْ مُتَنَوِّعُونَ فِي الرُّؤْيَةِ وَالسَّمَاعِ فَالْوَاحِدُ مِنْهُمْ يَتَبَيَّنُ لَهُ مَنْ حَالِ الْمَشْهُودِ مَا لَمْ يَتَبَيَّنْ لِلْآخَرِ حَتَّى قَدْ يَخْتَلِفُونَ فَيُثْبِتُ هَذَا مَا لَا يُثْبِتُ الْآخَرُ فَكَيْفَ فِيمَا أُخْبِرُوا بِهِ مِنْ الْغَيْبِ. وَالنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَخْبَرَهُمْ عَنْ الْغَيْبِ بِأَحَادِيثَ كَثِيرَةٍ وَلَيْسَ كُلُّهُمْ سَمِعَهَا مُفَصَّلَةً وَاَلَّذِينَ سَمِعُوا مَا سَمِعُوا لَيْسَ كُلُّهُمْ فَهِمَ مُرَادَهُ بَلْ هُمْ مُتَفَاضِلُونَ فِي السَّمْعِ وَالْفَهْمِ كَتَفَاضُلِ مَعْرِفَتِهِمْ وَإِيمَانِهِمْ بِحَسَبِ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى يُثْبِتَ أَحَدُهُمْ أُمُورًا كَثِيرَةً وَالْآخَرُ لَا يُثْبِتُهَا لَا سِيَّمَا مَنْ عَلِقَ بِقَلْبِهِ شُبَهُ الْنُّفَاةِ؛ فَهُوَ يَنْفِي مَا أَثْبَتَهُ الْكِتَابُ وَالسُّنَّةُ وَمَا عَلَيْهِ أَهْلُ الْحَقِّ. وَهَذَا يُبَيِّنُ لَك أَنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ كُلَّهُمْ مُؤْمِنُونَ بِاَللَّهِ وَكِتَابِهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ - وَإِنْ كَانُوا مُتَفَاضِلِينَ فِي الْإِيمَانِ - إلَّا مَنْ شَاقَّ الرَّسُولَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ الْهُدَى وَاتَّبَعَ غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ. ثُمَّ هُمْ يَتَفَاضَلُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْإِرَادَةِ فَإِذَا كَانَ أَحَدُهُمْ أَكْثَرَ مَحَبَّةً لِلَّهِ وَذِكْرًا وَعِبَادَةً كَانَ الْإِيمَانُ عِنْدَهُ أَقْوَى وَأَرْسَخَ مِنْ حَيْثُ الْمَحَبَّةُ وَالْعِبَادَةُ لِلَّهِ وَإِنْ كَانَ لِغَيْرِهِ مِنْ الْعِلْمِ بِالْأَسْمَاءِ وَالصِّفَاتِ مَا لَيْسَ لَهُ.
translated_text:
thus each of them has in his heart a mental representation of the Book and the Messenger corresponding to his knowledge. Although they share faith in Allah, His Book, and His Messenger, they differ in this regard and attain different degrees. The same applies to their faith in the Resurrection, Paradise, Hell, and other matters of the unseen, as well as to matters beyond direct perception that people relate to one another. Indeed, even when they witness events and hear sounds, they differ in what they see and hear. One person discerns aspects of what he witnesses that another does not. They may even disagree, with one affirming what another does not affirm. How much more so, then, regarding the unseen matters of which they have been informed!

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed them about the unseen in many hadiths, but not all of them heard these in detail. Nor did everyone who heard what he heard understand the Prophet’s intent. Rather, they differ in how much they have heard and understood, and their knowledge and faith vary accordingly. Thus, one may affirm many things that another does not affirm, especially someone whose heart has become entangled in the specious arguments of the deniers: he denies what the Book and the Sunnah affirm and what the people of truth uphold.

This makes clear to you that all these people believe in Allah, His Book, His Messenger, and the Last Day—although their faith varies in degree—except anyone who opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows a path other than that of the believers.

They also differ in knowledge and will. If one of them has greater love for Allah, remembers Him more, and worships Him more, his faith is stronger and more firmly rooted with respect to love and worship of Allah, even though another may possess knowledge of the divine names and attributes that he does not.

فَصَاحِبُ الْمَحَبَّةِ وَالذِّكْرِ وَالتَّأَلُّهِ يَحْصُلُ لَهُ مِنْ حُضُورِ الرَّبِّ فِي قَلْبِهِ وَأُنْسِهِ بِهِ مَا لَا يَحْصُلُ لِمَنْ لَيْسَ مِثْلَهُ. وَكَذَلِكَ الْإِيمَانُ بِالرَّسُولِ قَدْ يَكُونُ أَحَدُ الشَّخْصَيْنِ أَعْلَمَ بِصِفَاتِهِ وَالْآخَرُ أَكْثَرَ مَحَبَّةً لَهُ وَكَذَلِكَ الْأَشْخَاصُ - الْمَشْهُورُونَ - قَدْ يَكُونُ الرَّجُلُ أَعْلَمَ بِمَا رَأَى وَالْآخَرُ أَكْثَرَ مَحَبَّةً لَهُ وَ 
{الْأَرْوَاحُ جُنُودٌ مُجَنَّدَةٌ فَمَا تَعَارَفَ مِنْهَا ائْتَلَفَ وَمَا تَنَاكَرَ مِنْهَا اخْتَلَفَ}

translated_text:
Thus, someone devoted to love, remembrance, and worship experiences a sense of the Lord’s presence in his heart and an intimacy with Him that someone unlike him does not. The same applies to faith in the Messenger: one person may know more about his attributes, while another loves him more. Likewise, with well-known individuals, one man may know more about someone he has seen, while another loves that person more. And:

“Souls are troops assembled: those that recognize one another unite, and those that do not recognize one another remain at odds.”

Their recognition of one another consists in their affinity and similarity in what they know, love, and dislike.

Many of these worshippers, whose hearts witness a mental image and who lose themselves in what they witness, imagine that they have seen Allah with their own eyes. This is because the power of witnessing has overwhelmed their hearts, leaving them without reason by which to distinguish. It is the heart that perceives things, sometimes through the outward senses and sometimes by itself. They therefore cease to distinguish between these two modes of perception. If they lose awareness of the distinction between them, they imagine that they have seen Him with their own eyes. If they lose awareness of the distinction between the one witnessing and the One witnessed, they imagine that they themselves are He, as it is related that Abū Yazīd said:

“There is none in this robe but Allah.”

And as another said:

“In You I lost awareness of myself,
And thought that You were I.”

The beloved had thrown himself into the water, and the lover threw himself in after him.

All this results from the strength of the heart’s witnessing and the weakness of reason. It resembles what a sleeper sees: because his reason is absent during sleep, he imagines that he sees what he sees with his physical eyes, and that he hears what he hears

original_text: بِأُذُنِهِ الظَّاهِرَةِ وَمَا يَتَكَلَّمُ بِهِ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِهِ بِلِسَانِهِ بِالْحِسِّ الظَّاهِرِ؛ وَعَيْنُهُ مُغْمَضَةٌ وَلِسَانُهُ سَاكِتٌ. وَقَدْ يَقْوَى تَصَوُّرُهُ الْخَيَالِيُّ فِي النَّوْمِ حَتَّى يَتَّصِلَ بِالْحِسِّ الظَّاهِرِ فَيَبْقَى النَّائِمُ يَقْرَأُ بِلِسَانِهِ وَيَتَكَلَّمُ بِلِسَانِهِ تَبَعًا لِخَيَالِهِ وَمَعَ هَذَا فَعَقْلُهُ غَائِبٌ لَا يَشْعُرُ بِذَلِكَ كَمَا يَحْصُلُ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ لِلسَّكْرَانِ وَالْمَجْنُونِ وَغَيْرِهِمَا. وَلِهَذَا جَاءَتْ الشَّرِيعَةُ بِأَنَّ الْقَلَمَ مَرْفُوعٌ عَنْ النَّائِمِ وَالْمَجْنُونِ وَالْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَخْتَلِفُوا إلَّا فِيمَنْ زَالَ عَقْلُهُ بِسَبَبِ مُحَرَّمٍ. وَهَذَا يُبَيِّنُ أَنَّ كُلَّ مَنْ أَقَرَّ بِاَللَّهِ فَعِنْدَهُ مِنْ الْإِيمَانِ بِحَسَبِ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ مَنْ لَمْ تَقُمْ عَلَيْهِ الْحُجَّةُ بِمَا جَاءَتْ بِهِ الْأَخْبَارُ لَمْ يَكْفُرْ بِجَحْدِهِ وَهَذَا يُبَيِّنُ أَنَّ عَامَّةَ أَهْلِ الصَّلَاةِ مُؤْمِنُونَ بِاَللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ - وَإِنْ اخْتَلَفَتْ اعْتِقَادَاتُهُمْ فِي مَعْبُودِهِمْ وَصِفَاتِهِ - إلَّا مَنْ كَانَ مُنَافِقًا - يُظْهِرُ الْإِيمَانَ بِلِسَانِهِ وَيُبْطِنُ الْكُفْرَ بِالرَّسُولِ - فَهَذَا لَيْسَ بِمُؤْمِنِ؛ وَكُلُّ مَنْ أَظْهَرَ الْإِسْلَامَ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ مُنَافِقًا فَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ لَهُ مِنْ الْإِيمَانِ بِحَسَبِ مَا أوتيه مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَهُوَ مِمَّنْ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ النَّارِ وَلَوْ كَانَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ الْإِيمَانِ وَيَدْخُلُ فِي هَذَا جَمِيعُ الْمُتَنَازِعِينَ فِي الصِّفَاتِ وَالْقَدَرِ عَلَى اخْتِلَافِ عَقَائِدِهِمْ. وَلَوْ كَانَ لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ إلَّا مَنْ يَعْرِفُ اللَّهَ كَمَا يَعْرِفُهُ نَبِيُّهُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمْ تَدْخُلْ أُمَّتُهُ الْجَنَّةَ؛ فَإِنَّهُمْ - أَوْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ - لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ هَذِهِ الْمَعْرِفَةَ؛ بَلْ يَدْخُلُونَهَا
translated_text:
with his physical ears, and that he speaks with his tongue through his outward senses; yet his eyes are closed and his tongue is still. His mental imagery during sleep may become so powerful that it connects with his outward senses, so that the sleeper recites and speaks with his tongue in response to what he imagines. Even then, his reason is absent, and he is unaware of this, just as similar things happen to someone who is intoxicated or insane, and to others. Hence, Islamic law declares that the pen of accountability is lifted from the sleeping, the insane, and the unconscious. Disagreement has arisen only concerning someone who loses his reason through something forbidden.

This shows that everyone who acknowledges Allah possesses faith to that extent. Moreover, someone against whom the proof concerning what the transmitted reports convey has not been established does not become a disbeliever by denying it. This shows that the general body of those who perform the prayer are believers in Allah and His Messenger—even though their beliefs concerning the One they worship and His attributes differ—except for a hypocrite who professes faith with his tongue while inwardly disbelieving in the Messenger. Such a person is not a believer.

Everyone who outwardly professes Islam and is not a hypocrite is a believer, possessing faith in proportion to what he has been granted of it. He is among those who will be brought out of the Fire, even if there is only an atom’s weight of faith in his heart. This includes all those who dispute over the divine attributes and divine decree, despite their differing beliefs.

If no one could enter Paradise except someone who knows Allah as His Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—knows Him, his community would not enter Paradise, for they—or most of them—are incapable of such knowledge. Rather, they will enter it

original_text:
وَتَكُونُ مَنَازِلُهُمْ مُتَفَاضِلَةً بِحَسَبِ إيمَانِهِمْ وَمَعْرِفَتِهِمْ وَإِذَا كَانَ الرَّجُلُ قَدْ حَصَلَ لَهُ إيمَانٌ يَعْرِفُ اللَّهَ بِهِ وَأَتَى آخَرُ بِأَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ عَجَزَ عَنْهُ لَمْ يُحَمَّلْ مَا لَا يُطِيقُ وَإِنْ كَانَ يَحْصُلُ لَهُ بِذَلِكَ فِتْنَةٌ لَمْ يُحَدِّثْ بِحَدِيثِ يَكُونُ لَهُ فِيهِ فِتْنَةٌ.
 فَهَذَا أَصْلٌ عَظِيمٌ فِي تَعْلِيمِ النَّاسِ وَمُخَاطَبَتِهِمْ بِالْخِطَابِ الْعَامِّ بِالنُّصُوصِ الَّتِي اشْتَرَكُوا فِي سَمَاعِهَا:
 كَالْقُرْآنِ وَالْحَدِيثِ الْمَشْهُورِ وَهُمْ مُخْتَلِفُونَ فِي مَعْنَى ذَلِكَ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ. وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ.
translated_text:
and their ranks will vary according to their faith and knowledge. If a person has attained faith through which he knows Allah, and someone else presents him with more than he can grasp, he is not to be burdened beyond his capacity. If this would subject him to a trial, one should not relate to him a report that would expose him to such a trial.

This is a principle of great importance in teaching people and addressing them collectively through texts they have all heard, such as the Quran and widely known hadith, even though they differ in their understanding of their meaning. Allah knows best. May Allah bless Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

original_text:
سُئِلَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ أَبُو الْعَبَّاسِ أَحْمَد بْنُ تَيْمِيَّة - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَنْ رَجُلَيْنِ اخْتَلَفَا فِي الِاعْتِقَادِ،
 فَقَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا:
 مَنْ لَا يَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى فِي السَّمَاءِ فَهُوَ ضَالٌّ.
 وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ:
 إنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ لَا يَنْحَصِرُ فِي مَكَانٍ وَهُمَا شَافِعِيَّانِ فَبَيِّنُوا لَنَا مَا نَتَّبِعُ مِنْ عَقِيدَةِ 
" الشَّافِعِيِّ "
 رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ وَمَا الصَّوَابُ فِي ذَلِكَ؟
الْجَوَابُ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، اعْتِقَادُ الشَّافِعِيِّ - رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ - وَاعْتِقَادُ 
" سَلَفِ الْإِسْلَامِ "
 
(*)
 كَمَالِكِ وَالثَّوْرِيِّ وَالْأَوْزَاعِي وَابْنِ الْمُبَارَكِ وَأَحْمَد بْنِ حَنْبَلٍ وَإِسْحَاقَ بْنِ رَاهَوَيْه؛ وَهُوَ اعْتِقَادُ الْمَشَايِخِ الْمُقْتَدَى بِهِمْ كالْفُضَيْل بْنِ عِيَاضٍ وَأَبِي سُلَيْمَانَ الداراني وَسَهْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ التستري وَغَيْرِهِمْ. فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ بَيْنَ هَؤُلَاءِ الْأَئِمَّةِ وَأَمْثَالِهِمْ نِزَاعٌ فِي أُصُولِ الدِّينِ. وَكَذَلِكَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ - رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ - فَإِنَّ الِاعْتِقَادَ الثَّابِتَ عَنْهُ فِي التَّوْحِيدِ وَالْقَدَرِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ مُوَافِقٌ لِاعْتِقَادِ هَؤُلَاءِ وَاعْتِقَادُ هَؤُلَاءِ هُوَ مَا كَانَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّحَابَةُ وَالتَّابِعُونَ لَهُمْ بِإِحْسَانِ وَهُوَ مَا نَطَقَ بِهِ الْكِتَابُ وَالسُّنَّةُ.

وهذه الفتوى مختصره، ففيها ما يدل على ذلك، كقوله في:
