 . وَمَعَ هَذَا فَبَدَنُهُ أَسْفَلُ مَا يَكُونُ. فَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُعْرَفَ أَنَّ الْحَرَكَةَ جِنْسٌ تَحْتَهُ أَنْوَاعٌ مُخْتَلِفَةٌ بِاخْتِلَافِ الْمَوْصُوفَاتِ بِذَلِكَ. وَمَا يُوصَفُ بِهِ نَفْسُ الْإِنْسَانِ مِنْ إرَادَةٍ وَمَحَبَّةٍ وَكَرَاهَةٍ وَمَيْلٍ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ
translated_text:
tranquillity and stillness; hence water is described as yaqan. Likewise, one says, “He became unsettled,” or, “He unsettled him, and he became unsettled,” meaning that he disturbed him. This is said both of someone whose soul becomes restless and of someone who becomes restless in soul and body until he leaves his place.

Likewise, one says, “His soul became restless,” or, “His soul became agitated,” and uses similar expressions denoting various kinds of movement. Whatever human beings find familiar and love is called a source of repose, because they find rest in it. One says, “So-and-so finds rest and reassurance in so-and-so.” Likewise, one says, “The heart finds rest and reassurance in so-and-so,” when that person is trustworthy and known for truthfulness, for truthfulness brings tranquillity and stillness.

A wife, too, is called a source of repose. Allah Most High says:

“He created for you spouses from among yourselves so that you may find rest in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy.”

He also says:

“And He made from it its mate, so that he might find rest in her.”

Thus, a man finds rest in a woman with both his heart and his body. A person’s body may be still while his soul is moving vigorously; conversely, his heart may be still while his body is moving. Someone who loves a thing and longs for it is described as moving towards it. Hence the saying, “Passionate love is the movement of an unoccupied soul.”

Hearts move towards Allah Most High through love, turning to Him in repentance, directing themselves towards Him, and other acts of the heart, even though the body is not moving upwards. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The closest a servant comes to his Lord is while he is prostrating.”

Yet his body is then at its lowest. It should therefore be understood that movement is a genus encompassing different kinds, which vary according to the things described as moving. The will, love, aversion, inclination, and similar attributes ascribed to the human soul

وهذا تصحيف صوابه: (هفا الطائر بجناحه)، (وهفا الشيء في الهواء) والكلام السابق واللاحق كله عن هذا اللفظ.
translated_text:
all involve the soul’s transition from one state to another and activity on its part; this is movement appropriate to its nature. Hence these meanings are expressed in terms of movement. One says, “So-and-so yearns towards so-and-so,” as in the verse:

My heart’s yearnings flutter towards the bān trees—
yet not for the trees, but for those in Dārat al-Bān.

This expression is used for the swift movement of something light. Thus one says, “The bird fluttered its wings,” meaning that it flapped them and flew; and something is said to flutter through the air when it drifts like a tuft of wool or the like (*). Likewise, “The gazelle passed by, bounding,” means that it was leaping. Hence a lapse is called a hafwa (slip), just as it is called a zalla (slip): a slip is a slight movement, and so too is a hafwa.

Similarly, a yearning lover whose love has grown stronger than attachment is called “sabā,” and his condition is called sabāba: the tenderness and heat of longing. A sabb is a yearning lover, so called because his heart pours towards the beloved as running water pours forth. Water pours down a mountain—that is, it descends. Since, in descending, it moves with a motion that nothing turns back, the lover’s movement is called “sabāba.” This expression is used of both praiseworthy and blameworthy love.

An example is the hadith:

“When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent Abū ‘Ubayda, may Allah be pleased with him, on a military expedition, he wept out of ardent love and longing for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Sabāba and sabb are related through ‘greater derivation.’ The Arabs alternate between a weak letter

Al-Jawharī said: “Sabiyy, too, is associated with longing. From this root one says tasābā, and sabā, yasbū, with the verbal nouns sabwa and subuww, meaning that he inclined towards youthful folly and vigour. Asbathu al-jāriya means ‘the girl stirred his desire.’”

This expression may also denote a praiseworthy inclination, according to the reading of:

“Indeed, those who believed, those who were Jews, the Christians, and the Sabians”

without a hamza (glottal stop), as in Nāfi‘’s reading. He omits the hamza in the word for “Sabians” throughout the Quran. Allah Most High has praised some of them.

Likewise, one says hanna ilayhi hanīnan, meaning “he yearned for him.” Related to this through ‘greater derivation’ is hanā, yahnū ‘alayhi hunuwwan, meaning “he inclined tenderly towards him.”

Al-Jawharī said: “Hanawtu ‘alayhi means ‘I showed him tenderness’; yahnī ‘alayhi likewise means ‘he shows him tenderness,’ as does tahannana. As the poet said:

‘The soul inclines to you from love’s searing pain—
yet how can you make it incline when you treat it with disdain?’”

He also said: “Hanīn means longing and the soul’s yearning. One says hanna ilayhi, yahinnu hanīnan, ‘he yearned for him’; such a person is called hānn. Hanān means mercy: one says hanna ‘alayhi, yahinnu hanānan, meaning ‘he showed him mercy.’ Hence the words of the Most High:

‘And compassion from Us, and purity.’

“Hannān, with the consonant doubled, means one possessed of mercy. Tahannana ‘alayhi means ‘he showed him mercy.’ The Arabs say hanānayka yā Rabb and hanānaka with the same meaning: ‘Your mercy, O Lord!’” These are al-Jawharī’s words.

A transmitted report explains “al-Hannān, al-Mannān” as follows: al-Hannān is He who turns towards those who turn away from Him, while al-Mannān is He who bestows His gifts before being asked. This is a vast subject.

 وَمِنْ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُفَسِّرُ ذَلِكَ بِمَعْنَى خَاصٍّ فَيَقُولُ:
 لَا حَوْلَ مِنْ مَعْصِيَتِهِ إلَّا بِعِصْمَتِهِ. وَلَا قُوَّةَ عَلَى طَاعَتِهِ إلَّا بِمَعُونَتِهِ. وَالصَّوَابُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْجُمْهُورُ هُوَ التَّفْسِيرُ الْأَوَّلُ وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ
translated_text:
The point here is that all of these are forms within the general category of movement. Movement in this broad sense is a change from one state to another. This is the meaning conveyed by our saying: “There is no change and no power except through Allah.”

The two Sahīh collections report that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Abū Mūsā (may Allah be pleased with him): “Shall I direct you to a treasure among the treasures of Paradise?” He replied, “Yes.” He said: “There is no change and no power except through Allah.”

Sahīh Muslim and other collections report that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said:

“When the caller to prayer says, ‘Allah is the Greatest,’ and a man says, ‘Allah is the Greatest’; then the caller says, ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,’ and the man says, ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah’; then the caller says, ‘I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,’ and the man says, ‘I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah’; then the caller says, ‘Come to prayer,’ and the man says, ‘There is no change and no power except through Allah’; then the caller says, ‘Come to success,’ and the man says, ‘There is no change and no power except through Allah’; then the caller says, ‘Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest,’ and the man says, ‘Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest.’”

The word hawl encompasses every change from one state to another, while power is the ability to make that change. This mighty utterance thus indicates that neither the upper nor the lower world has any movement or change from one state to another, nor any power to do so, except through Allah.

the wording itself. For hawl is not restricted to turning away from disobedience, nor is power restricted to the power to obey. Rather, the word hawl encompasses every change. From it comes the word hīlah (a means or device), which follows the pattern fi‘lah, with an i-vowel, and denotes a particular kind of change. Similarly, jilsah and qi‘dah (ways of sitting), libsah (a way of dressing), iklah (a way of eating), dij‘ah (a way of lying down), and comparable forms denote a particular manner when pronounced with an i-vowel, whereas with an a-vowel they denote a single occurrence.

The original form of hīlah is hūlah. However, when an unvowelled wāw follows an i-vowel, it changes into a yā’, as in mīzān (a balance), mīqāt (an appointed time), and mī‘ād (an appointment). These follow the pattern mif‘āl; the corresponding regular forms would be miwzān and miwqāt. But because the unvowelled wāw follows an i-vowel, it changes into a yā’. Allah Most High says:

“Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who cannot devise any means”

—that is, any means whatsoever. The word is indefinite within a negative construction and therefore encompasses every kind of means.

The same applies to the word quwwah (power). Allah Most High says:

“Allah is the One Who created you in weakness, then after weakness gave you strength, then after strength gave you weakness and grey hair.”

The word quwwah may denote a more complete degree of ability: an ability superior to another, or complete ability. It may also encompass the force found in inanimate things, unlike the word qudrah (ability). Thus, the negation expressed by the word “power” is broader and more comprehensive. If there is no power except through Him, then, all the more certainly, there is no ability except through Him. This is a vast subject.

This is also the position of Abū ‘Abd Allāh ibn Hāmid and others.

Many of the people of hadith and the Sunnah say: “The meaning is correct, but this term should not be used, since it does not occur in the transmitted reports.” Abū ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Barr and others mention this in their discussions of the hadith of descent.

The position widely recognized among the people of the Sunnah and hadith as that of the early generations is to affirm what the Quran and Sunnah state: that He comes, descends, and performs other such intransitive acts.  فَمَنْ وَصَفَهُ بِمِثْلِ صِفَاتِ الْمَخْلُوقِينَ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنْ الْأَشْيَاءِ فَهُوَ مُخْطِئٌ قَطْعًا كَمَنْ قَالَ إنَّهُ يَنْزِلُ فَيَتَحَرَّكُ وَيَنْتَقِلُ كَمَا يَنْزِلُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ السَّطْحِ إلَى أَسْفَلِ الدَّارِ كَقَوْلِ مَنْ يَقُولُ:
 إنَّهُ يَخْلُو مِنْهُ الْعَرْشُ؛ فَيَكُونُ نُزُولُهُ تَفْرِيغًا لِمَكَانِ وَشَغْلًا لِآخَرَ؛ فَهَذَا بَاطِلٌ يَجِبُ تَنْزِيهُ الرَّبِّ عَنْهُ كَمَا تَقَدَّمَ.
translated_text:
Allah will come on the Day of Resurrection, with the angels in rows, to bring the nations to account and have them presented before Him, as He wills and in whatever manner He wills. The Most High says:

‘Are they waiting for anything but for Allah to come to them in canopies of clouds, together with the angels, and for the matter to be decided?’

And the Most High says:

‘And your Lord comes, with the angels in rows.’”

He said: “They also unanimously agreed that Allah descends every night to the lowest heaven, as the transmitted reports state, in whatever manner He wills, without assigning any limits in this regard.” He then narrated through his chain of transmission from Muhammad ibn Waddāh, who said: “I also asked Yahyā ibn Ma‘īn about the descent, and he replied: ‘Yes, I affirm it, without assigning any limit to it.’”

(The third position is to refrain from either denial or affirmation. This is the position preferred by many hadith scholars, jurists, and Sufis, such as Ibn Batta and others. Some of them turn their minds away from considering either possibility, while others incline inwardly toward one of them but express neither denial nor affirmation. What must be held with certainty is that nothing is like Allah in any of the attributes with which He describes Himself.

Anyone who attributes to Him, in any respect, attributes like those of created beings is certainly mistaken. An example is someone who says that He descends, moving and changing location as a person descends from the roof to the lower part of a house—as in the assertion that the Throne is left without Him, so that His descent consists of vacating one place and occupying another. This is false, and the Lord must be declared free of it, as explained above.

وَهَذَا هُوَ الَّذِي تَقُومُ عَلَى نَفْيِهِ وَتَنْزِيهِ الرَّبِّ عَنْهُ الْأَدِلَّةُ الشَّرْعِيَّةُ وَالْعَقْلِيَّةُ؛
 فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى أَخْبَرَ أَنَّهُ الْأَعْلَى وَقَالَ:
 
{سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى}
 . فَإِنْ كَانَ لَفْظُ الْعُلُوِّ لَا يَقْتَضِي عُلُوَّ ذَاتِهِ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ؛ لَمْ يَلْزَمْ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ. وَحِينَئِذٍ فَلَفْظُ النُّزُولِ وَنَحْوِهِ يُتَأَوَّلُ قَطْعًا إذْ لَيْسَ هُنَاكَ شَيْءٌ يُتَصَوَّر مِنْهُ النُّزُولُ. وَإِنْ كَانَ لَفْظُ الْعُلُوِّ يَقْتَضِي عُلُوَّ ذَاتِهِ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ فَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ الْأَعْلَى مَنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ كَمَا أَنَّهُ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ. فَلَوْ صَارَ تَحْتَ شَيْءٍ مِنْ الْعَالَمِ لَكَانَ بَعْضُ مَخْلُوقَاتِهِ أَعْلَى مِنْهُ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ هُوَ الْأَعْلَى وَهَذَا خِلَافُ مَا وَصَفَ بِهِ نَفْسَهُ.

 أَنَّهُ خَلَقَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ اسْتِوَاؤُهُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ يَتَضَمَّنُ أَنَّهُ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ؛ لَمْ يَكُنْ الِاسْتِوَاءُ مَعْلُومًا وَجَازَ حِينَئِذٍ أَلَّا يَكُونَ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ شَيْءٌ؛ فَيَلْزَمُ تَأْوِيلُ النُّزُولِ وَغَيْرِهِ. وَإِنْ كَانَ يَتَضَمَّنُ أَنَّهُ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ فَيَلْزَمُ اسْتِوَاؤُهُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ وَقَدْ أَخْبَرَ أَنَّهُ اسْتَوَى عَلَيْهِ لَمَّا خَلَقَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ وَأَخْبَرَ بِذَلِكَ عِنْدَ إنْزَالِ الْقُرْآنِ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ بِأُلُوفِ مِنْ السِّنِينَ وَدَلَّ
translated_text:
And it is precisely this that the scriptural and rational proofs establish must be denied of the Lord and from which He must be declared free. For Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has declared that He is the Most High, saying:

“Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.”

If the term “highness” does not entail that He Himself is above the Throne, then it does not follow that He is over the Throne. In that case, “descent” and similar expressions must certainly be interpreted figuratively, since there would be nothing there from which descent could be conceived. But if the term “highness” entails that He Himself is above the Throne, then He, glorified be He, is higher than everything, just as He is greater than everything. Were He to come beneath anything in the created world, some of His creatures would be higher than Him, and He would no longer be the Most High. This contradicts His description of Himself.

Furthermore, He has declared that He created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne. If His rising over the Throne does not entail that He is above it, then His rising over the Throne would not be known, and it would then be possible that nothing is above the Throne. This would require interpreting descent and other such expressions figuratively. But if it does entail that He is above the Throne, then His being over the Throne necessarily follows. He has declared that He rose over it after creating the heavens and the earth in six days, and He reported this when He sent down the Quran to Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thousands of years later; and it is indicated

translated_text:
by His words that, when the Quran was revealed, He was established over His Throne, for He said:

“It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne. He knows what enters the earth and what emerges from it, what descends from heaven and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah sees all that you do.”

In the hadith of the mountain goats, narrated by the compilers of the Sunan collections, such as Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī and others, when a cloud passed overhead, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Do you know what this is?”

They replied, “Allah and His Messenger know best.”

He said, “Clouds.” They said, “Clouds.” He said, “And rain clouds.” They said, “And rain clouds.” He mentioned the heavens, their number, and the distance between each pair of heavens, then said, “And Allah is above His Throne, and He knows your condition.”

Likewise, in the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut‘im, narrated by Abū Dāwūd and others, Jubayr ibn Mut‘im said:

A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, people are suffering hardship, families are hungry, wealth has been lost, and livestock have perished. Ask Allah to send us rain, for we seek your intercession with Allah, and we seek Allah’s intercession with you.”

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Woe to you! Do you know what you are saying?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, glorified Allah and continued to do so until this was reflected in the faces of his Companions. Then he said, “Woe to you! Do you know who Allah is? Allah is over His Throne, and His Throne is above His heavens like a dome.” And he gestured with his hand.

وَهَذَا إخْبَارٌ عَنْ أَنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ فِي تِلْكَ الْحَالِ كَمَا دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ كَمَا أَخْبَرَ أَنَّهُ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ وَأَنَّهُ مَعَنَا أَيْنَمَا كُنَّا. وَكَوْنُهُ مَعَنَا أَمْرٌ خَاصٌّ؛ فَكَذَلِكَ كَوْنُهُ مُسْتَوِيًا عَلَى الْعَرْشِ. وَكَذَلِكَ سَائِرُ النُّصُوصِ تُبَيِّنُ وَصْفَهُ بِالْعُلُوِّ عَلَى عَرْشِهِ فِي هَذَا الزَّمَانِ؛ فَعُلِمَ أَنَّ الرَّبَّ سُبْحَانَهُ لَمْ يَزَلْ عَالِيًا عَلَى عَرْشِهِ. فَلَوْ كَانَ فِي نِصْفِ الزَّمَانِ أَوْ كُلِّهِ تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ أَوْ تَحْتَ بَعْضِ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ؛ لَكَانَ هَذَا مُنَاقِضًا لِذَلِكَ. وَأَيْضًا فَقَدْ ثَبَتَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ الصَّحِيحِ الَّذِي رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ وَغَيْرُهُ 
{عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الْأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَك شَيْءٌ؛ وَأَنْتَ الْآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَك شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَك شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَك شَيْءٌ}

" الْأَسْمَاءِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ "
 الَّذِي فِيهِ ذِكْرُ الْإِدْلَاءِ قَدْ ذَكَرْنَاهُ فِي 
" مَسْأَلَةِ الْإِحَاطَةِ "
 وَهُوَ مِمَّا يُبَيِّنُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَزَالُ عَالِيًا عَلَى الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ مَعَ ظُهُورِهِ وَبُطُونِهِ وَفِي حَالِ نُزُولِهِ إلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا.
translated_text:
And this states that He, glorified be He, was above the Throne at that time, as the Quran indicates, just as He has stated that He rose over the Throne and that He is with us wherever we are. His being with us is a particular circumstance; the same applies to His being established over the Throne. Likewise, the other texts describe Him as being high above His Throne at this time. Thus, it is known that the Lord, glorified be He, has always been high above His Throne. If He were beneath the Throne or beneath some created beings for half the time, or all of it, this would contradict that.

Furthermore, it is established in the authentic hadith narrated by Muslim and others that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say:

“O Allah, You are the First, and there is nothing before You. You are the Last, and there is nothing after You. You are the Outward, and there is nothing above You. You are the Inward, and there is nothing beyond You.”

This explicitly states that nothing is above Allah. His being the Outward is an inseparable attribute of His, just as He is the First and the Last; the same applies to His being the Inward. Thus, He always remains the Outward, with nothing above Him, and He always remains the Inward, with nothing beyond Him.

Furthermore, we have already discussed, in “The Question of Encompassing,” the report of Abū Dharr, Abū Hurayrah and Qatādah cited in explanation of these “four names,” which mentions lowering. It is among the reports demonstrating that Allah always remains high above created beings while being both the Outward and the Inward, and when He descends to the lowest heaven.

Furthermore, Allah Most High says:

“They have not esteemed Allah as He deserves. On the Day of Resurrection, the whole earth will be in His grasp, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand. Glorified and exalted is He above what they associate with Him!”

It is impossible for One whose greatness is such to be confined by anything He has created. Authentic hadiths explaining this verse have been reported from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; the scholars of hadith have unanimously affirmed their authenticity and received them with acceptance. End of quotation.
